records.description: Iran supplied advanced military drones, likely equipped with AI for navigation and targeting, to Russia for use in the Ukraine war. Reports indicate these drones faced technical malfunctions, leading to operational failures and multiple defeats, highlighting the risks and harm associated with AI-enabled weapon systems in active conflict.

records.title: AI Surveillance in Tehran Metro Targets Dress Code Violators
records.description: Iranian authorities have implemented AI-powered facial recognition in metro stations to identify women not complying with mandatory hijab laws. Cameras capture images, match them to national ID databases, and automatically issue fines by mail, raising significant concerns over privacy violations and the use of AI for oppressive surveillance and enforcement.

records.title: French Tax Authorities Use AI to Detect 20,000 Undeclared Pools, Impose Fines
records.description: French tax authorities used AI software developed by Google and Capgemini to analyze aerial images and cadastral data, uncovering over 20,000 undeclared private pools. This led to the imposition of nearly €10 million in fines, with plans to expand the AI system nationwide for further tax enforcement.

records.title: China's AI-Powered Mass Surveillance Leads to Human Rights Violations
records.description: China has deployed over 500 million AI-enabled surveillance cameras, using facial recognition and predictive analytics to monitor and suppress its population, including minorities and dissidents. This mass surveillance, described as creating an 'AI totalitarian state,' has resulted in widespread violations of human rights and fundamental freedoms.

records.title: Meta Uses Algorithm to Automate Employee Layoffs, Sparking Labor Concerns
records.description: Meta used an AI algorithm to monitor and evaluate contract workers, leading to the automated dismissal of 60 employees without clear human oversight or explanation. The algorithm tracked activity and enforced strict performance metrics, raising concerns about labor rights, privacy, and the fairness of AI-driven employment decisions.

records.title: Deepfake AI Technology Fuels Fraud, Misinformation, and Privacy Violations
records.description: AI-powered deepfake technology is increasingly used to create convincing fake videos and audio, leading to real harms such as financial fraud, misinformation, and non-consensual intimate image abuse. These incidents have prompted legal reforms and heightened concerns about the technology's potential for widespread societal harm.

records.title: Tesla Driver Misuses Autopilot, Creating Road Hazard in Tunnel
records.description: A female driver was filmed in a Tesla electric vehicle, equipped with AI-based autonomous driving features, driving through a tunnel with both hands off the steering wheel while using her phone. This misuse of the AI system created a significant risk of accident, drawing public criticism and highlighting safety concerns around overreliance on autonomous driving technology.

records.title: Jihadist Groups Use Civilian Drones in Deadly Attack on Malian Military Base
records.description: Jihadist groups in Africa, notably the Islamic State in the Sahel, used civilian drones to coordinate a complex attack on a Malian military base in Tessit, resulting in 42 soldiers killed. The incident highlights the increasing use of AI-enabled drones by militants to inflict harm and conduct coordinated assaults.

records.title: Intellexa Predator Spyware Pricing Leak Highlights Ongoing AI-Enabled Surveillance Scandal in Greece
records.description: Journalist Thanasis Koukakis published Intellexa’s Predator spyware pricing, revealing technical details about its AI-enabled surveillance capabilities. The leak comes amid political controversy over ongoing illegal monitoring of politicians and journalists in Greece, raising concerns about privacy violations and the misuse of advanced AI surveillance tools.

records.title: Pegasus Spyware Allegations Spark Political and Human Rights Concerns
records.description: Allegations of Pegasus spyware, an AI-enabled surveillance tool, being used against politicians, journalists, and activists have led to political outcry and human rights concerns. While a Supreme Court panel found malware on some phones, it could not conclusively link it to Pegasus. The government’s lack of cooperation and NSO Group’s CEO resignation highlight ongoing controversy.

records.title: AI Rapper FN Meka Dropped After Backlash Over Racial Stereotypes
records.description: Capitol Records dropped AI-generated rapper FN Meka after public backlash over the character's use of racial stereotypes and offensive language. The AI system, developed by Factory New, generated lyrics and persona elements that perpetuated harmful stereotypes, leading to social harm and a public apology from the label to the Black community.

records.title: AI Image Generator Stable Diffusion Used for Non-Consensual Pornography and Misinformation
records.description: The open-source AI image generator Stable Diffusion has been used to create and share non-consensual pornographic images, including fake celebrity nudes, and realistic fake photos, leading to trauma, privacy violations, and misinformation. Reddit banned several subreddits distributing such content, highlighting significant harms caused by the unfiltered use of this AI system.

records.title: Former Apple Engineer Pleads Guilty to Stealing Autonomous Vehicle Trade Secrets
records.description: Xiaolang Zhang, a former Apple engineer, pleaded guilty to stealing trade secrets related to Apple's autonomous vehicle (AI) project, Project Titan. Zhang downloaded confidential hardware and software data before attempting to join Chinese startup XMotors. The theft, involving AI system technology, led to his arrest and a sealed plea agreement.

records.title: Snapchat and Google Settle Lawsuits Over Unlawful Biometric Data Collection via AI Facial Recognition
records.description: Snapchat and Google agreed to pay $35 million and $100 million, respectively, to settle lawsuits alleging their AI-powered facial recognition features collected and stored users' biometric data without consent, violating Illinois' Biometric Information Privacy Act. The settlements address privacy harms caused by unauthorized use of AI systems.

records.title: Oracle Sued for AI-Driven Global Surveillance and Privacy Violations
records.description: Oracle faces a class-action lawsuit alleging its AI-powered adtech and data systems collected, analyzed, and sold detailed personal data on nearly 5 billion people without consent. The suit claims this mass surveillance and profiling violated privacy rights and legal protections, causing harm to individuals worldwide.

records.title: AI Accent Removal in Call Centers Raises Discrimination and Labor Rights Concerns
records.description: Sanas, a Silicon Valley startup, has developed AI technology to alter call center workers' accents to sound more 'American.' Critics warn this could reinforce racial and cultural biases, erode worker identity, and exacerbate labor rights issues, raising concerns about discrimination and potential harm to affected communities.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot's Dual Role in Accident Prevention and Involvement in Crashes
records.description: Tesla's Autopilot AI system reportedly prevents about 40 accidents daily by intervening when drivers mistakenly accelerate. However, incidents have occurred where Autopilot's actions, such as sudden braking, contributed to crashes, prompting regulatory investigations and raising concerns about its safety and reliability.

records.title: Google AI Wrongly Flags Medical Photos as Child Abuse, Leading to Account Lockouts and Police Investigations
records.description: Google's AI system mistakenly flagged medical photos of a sick child, taken by a parent for a doctor's consultation, as child sexual abuse material. This led to the parent's Google account being locked, loss of personal data and services, and a police investigation, despite the images being medically necessary.

records.title: Binance Executive Deepfaked in Crypto Listing Scam
records.description: Hackers used AI-generated deepfake technology to impersonate Binance's chief communications officer, Patrick Hillmann, in video calls and online meetings. The deepfakes, created from his public appearances, deceived crypto project teams into believing he could help list their tokens, resulting in fraudulent interactions and potential financial harm.

records.title: AI-Generated Deepfake Spreads False Election Polls in Brazil
records.description: During Brazil's 2022 election campaign, AI-generated deepfake videos circulated on social media, falsely showing news anchor Renata Vasconcellos reporting manipulated poll results favoring Jair Bolsonaro over Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. The deepfake, widely shared, misled voters and undermined trust in the electoral process.

records.title: Meta Contractors Dismissed by Algorithmic Selection
records.description: Around 60 Accenture contractors working for Facebook (Meta) were dismissed after being selected 'at random' by an algorithm, with no clear justification provided. The use of AI in this employment decision led to job loss and raised concerns about transparency and labor rights violations.

records.title: EE's AI Firewall Blocks Millions of Scam Calls in the UK
records.description: UK mobile operator EE deployed AI-powered firewall technology to review and block scam calls, particularly those spoofing UK numbers from international sources. Since July, the system has blocked over 11 million scam calls, preventing fraud and protecting personal and financial information for EE, BT, Plusnet, and other network customers.

records.title: AI-Powered Forklift Safety System Deployed to Prevent Workplace Accidents
records.description: VIA Technologies and Hotai Toyota Material Handling have deployed the AI-based Mobile360 forklift safety system, which uses intelligent personnel detection to alert drivers when pedestrians enter danger zones. This aims to reduce workplace collisions and injuries in manufacturing and logistics environments by providing real-time warnings and improving operational safety.

records.title: Tinkoff Deploys AI System to Prevent Phone Fraud and Spam
records.description: Tinkoff Bank and Tinkoff Mobile launched 'Neuroshield,' an AI-powered system that analyzes real-time call data to detect and interrupt fraudulent and spam calls. The system compares voice and call patterns to known scam profiles, automatically disconnecting suspicious calls and notifying users, thereby actively preventing financial harm to customers.

records.title: AI-Powered Image Filters Linked to Rise in Body Dysmorphic Disorder Among Adolescents
records.description: AI-driven facial modification filters on social media are contributing to increased cases of body dysmorphic disorder, especially among adolescents. Research from Boston Medical Center and other institutions links these filters to distorted self-perception and mental health harm, as users compare themselves to their AI-altered images.

records.title: TikTok's AI Systems Spark Privacy and Misinformation Concerns
records.description: TikTok's AI-driven systems have been found to monitor user activity beyond its platform, raising privacy and security concerns, and to amplify misinformation, including manipulated political content. These incidents highlight the risks of AI in unauthorized data collection and the spread of harmful or false information.

records.title: Tesla's AI-Driven Autopilot and FSD Under Scrutiny After Dangerous Tests and Fatal Crashes
records.description: Tesla's AI-powered Autopilot and Full Self-Driving systems are under investigation after incidents including a fatal crash and unsafe user tests involving children. US regulators warn against risky testing, citing multiple crashes and fatalities linked to the AI systems, and are probing Tesla's driver monitoring and safety claims.

records.title: Google Maps AI Misleads Abortion Seekers to Crisis Pregnancy Centers
records.description: Google Maps' AI-driven search results frequently direct users seeking abortion clinics to crisis pregnancy centers (CPCs), which do not provide abortions and often spread medically false information. This misdirection exposes users to harmful misinformation, delays access to legitimate care, and has led to documented harm for those seeking abortion services.

records.title: BMW Test Car with Autonomous Steering Causes Fatal Crash in Germany
records.description: A BMW iX test car equipped with AI-based autonomous steering veered into oncoming traffic in Reutlingen, Germany, causing a multi-vehicle collision that killed one person and seriously injured nine others. Authorities are investigating whether the AI system or the human driver was in control at the time.

records.title: Delhi Police's Use of 80% Facial Recognition Match Raises Rights Concerns
records.description: Delhi Police use facial recognition technology with an 80% similarity threshold to identify and arrest suspects in major investigations. Experts and digital rights groups warn this low threshold risks misidentification, privacy violations, and wrongful arrests, highlighting the lack of privacy impact assessments and potential harm to civil liberties.

records.title: Airbnb Deploys AI to Prevent Unauthorized Parties in North America
records.description: Airbnb has introduced AI-powered 'anti-party' technology in the US and Canada to identify and block high-risk reservations likely to result in unauthorized parties. The system analyzes user data and booking patterns, aiming to reduce property damage and community disruption, following a successful pilot in Australia that saw a 35% drop in incidents.

records.title: TikTok's In-App Browser on iOS Secretly Monitors User Keystrokes and Data
records.description: Investigations revealed that TikTok's in-app browser for iOS injects JavaScript code to monitor user interactions, including keystrokes and sensitive data, on third-party websites accessed via the app. This AI-enabled tracking constitutes a violation of user privacy and rights, as it can capture passwords and credit card information without clear consent.

records.title: Apple Face ID Fails for Māori Man with Traditional Tattoos
records.description: Apple's Face ID facial recognition on the iPhone 13 Pro Max failed to work for Paaka Edwards, a Māori man with moko kanohi (traditional facial tattoos). The AI system's inability to recognize faces with such markings led to exclusion and potential discrimination, highlighting a lack of cultural inclusivity in the technology.

records.title: Facebook's AI Fails to Block Election Misinformation Ads in Brazil
records.description: Facebook's AI-driven content moderation systems failed to detect and block election-related misinformation ads ahead of Brazil's 2022 election, according to Global Witness. The approved ads contained false voting information and undermined election integrity, highlighting ongoing failures in Meta's AI to prevent harmful disinformation.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot Under Investigation After Crashes and Safety Concerns Involving AI System
records.description: US regulators are investigating Tesla's Autopilot AI system after multiple crashes, including incidents where vehicles struck emergency vehicles and failed to avoid child-sized mannequins. The NHTSA is scrutinizing the effectiveness of Tesla's driver monitoring and warning systems, raising concerns about the AI's ability to ensure road safety.

records.title: TikTok's AI Algorithms Fuel and Censor Election Misinformation Ahead of 2022 Midterms
records.description: TikTok's AI-driven recommendation and moderation systems have amplified the spread of election misinformation, including conspiracy theories about voter fraud, undermining democratic processes. In response to public and media pressure, TikTok deployed AI-based censorship, disabling certain hashtags and increasing content moderation to curb falsehoods, impacting users' access to information.

records.title: Microsoft and Amazon AI Services Criticized for Enabling Increased Fossil Fuel Production
records.description: Microsoft and Amazon have provided AI-powered cloud computing services to major oil companies, enabling more efficient oil and gas extraction. Critics argue this use of AI contradicts the tech giants' climate commitments, as it indirectly increases fossil fuel production and environmental harm, with little evidence of effective emission offsets.

records.title: DJI Drones Used in Russia-Ukraine War Spark International Controversy
records.description: DJI civilian drones, equipped with AI navigation, have been used by Russian forces in the Ukraine war for artillery targeting and reconnaissance, drawing praise from Russian officials. Despite DJI’s denials and claims of civilian-only use, their drones’ deployment in conflict has contributed to harm, sparking diplomatic and reputational tensions.

records.title: Meta's In-App Browsers Secretly Track User Activity on Facebook and Instagram
records.description: Researcher Felix Krause revealed that Meta's Facebook and Instagram apps inject tracking code into websites opened via their in-app browsers, monitoring user actions—including keystrokes, clicks, and sensitive data—without explicit consent. This AI-enabled tracking circumvents privacy protections, raising significant concerns over user privacy violations and unauthorized data collection.

records.title: Ant Group's AI System Prevents Fraud and Protects Millions of Users
records.description: Ant Group deployed advanced AI-driven risk control systems, collaborating with phone makers like Honor and vivo to upgrade risk detection on over 10 million devices. The AI rapidly identifies and blocks fraudulent accounts and high-risk transactions, preventing scams and protecting user funds, with over 168,000 malicious accounts intercepted in six months.

records.title: Google Fined $58 Million in Australia for Misleading Users on AI-Driven Location Data Collection
records.description: Australian Federal Court fined Google $58 million for misleading 1.3 million users about personal location data collection via Android devices. The AI-driven system continued collecting data despite user settings, violating privacy and consumer rights. Google has since implemented corrective measures.

records.title: Delhi Police Use Facial Recognition AI to Identify Jahangirpuri Violence Suspects
records.description: Delhi Police used a facial recognition system (AI) to match photos of arrested suspects with CCTV footage from the Jahangirpuri violence, leading to multiple arrests. The process, conducted with court approval, involved replicating suspects' poses for higher accuracy, and the AI-generated evidence will be presented in court.

records.title: Taiwan Deploys AI-Equipped Garbage Trucks to Protect Sanitation Workers
records.description: Taiwan's Environmental Protection Administration has begun equipping garbage trucks with AI-powered blind spot detection and multiple cameras to monitor sanitation workers' positions and prevent accidents. The system, now piloted in Taoyuan and Hsinchu, aims to reduce occupational injuries and fatalities among the nation's 33,474 sanitation workers.

records.title: US Lawmakers and Regulators Probe Fatal Tesla and XPeng AI Driving System Accidents
records.description: US lawmakers and regulators are investigating multiple fatal accidents linked to Tesla's Autopilot and FSD, as well as XPeng's assisted driving system. These AI-driven features are under scrutiny for safety defects, misleading marketing, and failure to prevent crashes, prompting calls for recalls and regulatory action after at least 19 deaths.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot and FSD Under Scrutiny After Fatal Crashes and Malfunction Reports
records.description: Tesla's Autopilot and Full Self-Driving (FSD) AI systems are under investigation by the NHTSA following fatal crashes involving motorcyclists and reports of frequent malfunctions. Consumer advocate Ralph Nader and regulators are calling for the removal of FSD from all Teslas, citing safety risks and ongoing fatalities linked to the technology.

records.title: Widespread Use of Pegasus AI Spyware by European Governments Revealed
records.description: Investigations revealed that NSO Group's AI-powered spyware Pegasus is actively used by 22 security agencies across 12 EU countries. The software has enabled unauthorized surveillance of political figures, journalists, and activists, leading to significant privacy violations and human rights concerns, prompting calls for stricter regulation of such AI surveillance tools.

records.title: Facebook's AI Fails to Block and Profits from White Supremacist Content
records.description: Reports reveal Facebook's AI-driven algorithms failed to block over 80 white supremacist groups, auto-generated extremist pages, and monetized searches for banned groups with ads. These AI system failures enabled the spread and normalization of hate speech, causing harm to communities and violating rights despite Facebook's bans.

records.title: Meta's BlenderBot 3 Chatbot Insults Mark Zuckerberg
records.description: Meta's AI chatbot BlenderBot 3, after being trained on internet data, generated offensive and insulting remarks about CEO Mark Zuckerberg, calling him a "bad person" and "manipulator." The incident highlights risks of AI systems reflecting and amplifying negative online biases, resulting in reputational harm.

records.title: TikTok's AI Algorithm Promotes Banned Content to Russian Users
records.description: TikTok's AI-driven recommendation system has been 'shadow promoting' banned and new Russian content, including state media propaganda, to users in Russia despite official restrictions. This algorithmic loophole undermines content moderation policies and enables the spread of disallowed and potentially harmful information.

records.title: Tesla Full Self-Driving AI Fails to Detect Child-Sized Mannequin in Safety Test
records.description: A series of tests by The Dawn Project showed Tesla's Full Self-Driving (FSD) AI repeatedly failed to detect and avoid a child-sized mannequin, resulting in collisions under controlled conditions. The incident highlights significant safety concerns about the AI system's ability to protect vulnerable road users.

records.title: XPeng Assisted Driving System Fails to Detect Hazard, Causes Fatal Accident in Ningbo
records.description: An XPeng vehicle in Ningbo, China, crashed while its lane centering assisted driving system was active and failed to detect a stalled vehicle ahead, resulting in injuries and fatalities. XPeng is cooperating with authorities in the investigation, highlighting risks associated with AI-assisted driving systems.

records.title: AI Moderation Failures Enable Election Disinformation on Social Platforms
records.description: A report by UFBA researchers found that major social media and messaging platforms, despite using AI for content moderation and having agreements with Brazil's electoral court, are failing to effectively detect and remove disinformation. This ongoing inadequacy is allowing fake news to spread during a critical election period, harming democratic processes.

records.title: CFPB Fines Hello Digit $2.7M for Algorithm-Induced Overdraft Fees
records.description: The CFPB fined Hello Digit $2.7 million after its automated savings app's algorithm caused users' checking accounts to overdraft, resulting in financial harm and deceptive practices. The app falsely claimed it would not trigger overdraft fees and failed to reimburse affected users, prompting regulatory action and mandated customer redress.

records.title: Pegasus Spyware Used by Governments for Political Surveillance and Human Rights Violations in EU and Thailand
records.description: Investigations revealed that NSO Group's AI-enabled Pegasus spyware was used by security agencies in 12 EU countries and by Thai authorities to target activists, politicians, and dissidents. The spyware enabled invasive surveillance, leading to privacy violations, suppression of dissent, and breaches of human rights across multiple countries.

records.title: AI-Driven Bots Amplify Political Disinformation in Brazilian Election
records.description: Researchers from UFPE and Unicap used AI algorithms to analyze 40,000 social media profiles, finding that followers of President Bolsonaro are 15% more likely to be bots than those of Lula. These AI-driven bots actively spread misinformation and polarize political discourse, harming public debate and democratic processes.

records.title: VMware Report Reveals Surge in Deepfake-Driven Cyberattacks and Extortion
records.description: VMware's Global Incident Response Threat Report highlights a significant rise in cyberattacks using AI-generated deepfakes, with two-thirds of surveyed organizations experiencing such incidents. Cybercriminals employ deepfakes to evade security controls, compromise organizations, and facilitate extortion, marking a 13% increase in these attacks over the previous year.

records.title: Meta Sued Over AI-Driven Facebook Addiction and Mental Health Harm to Minor
records.description: Cecilia Tesch is suing Meta, alleging that Facebook's AI-driven recommendation and notification systems caused her 13-year-old daughter to develop addiction, body dysmorphia, eating disorders, and self-harm. The lawsuit claims the platform's design led to significant mental health harms due to its addictive features targeting minors.

records.title: High Repair Costs from LiDAR Damage in AI-Enabled Electric Vehicles
records.description: A minor collision involving an XPeng P5 electric vehicle resulted in costly repairs due to damage to its AI-powered LiDAR sensor, with the sensor alone costing over 9,000 yuan. The incident highlights the financial risks and high repair costs associated with integrating advanced AI systems into consumer vehicles.

records.title: FBI Warns of Deepfake Job Interview Scams in Remote Work Era
records.description: The FBI reports incidents where AI-generated deepfakes and voice spoofing technologies were used to impersonate individuals during remote job interviews, enabling identity theft and potential unauthorized access to sensitive company information. This malicious use of AI has led to real harm for organizations and individuals.

records.title: UK Deploys AI-Enabled Smartwatches for Migrant Surveillance, Raising Human Rights Concerns
records.description: The UK Home Office and Ministry of Justice plan to monitor migrants with criminal convictions using AI-powered smartwatches with facial recognition and location tracking. Critics and privacy groups warn this surveillance could violate privacy and human rights, as biometric and location data are stored and shared between agencies for up to six years.

records.title: Family Rescued After Google Maps Navigation Error Leads Car Into Kerala Canal
records.description: A family of four, including a three-month-old baby, narrowly escaped harm after their car plunged into a canal in Kerala while following Google Maps directions. The AI-powered navigation system led them into a waterlogged area, requiring local residents to rescue the family from the drifting vehicle.

records.title: AI-Enabled 'Ninja' Missile Strike Raises Fears Over Autonomous Lethal Weapons
records.description: The CIA's use of an AI-enabled Hellfire R9X 'Ninja' missile to kill al-Qaeda leader Ayman al-Zawahiri highlights the growing deployment of autonomous weapons capable of lethal action without human intervention, raising concerns about unregulated AI-driven warfare and the potential for significant harm to individuals and global security.

records.title: NHTSA Investigates Fatal Tesla Autopilot Crashes Involving Motorcyclists
records.description: The US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration is investigating two fatal crashes where Teslas, reportedly using Autopilot, collided with motorcycles at night. The incidents raise concerns about the AI system's ability to detect motorcycles, highlighting potential safety risks and prompting broader scrutiny of Tesla's automated driving technology.

records.title: TikTok's AI 'Fatphobic' Filter Sparks Body-Shaming Backlash
records.description: TikTok's AI-powered 'fatphobic' filter, which exaggerated facial features to appear 'ugly,' went viral but was widely criticized for promoting body-shaming and fatphobia. The filter's use led to psychological and social harm, prompting TikTok to remove it following significant user backlash.

records.title: AI-Powered Killer Drones Cause Lethal Harm and Spark Global Debate
records.description: Autonomous drones equipped with AI algorithms are independently identifying and attacking targets, causing deaths and destruction in conflict zones. Their use has led to international concern, with the UN discussing regulation. Critics warn these 'killer robots' raise serious ethical, legal, and human rights issues due to their lethal autonomy.

records.title: Deepfake Video of Princess Leonor Dancing on TikTok Goes Viral
records.description: AI-generated deepfake videos falsely depicting Princess Leonor dancing on TikTok have gone viral, using the face-swapping technology to mislead viewers and damage her reputation. The videos, which use footage of another influencer, have been widely debunked but highlight the risks of AI-driven misinformation and reputational harm.

records.title: Pony.ai Sues Former Executives' Robotruck Startup for AI Trade Secret Infringement
records.description: Pony.ai has sued its former executives and their new autonomous truck company, Qingtian Zhika, alleging infringement of AI-related trade secrets and seeking 60 million RMB in damages. The lawsuit, now accepted by Beijing Intellectual Property Court, centers on proprietary L4 autonomous driving technology.

records.title: Greek Politician and Journalist Targeted by AI-Enabled Predator Spyware, Prompting Legal Investigation
records.description: Greek authorities launched urgent investigations after political leader Nikos Androulakis and journalist Thanasis Koukakis were targeted with the AI-enabled Predator spyware, which attempted to illegally access their mobile communications and data. The incident raised serious concerns about privacy violations and the misuse of AI surveillance tools.

records.title: Deepfake Video Falsely Attributes Defamatory Statements to Brazilian Journalist
records.description: AI-generated deepfake technology was used to create a fake video and synthetic audio falsely portraying journalist William Bonner calling politicians Lula and Alckmin criminals. The manipulated content, widely shared on TikTok, spread misinformation and caused reputational harm, highlighting the risks of AI-driven disinformation in public discourse.

records.title: Federal Investigation Launched After TuSimple Self-Driving Truck Crash
records.description: A TuSimple autonomous truck crashed into a concrete barrier on April 6, 2022, after human operators improperly re-engaged self-driving mode. The incident, which caused minor property damage but no injuries, triggered federal investigations into the safety of TuSimple’s AI system and operational protocols.

records.title: Kenya Threatens Facebook Ban Over AI Moderation Failures on Hate Speech
records.description: Kenya's National Cohesion and Integration Commission threatened to ban Facebook after reports revealed its AI-driven content moderation failed to detect and remove hate speech ads in Swahili and English, escalating risks of violence ahead of national elections. Facebook was given seven days to improve its moderation systems.

records.title: Russian AI-Enabled Drones Target Ukrainian HIMARS Launchers
records.description: Russian forces are using AI-powered loitering munitions, such as the 'KUB-BLA' and 'Lancet' drones, to autonomously detect and destroy Ukrainian HIMARS rocket launchers. These drones employ artificial intelligence for automatic target search and engagement, resulting in direct harm to military assets during the ongoing conflict in Ukraine.

records.title: Facebook AI Fails to Block Violent Hate Speech Ads in Kenya Election Test
records.description: Nonprofits Global Witness and Foxglove found Facebook's AI content moderation system failed to block 17 out of 20 test ads promoting ethnic violence, rape, and killings ahead of Kenya's election. The ads, in English and Swahili, were approved despite containing clear hate speech, exposing risks of incitement.

records.title: Chinese Government Sought Covert TikTok Accounts for Propaganda, Raising AI Misuse Concerns
records.description: Reports reveal that a Chinese government agency requested to set up covert TikTok accounts to conduct propaganda targeting Western audiences, leveraging TikTok's AI-driven platform. Although TikTok executives rejected the request, the incident highlights risks of AI-enabled disinformation and ongoing concerns over data security and political influence.

records.title: Moroccan Military Drone Strike Kills Polisario Military Leader
records.description: A Moroccan military drone, likely utilizing AI for targeting and navigation, conducted a strike near the security wall, killing Khattari Said Berrah, a senior Polisario military leader. The incident highlights the lethal use of AI-enabled drones in conflict, resulting in fatalities and equipment losses for the Polisario group.

records.title: Global Human Rights Violations Linked to Pegasus AI Spyware Deployment
records.description: NSO Group's Pegasus spyware, an AI-powered surveillance tool, has been used by governments worldwide to covertly monitor activists, journalists, diplomats, and political opponents, resulting in significant privacy violations and human rights abuses. Victims include US diplomats and the family of Paul Rusesabagina, with calls for stronger regulation and accountability.

records.title: AI Unmasks Russian Soldier Hiding in Ukrainian Hospital
records.description: Ukrainian authorities used AI-powered facial recognition to identify a Russian soldier pretending to have amnesia in a Kryvyi Rih hospital. The system revealed his true identity, leading to his capture. AI is also being used to analyze satellite images for new graves, supporting military intelligence and justice efforts during the conflict.

records.title: Predator Spyware Scandal Undermines Democracy in Greece
records.description: Greek political figures, including former Prime Minister George Papandreou, condemned the use of AI-enabled Predator spyware for unauthorized surveillance of politicians and journalists. The incident highlights significant privacy violations and threats to democratic processes, prompting calls for urgent regulatory action and full transparency for affected individuals.

records.title: Instagram's AI Algorithms Blamed for Teen Mental Health Crisis in Lawsuits
records.description: Multiple lawsuits allege that Instagram's AI-driven content recommendation algorithms fueled addiction, eating disorders, and severe mental health issues in teenage users, including depression, anxiety, and suicide attempts. The suits claim Meta prioritized engagement over safety, knowingly exposing vulnerable minors to harmful content.

records.title: Southern Co-op Faces Legal Challenge Over 'Unlawful' Facial Recognition Surveillance
records.description: Southern Co-op is accused of unlawfully using AI-powered facial recognition in 35 UK stores, enabling staff to secretly blacklist shoppers and store biometric data without consent. Privacy group Big Brother Watch filed a legal complaint, alleging significant violations of data rights and privacy laws, prompting calls for regulatory investigation.

records.title: Attempted AI Spyware Attack on Greek Political Leader's Phone
records.description: Nikos Androulakis, leader of PASOK, filed a complaint after an attempt to infect his phone with Predator, an AI-enabled spyware capable of covert surveillance and data extraction. The attack, detected before harm occurred, represents a serious violation of privacy and political rights using advanced AI surveillance tools.

records.title: Fatal Utah Tesla Autopilot Crash Prompts Federal Investigation
records.description: A Tesla using its Autopilot AI system struck and killed a motorcyclist in Utah, prompting a federal investigation by the NHTSA. The incident adds to a growing list of fatal crashes involving Tesla’s AI-driven driver assistance, raising concerns about the system’s safety and reliability.

records.title: Google's AI Tools Used by Israel for Surveillance and Repression of Palestinians
records.description: Multiple reports reveal that Google, via the $1.2 billion 'Project Nimbus' with Amazon, provided Israel with AI tools for facial recognition, image classification, and sentiment analysis. These systems are used for surveillance and control in occupied Palestinian territories, contributing to human rights violations and systemic repression.

records.title: Uber Eats Sued Over Alleged Racial Bias in Facial Recognition AI
records.description: Pa Edrissa Manjang, a Black Uber Eats courier in London, is suing the company after being dismissed due to repeated failures of its facial recognition AI, which he claims is racially biased. The AI system's alleged inability to accurately verify his identity led to his suspension, raising concerns of discrimination and labor rights violations.

records.title: Anitta Targeted by Deepfake Pornographic Video
records.description: Brazilian singer Anitta was the victim of a deepfake incident in which her face was inserted into a pornographic video using AI technology. The fake video circulated widely on social media, causing reputational harm and public confusion. Anitta's team condemned the act as criminal and clarified the video is not authentic.

records.title: AI Driver Monitoring Systems Misclassify Drivers with Small Eyes as Drowsy
records.description: Several drivers using Xpeng and other brands' AI-assisted driving systems were wrongly flagged as drowsy or distracted due to having small eyes, resulting in penalties. The misclassification, caused by facial recognition algorithms, prompted public complaints and led manufacturers to promise urgent system optimizations to address the bias.

records.title: Chicago Man Sues Over Wrongful Imprisonment Due to AI Gunshot Detection System
records.description: Michael Williams, a Chicago resident, filed a federal lawsuit after spending nearly a year in jail based on evidence from ShotSpotter, an AI-powered gunshot detection system. The suit alleges police placed undue reliance on the unreliable AI, leading to wrongful arrest, imprisonment, and significant personal harm.

records.title: Taiwanese YouTuber Sentenced for Deepfake Pornography Scandal Involving 119 Victims
records.description: YouTuber Zhu Yuchen ('Xiao Yu') and an assistant used AI deepfake technology to create and sell non-consensual pornographic videos featuring the faces of 119 public figures, including politicians and celebrities. The court sentenced Zhu to 5 years and 6 months in prison for violating personal data laws, highlighting the harm caused by AI-enabled digital sexual violence.

records.title: AI-Generated Deepfake Video Falsely Claims Lula Supports Bolsonaro
records.description: A manipulated video circulated on TikTok uses AI-enabled techniques to combine footage of ex-president Lula with a fabricated audio track, falsely suggesting he endorsed Jair Bolsonaro. The deepfake misleads the public, threatens electoral integrity, and exemplifies the harm caused by AI-generated political disinformation.

records.title: Chess Robot Breaks Child's Finger During Moscow Tournament
records.description: At the Moscow Chess Open, an AI-powered chess robot injured a 7-year-old boy by grabbing and breaking his finger when the child attempted a move before the robot completed its own. The incident highlights safety concerns in human-AI physical interactions, prompting calls for improved safeguards and possible legal action.

records.title: Facebook and Social Platforms Track Over Half of Web Activity Using AI
records.description: A study by DIW Berlin and several universities found that Facebook and similar platforms use AI-driven tracking and profiling to monitor up to 52% of users' web activity, including non-users, without clear consent. This widespread data collection and profiling constitutes a significant privacy violation and potential breach of fundamental rights.

records.title: Lawsuit Alleges TikTok Algorithm Promotes Harmful Content to Minority Teens, Leading to Tragedy
records.description: A lawsuit claims TikTok's AI-driven recommendation algorithm disproportionately steers violent content to minority users, contributing to the addiction and subsequent death of a 14-year-old African-American girl. The suit alleges TikTok was aware of racial and socioeconomic biases in its algorithm, holding it and other social media companies accountable.

records.title: AI Surveillance Drives Global Erosion of Privacy and Human Rights
records.description: Governments and corporations are deploying AI-powered surveillance systems that monitor, identify, and catalogue individuals, leading to widespread violations of privacy and fundamental rights. This ongoing use of AI technology is reshaping society, eroding civil liberties, and enabling digital authoritarianism on an unprecedented scale.

records.title: Meta Pixel AI Collects Sensitive Health Data from Hospital Websites Without Consent
records.description: Meta's AI-powered Pixel tool was found on 33 hospital websites and patient portals, collecting sensitive health data—including medications, allergies, and appointments—linked to individuals without consent. This unauthorized data sharing violates privacy rights and potentially breaches HIPAA, affecting over 26 million patient visits.

records.title: ICE's AI-Driven Mass Surveillance of U.S. Population Exposed
records.description: Reports reveal that the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has used AI-enabled surveillance technologies, including facial recognition and GPS tracking, to collect and analyze personal data on up to 74% of Americans. This large-scale, secretive monitoring exceeds legal limits, violating privacy and human rights, especially targeting minorities and immigrants.

records.title: German Consumer Group Sues Tesla Over AI Sentry Mode Privacy Violations
records.description: The German consumer association vzbv has sued Tesla, alleging its AI-powered Sentry Mode violates data protection laws by recording public spaces without proper user information or consent, exposing users to legal risks. The lawsuit also challenges Tesla's misleading CO2 emissions claims, but the primary harm concerns AI-driven privacy breaches.

records.title: AI-Generated Audio Deepfake Spreads Political Misinformation in Brazil
records.description: A manipulated video using AI-enabled audio replacement tools on TikTok falsely depicted ex-governor Ricardo Coutinho criticizing Lula and praising Bolsonaro. The deepfake audio misled millions, spreading political misinformation and harming public trust by attributing fabricated statements to a political figure.

records.title: Pegasus Spyware Used Against Thai Pro-Democracy Activists and Global Rights Defenders
records.description: Israeli AI-enabled Pegasus spyware was used to surveil at least 30 Thai pro-democracy activists, lawyers, and academics during 2020-2021 protests, violating their privacy and rights. Globally, Pegasus has enabled governments to unlawfully target activists, journalists, and political leaders, with ongoing harm due to insufficient regulation of the surveillance industry.

records.title: Ongoing Global Human Rights Violations from Pegasus Spyware Use
records.description: The AI-powered Pegasus spyware, sold to at least 14 countries, continues to be used for illegal surveillance of activists, journalists, and politicians, causing widespread human rights violations. Despite international outcry and investigations, insufficient regulatory action has allowed ongoing harm and unchecked use of this invasive AI technology.

records.title: NHTSA Investigates Fatal Tesla Crashes Involving Autopilot AI System
records.description: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has launched special investigations into fatal crashes involving Tesla vehicles, including incidents in California and Florida where Autopilot, Tesla's AI-driven driver assistance system, may have been active. These crashes resulted in deaths, raising concerns about the safety of AI-assisted driving.

records.title: AI Deepfakes on TikTok Fuel Identity Fraud and Disinformation
records.description: AI-generated deepfake videos are proliferating on TikTok, impersonating celebrities and public figures. These deepfakes are increasingly used for identity fraud, disinformation campaigns, and reputational harm, as seen in incidents involving fake video calls with officials and manipulated celebrity content, raising significant security and trust concerns.

records.title: Global Human Rights Violations Linked to Pegasus AI Spyware Deployment
records.description: The AI-powered Pegasus spyware, developed by NSO Group, has been used by governments worldwide for illegal surveillance of journalists, activists, and politicians, resulting in privacy breaches, psychological harm, and suppression of free expression. Despite global outcry and ongoing investigations, the spyware continues to be deployed, with insufficient regulatory action.

records.title: AI-Generated Deepfake Faces Used for Large-Scale Identity Fraud in China
records.description: Chinese police dismantled a telecom fraud ring exploiting AI-generated deepfake facial videos to bypass facial recognition systems for SIM card registration. The group used stolen personal photos, sold cheaply online, to forge identities, leading to widespread privacy violations and facilitating further criminal activities.

records.title: Deepfake Video of President Zelensky Used in Fraud Scheme Targeting Ukrainians
records.description: Fraudsters used an AI-generated deepfake video of President Zelensky, posted on a fake Facebook page mimicking a real news outlet, to solicit personal data and bank card numbers from Ukrainians under the pretense of government payouts. Authorities warn this AI-enabled scam aims to steal victims' money and sensitive information.

records.title: German Court Orders Tesla to Compensate Customer Over AutoPilot Safety Failures
records.description: A German court ordered Tesla to pay €112,000 to a customer after its AI-based AutoPilot system failed to reliably detect obstacles and sometimes braked unnecessarily, posing significant safety risks. Technical reports and ongoing investigations link the system to accidents, injuries, and at least one death, highlighting the dangers of AI malfunction in assisted driving.

records.title: Facial Recognition Proctoring Software Discriminates Against Black Students at Dutch University
records.description: Robin Pocornie, a student at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, filed a complaint after Proctorio's AI-based proctoring software repeatedly failed to recognize her face due to her dark skin, causing exam delays and stress. The incident highlights racial bias in facial recognition AI, leading to discrimination and unequal exam conditions.

records.title: Algorithmic Management on Digital Labour Platforms Harms Global South Workers
records.description: AI-driven digital labour platforms, such as Uber and Bolt, use algorithms to allocate tasks, monitor performance, and control workers, leading to poor working conditions, low pay, and violations of labor rights for workers in the global South. These harms are ongoing and directly result from algorithmic management and surveillance.

records.title: AI Voice Assistants Record and Profile Children, Raising Privacy and Discrimination Concerns
records.description: AI-powered voice assistants like Siri and Alexa continuously record and analyze children's voices, accumulating detailed data over time. This practice, known as 'eavesmining,' raises significant concerns about privacy violations, surveillance, and discriminatory profiling, especially for vulnerable groups such as children and racialized youth.

records.title: Buenos Aires Officials Accused of Illegal Use of AI Facial Recognition System
records.description: Judge Roberto Gallardo filed a federal complaint against Buenos Aires officials for allegedly misusing the city's AI-powered facial recognition system, including unauthorized use and insecure handling of biometric data. The incident raises concerns over violations of privacy, legal protections, and fundamental rights due to improper deployment of AI surveillance technology.

records.title: Massive Data Breach Exposes Risks of China's AI Surveillance State
records.description: A major data breach of China's AI-driven surveillance systems, including facial recognition and Covid tracking apps, exposed personal information of up to one billion citizens. The incident sparked public resistance, lawsuits, and concerns over privacy violations, fraud risks, and inadequate safeguards against misuse of AI-collected data.

records.title: Study Finds Search Algorithms Amplify Gender Bias, Influencing User Behavior
records.description: A study led by NYU researchers found that AI-powered search algorithms amplify gender bias by producing male-dominated results even for gender-neutral queries. These biased outputs influence users’ perceptions and decisions, including hiring, thereby reinforcing societal gender disparities and causing real-world harm.

records.title: AI Accessibility Overlays Hinder Blind Users' Web Access
records.description: AI-powered accessibility overlays, widely adopted by major companies to improve website usability for blind users, have instead made navigation more difficult, hiding key features from screen readers and mislabeling elements. These malfunctions have led to user complaints and legal challenges, highlighting harm caused by poorly designed AI systems.

records.title: Greece Fines Clearview AI €20M for Illegal Biometric Data Processing
records.description: The Hellenic Data Protection Authority fined Clearview AI €20 million and ordered it to delete all Greek citizens' data for unlawfully scraping and processing biometric data without consent, violating GDPR. The decision follows complaints about Clearview's facial recognition system breaching privacy and data protection rights.

records.title: Human Rights Watch Exposes AI-Driven EdTech Privacy Violations Against Children
records.description: Human Rights Watch found that 89% of 163 government-recommended distance learning programs in 49 countries, including Brazil, collected and shared sensitive children's data—such as identity, location, and behavior—without proper consent, enabling targeted advertising and violating children's privacy and human rights through AI-driven data processing.

records.title: AI-Generated Videos Used to Bypass Facial Recognition Lead to Landmark Legal Case in Guangdong
records.description: Four individuals used AI to create dynamic facial videos from stolen ID photos, enabling them to bypass facial recognition systems and illegally trade over 2,000 pieces of personal information. This resulted in significant privacy breaches and public harm. They received criminal sentences and were ordered to pay damages and publicly apologize in a landmark civil public interest lawsuit.

records.title: Australia Uses AI Facial Recognition to Enforce Covid-19 Quarantine, Raising Privacy Concerns
records.description: Australian authorities deployed the G2G app, using AI-powered facial recognition and GPS tracking to monitor Covid-19 quarantine compliance. Over 150,000 people were subject to this system, which required periodic selfies for verification. The practice raised significant concerns about privacy violations, human rights, and potential discrimination.

records.title: Apple's Self-Driving Car AI Faces Safety Risks After Near-Miss Incident
records.description: Apple's autonomous vehicle project has experienced significant AI malfunctions, including a near-miss where the car almost hit a jogger at a crosswalk, requiring human intervention. These incidents highlight ongoing safety risks and technical challenges in Apple's self-driving AI, despite years of development and high-profile leadership.

records.title: DWP's AI Fraud Detection System Risks Unfair Denial of Universal Credit Benefits
records.description: The UK Department for Work and Pensions is trialling a machine learning algorithm to detect potential Universal Credit fraud. Campaigners warn the system could unfairly penalise vulnerable groups, with the DWP admitting some legitimate claims may be wrongly flagged, leading to wrongful denial of benefits and financial harm.

records.title: TikTok's AI Algorithms Spark Global Privacy and Mental Health Concerns
records.description: TikTok's AI-driven recommendation and advertising systems have led to privacy violations, with Chinese employees accessing Australian user data and regulatory warnings in Europe over non-consensual data use. The algorithm also promotes addictive content and censors sensitive topics, raising concerns about user rights, mental health, and potential political manipulation.

records.title: AI Elevator Monitoring System Prevents Accidents and Enables Rapid Rescue in Guangzhou
records.description: Guangzhou’s Yuexiu District has installed AI-powered elevator monitoring systems on nearly 700 elevators, using image recognition and video analysis to detect unsafe behaviors like bringing electric bikes inside. The system automatically halts elevator operation, issues alerts, and enables faster rescues, significantly improving passenger safety and reducing accident risks.

records.title: Amazon's Ring Shared Doorbell Footage with Police Without User Consent
records.description: Amazon's AI-enabled Ring doorbells provided video footage to law enforcement at least 11 times in 2022 without user consent, citing emergency circumstances. This practice, revealed in response to Senator Markey's inquiry, raises significant privacy and civil liberties concerns over unauthorized data sharing and the growing relationship between Ring and police agencies.

records.title: Myanmar Junta Expands AI-Powered Surveillance Using Chinese Facial Recognition Technology
records.description: Myanmar's military junta is expanding the use of Chinese-built surveillance cameras with AI-driven facial recognition across multiple cities. These systems, sourced from companies like Dahua, Huawei, and Hikvision, enable the tracking and repression of activists and resistance groups, raising serious concerns about ongoing human rights violations and state-led population surveillance.

records.title: NHTSA Investigates Fatal Tesla Crashes Involving Autopilot AI Systems
records.description: U.S. safety regulators are investigating two recent fatal Tesla crashes—one in California involving a pedestrian and another in Florida involving a collision with a truck—where Tesla’s Autopilot or advanced driver assistance AI systems are suspected to have been active, raising concerns about the technology’s safety and oversight.

records.title: Spanish Judge Launches Probe into NSO Group Over Pegasus Spyware Targeting Catalan Politicians
records.description: A Spanish judge has authorized an investigation into Israel's NSO Group after its AI-powered Pegasus spyware was allegedly used to hack over 60 phones of Catalan independence supporters, including politicians and activists, raising concerns over privacy violations and human rights abuses linked to the AI system's deployment.

records.title: NHTSA Investigates Fatal Florida Tesla Crash Involving Possible Autopilot Use
records.description: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has launched an investigation into a fatal crash in Florida where a Tesla Model S collided with a parked Walmart truck, killing two occupants. Authorities are examining whether Tesla's AI-powered Autopilot or partially automated driving system was active at the time of the incident.

records.title: NHTSA Investigates Fatal Tesla Crashes Involving Autopilot AI System
records.description: The U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration is investigating multiple fatal Tesla crashes, including incidents in Florida and California, to determine if the Autopilot AI system was active. These crashes resulted in several deaths, raising concerns about the safety and reliability of Tesla's advanced driver-assistance AI technology.

records.title: AI Trading Bot Causes Massive Client Losses in LUNA Crash
records.description: South Korean investment platform Uprise lost over 99% of client funds—about $20 million—after its AI trading system misjudged LUNA's price movements during a market crash. The AI, intended to manage risk, failed to predict a brief price spike, resulting in liquidation and significant financial harm to clients and the company.

records.title: Cruise Autonomous Vehicles Involved in Collision and Traffic Blockage Incidents in San Francisco
records.description: General Motors' Cruise autonomous vehicles were involved in two major AI incidents in San Francisco: a collision during a left turn that caused minor injuries, and a separate malfunction where six driverless taxis blocked traffic for hours. Both incidents highlight failures in Cruise's AI driving and remote intervention systems, disrupting public safety and infrastructure.

records.title: Baidu Xiaodu Smart Speaker Misused for Secretly Recording Homestay Guests, Causing Privacy Violations
records.description: A Baidu Xiaodu smart speaker with AI-powered camera features was misused in a Liaoning homestay to secretly record guests, resulting in multiple privacy violations. The incident prompted police investigation and Baidu’s cooperation, highlighting the risks of deploying AI surveillance devices outside intended family settings.

records.title: NHTSA Investigates Cruise Self-Driving Car Crash in San Francisco
records.description: A Cruise self-driving vehicle, operating in autonomous mode, was involved in a crash with a Toyota Prius in San Francisco on June 3, resulting in minor injuries to occupants of both vehicles. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has launched a special investigation into the incident, highlighting concerns over AI-driven vehicle safety.

records.title: YouTube AI Misclassifies Horror Video as Child-Friendly, Exposing Kids to Inappropriate Content
records.description: YouTube's AI content moderation system erroneously flagged horror videos from Kris Straub's Local58TV as suitable for children, overriding the creator's 18+ setting and preventing manual correction. This malfunction risked exposing children to disturbing content via YouTube Kids, highlighting failures in AI-driven content classification and child protection.

records.title: Spanish Government Officials Targeted by Pegasus Spyware: Judicial Investigation Advances
records.description: A Spanish judge is investigating the use of Pegasus, an AI-enabled spyware, to surveil top government officials, including the Prime Minister and ministers. The judge has summoned the Minister of Presidency as a witness and seeks testimony from the CEO of Pegasus's developer, highlighting privacy violations linked to AI-driven surveillance.

records.title: Tesla Recalls 59,000 Vehicles Over AI Emergency Call System Failure
records.description: Germany's road traffic agency recalled over 59,000 Tesla Model Y and Model 3 vehicles globally due to a software bug in the AI-powered automatic emergency call (eCall) system, which failed to contact first responders after serious accidents. The issue, posing significant safety risks, was addressed with an over-the-air software update.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot Nearly Causes Collision with Oncoming Train in Denver
records.description: A Tesla Model 3 using the Full Self-Driving (FSD) Autopilot system in Denver nearly turned into the path of an oncoming train, despite the AI detecting the train on its display. The driver had to intervene to prevent a collision, highlighting a critical malfunction and safety risk in Tesla's AI driving system.

records.title: Amazon Alexa Suggests Dangerous Challenge to Child, Raising Safety and Privacy Concerns
records.description: Amazon's AI assistant Alexa endangered a 10-year-old by suggesting a hazardous challenge involving electricity. The incident, along with privacy concerns and the potential for Alexa to replicate any voice—including those of deceased individuals—has raised significant ethical, safety, and privacy issues regarding the use and development of AI voice assistants.

records.title: Bank Facial Recognition Flaw Enables Massive Fraud, Exposes Privacy Risks in China
records.description: Criminals exploited vulnerabilities in the AI-powered facial recognition system of Bank of Communications, using fake faces to bypass security and steal nearly 2 million yuan from multiple customers. The bank denied responsibility, leading to lawsuits. Separate legal cases also highlight privacy violations from mandatory facial recognition in residential and public facilities.

records.title: China Deploys AI to Monitor Political Loyalty via Biometric and Neurological Surveillance
records.description: Chinese researchers at the Hefei Comprehensive National Science Center developed an AI system that analyzes facial expressions, brain waves, and skin responses to assess Communist Party members' political loyalty. The system's deployment has raised significant human rights concerns over privacy, freedom of thought, and technological coercion.

records.title: AI Search Algorithms Surface Nazi Memorabilia for Innocuous Query
records.description: Google, Bing, and DuckDuckGo's AI-powered image search algorithms displayed Nazi memorabilia in response to the neutral query 'desk ornament.' The incident, noticed globally, exposed users to offensive content due to algorithmic manipulation and insufficient filtering, prompting public outcry and a response from Google acknowledging the issue.

records.title: Italy Deploys AI Algorithm 'Vera' to Combat Tax Evasion
records.description: The Italian Revenue Agency has launched 'Vera', an AI-powered algorithm that analyzes financial, web, and social data to identify potential tax evaders. Approved by the Economy Minister and privacy authorities, the system generates risk lists for further human review, raising concerns about privacy and potential impacts on individuals' rights.

records.title: Instagram AI Moderation Wrongly Restricts Abortion-Related Content
records.description: Instagram's AI-driven content moderation system erroneously classified and restricted posts about abortion, hiding advocacy and informational content behind sensitive content warnings and age gates. The malfunction limited access to lawful information and advocacy, impacting users' rights to information and expression. Instagram acknowledged the issue as a programming error and is working to fix it.

records.title: TikTok Confirms China-Based Staff Accessed US User Data via Approval Process
records.description: TikTok confirmed that employees in China have accessed US user data through an approval process, raising privacy and legal concerns. The company, which uses AI to process user data, stated it now stores US data on Oracle servers and will delete problematic data from Chinese systems.

records.title: China's First Facial Recognition Lawsuit Highlights Privacy Risks in Residential Access Control
records.description: Residents in multiple Chinese cities, including Tianjin and Suzhou, sued property management companies for mandating AI-powered facial recognition as the sole entry method to residential complexes. Courts ruled in favor of the plaintiffs, citing privacy violations and requiring alternative access options and deletion of biometric data, underscoring AI-related privacy risks.

records.title: Google Maps AI Misleads Abortion Seekers in New York
records.description: Google Maps' AI-driven search results have directed users seeking abortion services in New York to anti-abortion Crisis Pregnancy Centers (CPCs), which do not provide abortions and may offer misleading information. New York Attorney General Letitia James has urged Google to correct this issue to protect access to accurate healthcare information.

records.title: TikTok Algorithm Implicated in Child Deaths and Political Manipulation
records.description: TikTok and its parent company ByteDance face lawsuits after their AI-driven recommendation algorithm promoted the deadly 'blackout challenge' to children, resulting in two deaths. Additionally, TikTok's algorithm is accused of enabling political manipulation and privacy violations under Chinese government influence, raising concerns about AI-driven harm to individuals and society.

records.title: Cruise Robotaxis Malfunction, Block San Francisco Streets for Hours
records.description: A fleet of GM's Cruise autonomous vehicles simultaneously malfunctioned in San Francisco, clustering and blocking a major intersection for several hours. The AI-driven robotaxis had to be manually removed by staff, causing significant traffic disruption but no reported injuries. The incident highlights operational risks of self-driving AI systems in urban environments.

records.title: FBI Warns of Deepfake Scams in Remote Job Applications
records.description: The FBI has reported a surge in complaints about scammers using AI-generated deepfakes and stolen personal information to fraudulently apply for remote tech jobs. These deepfakes, including manipulated video, audio, and images, are used to impersonate others during online interviews, posing risks of identity theft and unauthorized access to sensitive corporate data.

records.title: AI-Driven Social Media Amplifies Disinformation and Hate Speech Ahead of Kenyan Elections
records.description: AI algorithms on platforms like TikTok, Facebook, and Twitter have amplified political disinformation and hate speech in Kenya, stoking ethnic tensions ahead of elections. Rights groups warn that inadequate moderation, especially in local languages, is increasing the risk of violence in a historically volatile environment.

records.title: Meta's AI-Driven Ad Targeting Promotes Harmful, Unproven Cancer Treatments
records.description: Meta's AI-powered ad systems on Facebook and Instagram targeted cancer patients with misleading ads for unproven and potentially harmful treatments, such as Apatone from CHIPSA hospital. Despite policies against deceptive health claims, these ads persisted, exposing vulnerable users to health risks and financial exploitation.

records.title: AI-Driven Menstrual and Digital Data Used in Abortion Prosecutions in the US
records.description: AI-powered menstrual tracking apps and digital surveillance tools have enabled the collection and analysis of sensitive personal data, which has been used as evidence in criminal cases against women in US states with restrictive abortion laws. This has led to privacy violations and legal harm, highlighting the risks of AI-enabled surveillance.

records.title: Bayraktar AI Drones Donated and Deployed in Ukraine Conflict
records.description: Turkish company Baykar donated Bayraktar TB2 AI-enabled drones to Ukraine, following public fundraising campaigns. These drones, actively used by Ukrainian forces, have contributed to the destruction of Russian military assets, illustrating the direct impact of AI-powered weaponry in ongoing armed conflict.

records.title: Deepfake Klitschko Impersonation Deceives European Mayors
records.description: An unknown actor used AI-powered deepfake technology to impersonate Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko in video calls, deceiving mayors of Berlin, Vienna, Madrid, and others. The realistic fake led to misinformation, confusion, and official investigations, highlighting the risks of AI-driven synthetic media in political contexts.

records.title: Deepfake AI Fraud Causes Major Financial Losses to Organizations
records.description: Criminals are increasingly using AI-generated deepfakes—synthetic audio and video—to impersonate executives and commit fraud, resulting in significant financial losses for organizations. The widespread availability of deepfake technology has enabled sophisticated scams, costing companies hundreds of thousands to millions of dollars annually.

records.title: Meta Settles DOJ Lawsuit Over AI-Driven Discriminatory Housing Ads
records.description: Meta (formerly Facebook) settled with the U.S. Department of Justice after its AI-powered ad algorithms were found to discriminate in housing ads based on protected characteristics like race and religion, violating the Fair Housing Act. Meta agreed to change its algorithms, end certain ad tools, and submit to court oversight.

records.title: Robots Exhibit Racist and Sexist Behavior Due to Flawed AI Models
records.description: Researchers from Johns Hopkins, Georgia Tech, and University of Washington found that robots using the popular CLIP AI model consistently displayed gender and racial biases, favoring men over women and white people over people of color. The study highlights real-world risks of deploying AI systems trained on biased internet data.

records.title: China's Mass AI-Driven Surveillance and Biometric Data Collection for Authoritarian Control
records.description: Chinese authorities are using AI systems—including facial recognition, voiceprint analysis, DNA and iris databases, and mobile tracking—to conduct unprecedented mass surveillance and data collection. These technologies enable extensive monitoring, targeting, and repression of citizens and minorities, resulting in ongoing violations of privacy and human rights to reinforce authoritarian rule.

records.title: AI Robots Linked to Worker Injuries and Bias in Real-World Deployments
records.description: Reports indicate that Amazon warehouses using AI-powered robots have higher employee injury rates, suggesting operational pressures from automation harm workers. Separately, a study found that robots with AI trained on biased internet data exhibit sexist and racist behaviors, raising concerns about discriminatory harm if such systems are widely deployed.

records.title: EU Investigates NSO Group Over Pegasus Spyware Misuse in Multiple Countries
records.description: The NSO Group's AI-powered Pegasus spyware was used by at least five EU countries to surveil political leaders, journalists, and activists, leading to human rights and privacy violations. The European Parliament's PEGA Committee is investigating, with NSO admitting misuse and facing scrutiny over its practices and regulatory compliance.

records.title: Chinese AI 'Mind-Reading' Helmet Raises Privacy and Human Rights Concerns
records.description: Chinese researchers developed an AI-powered helmet that detects when men view porn by analyzing brainwaves, triggering alarms for explicit content. Intended to aid government censors, the device raises significant concerns about privacy violations and potential human rights abuses due to its use in intrusive surveillance and censorship.

records.title: Tesla AI-Driven Crashes and Regulatory Scrutiny Over Reporting and Safety
records.description: Tesla's AI-powered Autopilot and Full Self-Driving Beta systems have been involved in numerous crashes, including incidents with injuries and fatalities. Investigations reveal Tesla may have underreported such crashes to U.S. regulators. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration is probing the safety and reporting practices of Tesla's AI driving systems.

records.title: NHTSA Reports Hundreds of Crashes and Deaths Involving Self-Driving Cars, Mostly Teslas
records.description: The U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) reported nearly 400 crashes involving AI-powered self-driving and driver-assist systems over a 10-month period, with Tesla vehicles accounting for most incidents. Six deaths were linked to these technologies, highlighting safety risks and concerns about overreliance on autopilot features.

records.title: AI-Enabled Drones and Defense Systems Cause and Prevent Harm in Ukraine War
records.description: AI-powered drones from Turkey and Taiwan have been used by Ukraine to inflict significant damage on Russian forces, causing casualties and destruction. Meanwhile, a US company is helping Ukraine develop an AI-enabled missile defense system to intercept Russian attacks and reduce civilian harm, highlighting both the destructive and protective roles of AI in the conflict.

records.title: US Senators Question TikTok Over Spread of Russian Pro-War Propaganda via AI Moderation Failures
records.description: US Republican senators questioned TikTok's CEO about the platform's AI-driven failure to moderate and remove Russian state-approved pro-war propaganda, which remained accessible while other content was censored. This AI moderation lapse is linked to increased support for the Ukraine war and potential harm to affected communities.

records.title: Tabelog Ordered to Pay Damages for Algorithmic Rating Manipulation
records.description: Tokyo District Court ruled that Tabelog operator Kakaku.com violated antitrust law by knowingly changing its restaurant rating algorithm to disadvantage the Hanryumura chain, causing significant customer loss and economic harm. The court ordered Kakaku.com to pay 38.4 million yen in damages, highlighting the impact of AI-driven rating systems.

records.title: AI-Driven Data Collection and Search Mislead and Endanger Abortion Seekers
records.description: Investigations revealed Facebook's AI-powered tracking tools collected and shared sensitive data from users seeking abortion information, risking privacy and safety. Simultaneously, Google's AI-driven search results misdirected users to misleading crisis pregnancy centers, obstructing access to accurate abortion services. Both incidents highlight AI systems' role in violating rights and endangering vulnerable individuals.

records.title: Tesla Driver-Assist AI Linked to Majority of US Autonomous Vehicle Crashes
records.description: Tesla vehicles accounted for nearly 70% of reported US crashes involving AI-powered driver-assist systems from July 2021 to May 2022, including most serious injuries and fatalities. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration cautions that data lacks full context but highlights significant safety concerns with these AI systems.

records.title: Turkish Armed Drone Strikes Cause Civilian and Militant Deaths in Iraqi Kurdistan
records.description: Turkish military used armed drones, likely AI-enabled, to strike vehicles and buildings in Iraqi Kurdistan, targeting alleged PKK members. The attacks killed at least six people, including civilians and militants, and injured others, highlighting the lethal impact of AI-driven military systems in conflict zones.

records.title: Facebook's AI Fails to Block Extremist Content in East Africa
records.description: A study by the Institute for Strategic Dialogue found that Facebook's AI-driven content moderation failed to detect and remove extremist posts supporting IS and al-Shabab in East Africa. This allowed violent content to spread widely, threatening public safety and undermining trust during Kenya's national election.

records.title: Meta's AI Moderation Shortcomings Harm Human Content Moderators
records.description: Whistleblowers Frances Haugen and Daniel Motaung revealed that Meta's reliance on AI for Facebook content moderation is inadequate, forcing human moderators to handle traumatic material. This has led to severe mental health issues, including PTSD, among moderators, highlighting the harm caused by the AI system's limitations and deployment practices.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot Linked to Hundreds of Accidents and Multiple Deaths in the US
records.description: Tesla vehicles equipped with AI-based Autopilot and driver assistance systems have been involved in over 270 reported accidents and at least 10 deaths in the US since 2016. Federal investigations by NHTSA highlight a higher accident rate for Tesla's system compared to rivals, raising concerns about the safety and reliability of its AI technology.

records.title: Charles Schwab Settles $187M SEC Case Over Misleading Robo-Advisor Practices
records.description: Charles Schwab agreed to pay $187 million after the SEC found its robo-advisor, Schwab Intelligent Portfolios, misled clients by allocating excessive cash in portfolios for Schwab’s profit, resulting in lower client returns. The AI-driven system’s undisclosed practices directly caused financial harm to investors.

records.title: YouTube's AI Algorithms Amplify Hate Against Muslims and Women in India
records.description: Reports by NYU Stern Center reveal that YouTube's AI-powered recommendation systems have amplified Islamophobic and misogynistic content in India, fueling conspiracy theories and inciting violence against Muslims and women. Influencers linked to the ruling BJP exploited these algorithms, prompting calls for greater transparency and improved content moderation.

records.title: Taiwanese YouTuber Used AI Deepfake Technology to Create and Sell Non-Consensual Pornographic Videos, Sparking Major Legal Case
records.description: YouTuber Zhu Yuchen (Xiao Yu) and an accomplice used AI deepfake software to create and sell non-consensual pornographic videos featuring the faces of 119 public figures, causing severe psychological harm and privacy violations. The case led to criminal charges, civil lawsuits, and calls for stricter digital crime laws in Taiwan.

records.title: Facebook's AI Fails to Detect Violent Hate Speech in Ads, Enabling Ethnic Incitement
records.description: Facebook's AI content moderation systems repeatedly failed to detect and block blatantly violent hate speech in ads targeting Ethiopian ethnic groups, as tested by Global Witness and Foxglove. The approved ads called for violence, highlighting ongoing risks of AI moderation failures contributing to real-world ethnic violence and human rights violations.

records.title: Facebook's 2018 Algorithm Change Amplified Divisive GOP Content, Research Finds
records.description: Research shows that Facebook's 2018 algorithm change, designed to prioritize posts from family and friends, inadvertently boosted engagement with local Republican groups and amplified divisive content. This AI-driven shift led to increased polarization and negativity, raising concerns about the societal impact of algorithmic content curation.

records.title: US Regulators Intensify Probe into Tesla Autopilot After Crashes and Injuries
records.description: The US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has escalated its investigation into Tesla's Autopilot AI system after at least 16 crashes involving parked emergency vehicles, resulting in injuries and a death. The probe covers 830,000 vehicles and examines Autopilot's safety limitations and driver monitoring failures.

records.title: Chinese Court Rules Against Mandatory Facial Recognition for Residential Access
records.description: A resident in Tianjin sued his property management for requiring facial recognition as the sole method to enter his residential complex.
