records.description: Curtin University in Australia requested the retraction of a research paper by former staffer Liu Wanquan and Chinese collaborators, which developed AI facial recognition technology to identify Uyghur and other minorities. The research, funded by the Chinese government, lacked ethical approval and is linked to human rights abuses through state surveillance and repression.

records.title: Facebook Algorithm Change Amplifies Misinformation and Harm
records.description: In 2018, Facebook altered its AI-driven News Feed algorithm to prioritize reshared content, aiming to boost user well-being. Instead, the change led to increased misinformation, toxicity, and polarization, with internal research revealing harm to communities and teen mental health. Despite warnings, Facebook leadership did not reverse the algorithm.

records.title: AI-Enabled Drones Used in Combat and Swarm Attacks in Afghanistan and China
records.description: The Taliban used AI-enabled armed drones to track and attack targets during their capture of Kabul, causing direct harm. Separately, China has developed autonomous drone swarms capable of coordinated attacks, previously used to destroy oil fields. Both incidents highlight the real-world impact of AI-driven military drones.

records.title: Facebook Knew Instagram's AI Algorithms Harmed Teen Mental Health
records.description: Internal Facebook research revealed that Instagram's AI-driven content algorithms significantly worsened mental health issues among teens, especially girls, causing increased anxiety, depression, and body image problems. Despite knowing these harms, Facebook withheld evidence, prompting regulatory and legislative scrutiny in the US and UK.

records.title: NHTSA Investigates Tesla Autopilot and Similar AI Driver-Assist Systems After Crashes
records.description: The U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is investigating Tesla's Autopilot and similar AI-based driver-assist systems from 12 automakers after at least 11 crashes involving Tesla vehicles and emergency responders, resulting in one death and multiple injuries. The probe seeks data on system performance and crash reports.

records.title: Boeing 737 MAX AI System Defect Leads to Fatal Crashes and Legal Action
records.description: U.S. prosecutors are preparing to charge a former Boeing test pilot for misleading regulators about defects in the 737 MAX's automated flight control system (MCAS), an AI-related component. The system's malfunction led to two crashes in 2018 and 2019, causing 346 deaths and resulting in global grounding of the aircraft.

records.title: AI Deepfake App Enables Nonconsensual Pornography, Prompting Outcry and Deplatforming
records.description: A new AI-powered deepfake app allowed users to upload photos and generate highly realistic, nonconsensual pornographic videos, primarily targeting women. The app, discovered by researchers and reported by MIT Technology Review, caused significant psychological and reputational harm before being taken offline following public backlash. Similar unethical AI tools remain online.

records.title: AI-Enabled Saudi Military Drone Shot Down in Yemen's Saada Province
records.description: Yemeni forces shot down a Saudi Air Force Wing Loong 2 combat reconnaissance drone, an AI-enabled system, over Saada province during hostile operations. The incident highlights the use and destruction of AI-powered military drones in active conflict, resulting in harm to property and escalating military tensions.

records.title: Facebook's AI Moderation System Fails to Enforce Rules Equally, Causing Harm
records.description: Facebook's AI-driven content moderation system, intended to enforce platform rules, has been circumvented for millions of high-profile users through the 'XCheck' program. This selective enforcement has allowed harmful and rule-violating content to remain online, leading to psychological harm, privacy violations, and community harm, especially affecting children and teenagers.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot Misuse Leads to DUI Arrest and Raises Safety Concerns
records.description: A California driver was arrested for DUI after her Tesla, set on Autopilot, continued driving while she was unconscious, eventually stopping on a freeway. Studies also show Tesla Autopilot use leads to decreased driver attention, increasing safety risks. These incidents highlight the dangers of AI-assisted driving misuse.

records.title: Consumer Protection Agency Warns Against Relying on AI Apps for Mushroom Identification
records.description: The consumer protection agency in Saxony-Anhalt, Germany, warns that AI-based mobile apps for mushroom identification are unreliable and may lead to serious health risks, including poisoning. Overreliance on these apps, which often miss key features like smell and texture, has contributed to an increase in mushroom poisoning cases.

records.title: Apple Issues Emergency Update After Pegasus Spyware Exploits iOS Vulnerability
records.description: Apple released urgent security updates after researchers at Citizen Lab discovered that the NSO Group's Pegasus spyware exploited a zero-day vulnerability in iOS, enabling remote surveillance of activists, journalists, and politicians. The AI-enabled spyware led to significant privacy and human rights violations before the flaw was patched.

records.title: AI-Enabled Halo System Prevents Serious Injury in Formula 1 Crash
records.description: During the 2021 Italian Grand Prix in Monza, the AI-enabled Halo safety system in Lewis Hamilton's Formula 1 car prevented serious injury when Max Verstappen's car landed on Hamilton's cockpit. The system absorbed the impact, with Hamilton crediting it for saving his life and reducing harm.

records.title: Meituan Alters Delivery Algorithm After Labor Rights Concerns in China
records.description: Chinese food delivery giant Meituan is revising its AI-driven delivery time algorithm following government pressure and criticism that it created unsafe working conditions and eroded labor rights for gig workers. The changes aim to reduce pressure on riders and improve flexibility and worker protections.

records.title: Chevy Bolt Recalled After AI-Managed Battery Defects Cause Fires
records.description: General Motors recalled about 141,000 Chevrolet Bolt electric vehicles globally after battery defects, managed by AI-based systems, led to multiple fires. Owners reported safety concerns and demanded buybacks. The recall follows incidents dating back to 2019, highlighting failures in the vehicles' AI-driven battery management systems.

records.title: Facebook's AI Job Ad Algorithm Accused of Gender Discrimination in the UK
records.description: Campaign group Global Witness found that Facebook's AI-driven ad targeting system disproportionately showed job ads for roles like mechanics and pilots to men, and nursery nurses and psychologists to women in the UK. The system also allowed exclusion by gender and age, violating equality laws and leading to discriminatory outcomes.

records.title: Amazon's AI Algorithms Promote COVID-19 Misinformation, Lawmakers Raise Public Health Concerns
records.description: Amazon's AI-driven recommendation and search algorithms have promoted books and products containing COVID-19 misinformation, including anti-vaccine claims and false cures. U.S. lawmakers, including Sen. Elizabeth Warren and Rep. Adam Schiff, criticized Amazon for profiting from and failing to curb the spread of harmful health misinformation, raising public health concerns.

records.title: TikTok's AI Algorithm Exposes Minors to Harmful Adult Content
records.description: Investigations revealed that TikTok's AI-driven recommendation algorithm exposed minors, including users as young as 13, to thousands of videos featuring sex, drugs, alcohol, and other explicit content. Despite age restrictions, the AI system failed to filter harmful material, resulting in significant risk and harm to underage users.

records.title: Pegasus Spyware Used to Hack Hungarian Opposition Media Owner's Phone
records.description: In Hungary, the AI-enabled Pegasus spyware was used to hack the phone of Zoltán Páva, an opposition media owner and former politician. Security experts from Amnesty International and Citizen Lab confirmed unauthorized surveillance occurred in March and May 2021, violating privacy and human rights.

records.title: AI-Assisted Content Moderation on WhatsApp Breaches User Privacy
records.description: Reports reveal that Facebook uses AI systems to flag WhatsApp messages reported as spam, allowing human moderators to access and review these messages despite claims of end-to-end encryption. This practice has led to privacy violations and the sharing of user data with authorities, undermining WhatsApp's privacy assurances.

records.title: TikTok Faces Lawsuits in the Netherlands Over AI-Driven Privacy Violations Affecting Children
records.description: Dutch consumer groups have filed lawsuits against TikTok, alleging its AI-driven algorithms unlawfully collect and process user data, violating privacy laws and children's rights. The lawsuits demand billions in damages, citing lack of transparency and improper data handling affecting millions, including minors, in the Netherlands.

records.title: German Federal Police Acquires and Uses Controversial Pegasus Spyware
records.description: The German Federal Criminal Police Office (BKA) purchased and used a modified version of the AI-enabled Pegasus spyware from NSO Group, despite legal and ethical concerns. Pegasus has been linked to human rights violations globally, including surveillance of journalists and opposition figures, raising significant privacy and rights concerns in Germany.

records.title: Chinese AI-Driven Prenatal Test Under Investigation for Data Privacy and Military Links
records.description: Chinese company BGI's AI-powered NIFTY prenatal genetic test, used by over 8.4 million women globally, is under investigation by regulators in five countries over concerns about data privacy, potential sharing of sensitive genetic data with the Chinese military, and lack of transparency, raising risks of privacy and human rights violations.

records.title: Li Auto ONE's AI Braking System Fails to Detect Pedestrians, Manufacturer Confirms Issue
records.description: Tests of the 2021 Li Auto ONE's AI-powered automatic emergency braking (AEB) and assisted driving systems revealed a failure to detect and stop for pedestrian dummies and common road obstacles, posing safety risks. Li Auto acknowledged the issue, attributing it to incomplete software and promising future updates to address the malfunction.

records.title: Houthi Drone and Missile Attacks on Saudi Aramco Facilities Cause Injuries and Damage
records.description: Yemeni Houthi forces launched coordinated attacks using AI-enabled drones and ballistic missiles against Saudi Aramco facilities and military bases in multiple Saudi cities. The strikes caused injuries, including to children, and damaged homes, highlighting the direct harm resulting from the use of autonomous weapon systems.

records.title: Nigerian Government Warns of Harm from AI-Generated Deepfake News
records.description: The Nigerian government, represented by Minister Lai Mohammed, has raised concerns about the increasing use of AI-generated deepfake news targeting officials. These manipulated videos and images are spreading misinformation, damaging reputations, and misleading the public, making it difficult to distinguish real news from fabricated content.

records.title: AI Hiring Systems Exclude Millions of Qualified Job Seekers in the US
records.description: Automated hiring and résumé-screening AI systems used by US employers are systematically rejecting millions of qualified candidates due to inflexible and biased filtering criteria. This has led to widespread exclusion of 'hidden workers,' causing significant harm to job seekers and contributing to labor market inefficiencies.

records.title: AI-Enabled Military Drones Cause Civilian Harm in Ongoing Conflicts
records.description: Since 2015, the US has conducted over 14,000 drone strikes in Afghanistan using AI-enabled military drones, resulting in civilian deaths and violations of international law. The use of autonomous or semi-autonomous drones in warfare has led to significant harm to persons and communities.

records.title: Facebook AI Labels Black Men as 'Primates', Sparks Outrage and Apology
records.description: Facebook's AI-powered recommendation system mistakenly labeled videos featuring Black men as related to 'primates,' exposing significant racial bias in its algorithms. The incident led to public backlash, Facebook's apology, and the disabling of the feature while the company investigates the root cause.

records.title: Fatal Tesla Autopilot Crash Investigated in New York
records.description: A Tesla vehicle using its partially automated driving system struck and killed a man changing a flat tire on the Long Island Expressway in New York. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration is investigating the incident, highlighting ongoing concerns about the safety of Tesla's AI-driven Autopilot system.

records.title: Facebook's AI Algorithms Amplify Misinformation During 2020 US Election
records.description: A study reviewed by researchers from New York and Grenoble Alps universities found that Facebook's AI-driven recommendation algorithms amplified misinformation, resulting in false news receiving six times more engagement than reliable sources during the 2020 US election period. This highlights the platform's role in spreading harmful misinformation.

records.title: Apple and Other Tech Giants Face Lawsuits Over Voice Assistant Privacy Violations
records.description: Apple, along with Google and Amazon, faces multiple lawsuits in the United States alleging that their AI-powered voice assistants (Siri, Google Assistant, Alexa) recorded users' private conversations without consent, violating privacy rights. Courts have allowed class-action suits to proceed, highlighting ongoing concerns about AI-driven privacy breaches.

records.title: FAA Grounds Virgin Galactic After Spacecraft Deviates from Approved Flight Path
records.description: Virgin Galactic's SpaceShipTwo, carrying Richard Branson, deviated from its authorized flight path during a July 2021 mission, triggering safety warnings. The FAA grounded the spacecraft and launched an investigation, citing potential risks linked to the vehicle's advanced automated or AI-based navigation and control systems. No injuries occurred, but public safety concerns remain.

records.title: Apple Faces Lawsuit Over Siri's Unauthorized Recording of Private Conversations
records.description: A U.S. federal judge has allowed a class-action lawsuit against Apple to proceed, alleging that its AI voice assistant Siri improperly recorded and shared users' private conversations without consent due to accidental activations, violating privacy rights and data protection laws. The case highlights privacy risks associated with AI voice assistants.

records.title: China's COVID-19 AI Surveillance Expands to Mass Social Control
records.description: China's government used AI-driven big data systems to monitor COVID-19, collecting personal and biometric data to assign health risk codes. These systems are now being repurposed for broader mass surveillance and social credit enforcement, resulting in privacy breaches, data hacks, and increased social control, raising significant human rights concerns.

records.title: Delhi High Court Scrutinizes AI-Driven Surveillance Systems Over Privacy Concerns
records.description: The Delhi High Court has directed the Indian government to provide detailed legal and procedural information regarding the use of AI-enabled surveillance systems—CMS, NATGRID, and NETRA—following public interest litigation alleging these systems endanger citizens' privacy rights through generalized monitoring and interception of communications.

records.title: Vulnerabilities in Russian Banking Chatbots Enable Financial Theft
records.description: Security experts discovered critical vulnerabilities in AI-powered chatbots used by Russian banks, allowing attackers to bypass security, access sensitive customer data, and perform unauthorized money transfers. These flaws expose users to financial theft and privacy breaches, affecting a significant portion of Russian credit organizations.

records.title: Data Breach Exposes 1.3 Million Users of Indonesia's COVID-19 Tracing App
records.description: Indonesia is investigating a major data breach in its COVID-19 tracing app, eHAC, which exposed sensitive personal and health information of 1.3 million users due to inadequate security protocols. The breach, discovered by vpnMentor researchers, raises significant privacy concerns for affected individuals and institutions.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot Crash and AI Energy Management Efforts Highlight EV Risks
records.description: A Tesla vehicle using Autopilot crashed into a stationary police car in Florida, marking the 12th such incident involving emergency vehicles and raising concerns about AI-driven driver assistance safety. Separately, ex-Tesla engineers are developing AI-based energy management solutions to prevent power grid failures as EV adoption grows.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot and Battery AI Systems Under Investigation After Crashes and Fire
records.description: U.S. authorities are investigating Tesla's Autopilot AI after multiple crashes with emergency vehicles, resulting in injuries and a fatality. Separately, a Tesla Model X caught fire in a Luxembourg service center, raising concerns about AI-managed battery systems. Both incidents highlight safety risks linked to Tesla's AI technologies.

records.title: Theranos Blood Test Fraud Trial: Elizabeth Holmes Faces Charges Over AI System Misuse
records.description: Elizabeth Holmes, founder of Theranos, is on trial in California for allegedly defrauding investors, patients, and doctors by misrepresenting the capabilities of her company's AI-driven blood analysis system. The malfunction and misuse of the technology led to inaccurate medical results and significant financial harm.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot Crashes into Parked Police Car in Florida
records.description: A Tesla Model 3 operating on Autopilot collided with a parked police vehicle with flashing lights near Orlando, Florida, injuring the Tesla driver and another motorist. The incident is part of a series of similar crashes involving Tesla's AI system failing to detect emergency vehicles, prompting an NHTSA investigation.

records.title: California Lawmakers Target Amazon's AI-Driven Workplace Practices
records.description: California lawmakers are advancing a bill to regulate Amazon's use of AI-driven algorithms that set warehouse worker quotas and monitor performance. These systems have led to increased injuries and labor rights violations, prompting proposed requirements for transparency and protections against health-harming practices and retaliation.

records.title: Clearview AI Faces Legal and Global Scrutiny Over Unlawful Facial Recognition Practices
records.description: Clearview AI, a US-based facial recognition company, is under legal scrutiny for collecting and processing biometric data without consent, violating Illinois' Biometric Information Privacy Act (BIPA). Courts have allowed lawsuits to proceed, and leaked reports reveal unauthorized use by police in the Netherlands and government agencies in 24 countries, raising global privacy concerns.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot and Nio Driving-Assist Failures Lead to Crashes and Injuries
records.description: AI-powered driving-assist systems, including Tesla's Autopilot and Nio's pilot mode, were involved in multiple crashes in the US and China. Incidents included a fatal crash in China and several collisions in Florida, causing injuries and property damage, highlighting risks and ongoing regulatory investigations into these AI systems' safety.

records.title: US Drone Strikes in Afghanistan Cause Civilian Casualties Amid AI-Enabled Warfare
records.description: Following the US withdrawal from Afghanistan, President Biden authorized AI-enabled drone strikes targeting ISIS-K. These strikes, intended as retaliation for attacks on US forces, resulted in civilian casualties, including children. The incidents have sparked calls for a moratorium on drone warfare due to repeated harm caused by AI-driven military operations.

records.title: AI Deepfake Technology Used to Defame Chinese Actor Liu Haoran, Studio Files Police Report
records.description: Chinese actor Liu Haoran became the target of widespread defamatory videos and images created using AI face-swapping (deepfake) technology. The manipulated content, including explicit material, was maliciously distributed online, causing significant reputational harm. Liu's studio has reported the incident to police to protect his rights.

records.title: US Drone Strike Using AI Targets IS-K Planner in Afghanistan
records.description: The US military conducted a drone strike, likely utilizing AI for targeting, against an alleged IS-K planner in Afghanistan's Nangarhar province following a suicide bombing at Kabul airport. The AI-driven drone operation resulted in the reported death of the target, highlighting the lethal use of AI in military actions.

records.title: Toyota Suspends Self-Driving Shuttles After Paralympian Injured in Tokyo
records.description: During the Tokyo Paralympics, a Toyota e-Palette autonomous shuttle struck and injured visually impaired athlete Aramitsu Kitazono in the athletes' village. The incident, involving both AI and human oversight, led Toyota to suspend all self-driving shuttles and issue a public apology, highlighting challenges in autonomous vehicle safety.

records.title: US Federal Agencies and Indian Railways Expand Facial Recognition, Raising Privacy Concerns
records.description: Ten US federal agencies plan to significantly expand facial recognition surveillance for security and monitoring, sparking criticism from digital rights advocates over privacy and potential rights violations. Similarly, Indian Railways has deployed NtechLab's facial recognition system, raising civil liberties concerns amid pending privacy legislation.

records.title: Breach of Election Management Software Raises Security Risks
records.description: Unauthorized copies of Dominion Voting Systems software, used for managing and tallying election results, were distributed at a public event organized by Mike Lindell. The breach, involving software from Colorado and Michigan, increases the risk of election interference and threatens the integrity of future U.S. elections.

records.title: YouTube Uses AI to Remove Over 1 Million COVID-19 Misinformation Videos
records.description: YouTube, using AI-driven content moderation, has removed over one million videos containing dangerous COVID-19 misinformation, such as false cures and hoax claims, since February 2020. The action aims to mitigate public health risks posed by misinformation, relying on guidance from health authorities like the CDC and WHO.

records.title: Facebook Fined in South Korea for Unauthorized Facial Recognition AI Use
records.description: South Korea's Personal Information Protection Commission fined Facebook $5.5 million for creating and storing facial recognition templates of 200,000 users without consent between April 2018 and September 2019. The AI-driven privacy violation led to orders for Facebook to destroy the data and improve user consent mechanisms.

records.title: AI-Powered Smart Canes Improve Mobility for Visually Impaired in Bursa
records.description: In Bursa, Turkey, İnegöl Municipality introduced AI-powered smart canes for 24 visually impaired residents. The canes, equipped with sensors and smartphone integration, provide real-time audio and vibration alerts to help users navigate safely. Training sessions were held to ensure effective use, enhancing mobility and safety.

records.title: Shield AI's Autonomous Drones Deployed in Middle East Conflict Zones
records.description: Shield AI, a San Diego-based company, has raised $210 million to advance its AI-powered autonomous drones, which have been used by the U.S. military in Middle East conflict zones for surveillance and reconnaissance. The deployment of these AI systems in active war zones raises concerns about potential harm and risks associated with autonomous military technology.

records.title: DHS AI System ATLAS Flags Naturalized Americans for Citizenship Revocation
records.description: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security uses an AI system called ATLAS to scan immigrants' records and flag naturalized Americans for potential citizenship revocation. Operating with secret criteria and limited transparency, ATLAS has led to concerns about wrongful targeting, rights violations, and lack of due process for affected individuals.

records.title: Tesla's FSD and Autopilot AI Systems Linked to Accidents and Regulatory Scrutiny in the US
records.description: Tesla's Full Self-Driving (FSD) and Autopilot AI systems have been linked to multiple accidents in the US, resulting in injuries and one death. CEO Elon Musk admitted the latest FSD Beta is inadequate. US regulators have launched formal investigations into the safety and marketing of Tesla's autonomous driving features.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot Criticized Amid Safety Concerns and Federal Investigation
records.description: Elon Musk publicly criticized Tesla's FSD Beta 9.2 autopilot software, acknowledging its imperfections. This comes as the U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration investigates multiple crashes involving Tesla vehicles using the AI-driven system, raising concerns about its safety and the risk of harm to drivers and passengers.

records.title: TikTok's AI Algorithms Enable Spread of Extremist and Hateful Content
records.description: Reports from the Institute for Strategic Dialogue reveal that TikTok's AI-driven recommendation and moderation systems have failed to prevent the widespread dissemination of antisemitic, racist, and extremist content. Users exploit algorithmic weaknesses to evade detection, resulting in millions of views for harmful videos and significant community harm.

records.title: Apple's CSAM Detection AI Sparks Privacy Scandal and Technical Flaws
records.description: Apple has used AI-based systems since 2019 to scan iCloud Mail and user photos for child sexual abuse material (CSAM), sparking global privacy concerns. The NeuralHash algorithm, embedded in iOS, was found to have serious flaws, including hash collisions, risking wrongful accusations and privacy violations. Widespread protests and expert criticism followed.

records.title: US Army Uses Controversial Clearview AI Facial Recognition for Criminal Investigations
records.description: The US Army's Criminal Investigation Command has contracted Clearview AI's facial recognition system, which scrapes billions of social media images, for crime detection. The technology's unproven accuracy and privacy violations have raised concerns about potential misidentification and human rights infringements. The Army reportedly attempted to conceal its use of this AI tool.

records.title: Pegasus Spyware Exploits iPhone Vulnerabilities to Target Bahraini Activists
records.description: Citizen Lab discovered that the AI-powered Pegasus spyware, developed by NSO Group, exploited zero-click vulnerabilities in Apple’s iMessage to infect iPhones of at least nine Bahraini activists. The attacks bypassed Apple’s latest security protections, resulting in significant privacy and human rights violations.

records.title: AI Algorithms Used for Employee Dismissals in Spain Spark Labor Rights Concerns
records.description: Spanish labor union UGT reports that companies are using AI algorithms to automate employee dismissals, violating workers' fundamental rights and existing data protection laws. Notable cases include TAP Portugal and Xsolla. The incidents have prompted calls to accelerate EU legislation to regulate AI use in employment decisions.

records.title: Facebook Conceals Report on AI-Driven Spread of COVID-19 Vaccine Misinformation
records.description: Facebook concealed a report revealing that its AI-powered content recommendation system amplified a misleading article about COVID-19 vaccines, making it the most viewed link in the US in early 2021. The company's management withheld the report to avoid reputational harm, indirectly contributing to public health misinformation.

records.title: AI-Enabled Weapon Turret 'Koralp' Deployed in Turkey for Enhanced Targeting
records.description: Turkey has deployed the AI-powered remote-controlled weapon turret 'Koralp,' designed to autonomously identify and engage targets, including humans and vehicles, in combat scenarios. The system aims to reduce human error and increase operational speed, raising concerns about AI-driven lethal force and potential harm in military operations.

records.title: Apple's AI-Driven Privacy Enables CSAM Distribution, Prompting New Detection Tools
records.description: Internal messages revealed during the Epic Games trial show Apple's anti-fraud chief acknowledged that Apple's privacy-focused AI systems inadvertently made iCloud a major platform for distributing child sexual abuse material (CSAM). This realization led Apple to introduce AI-based CSAM detection tools to address the harm.

records.title: BMW Recalls 3,561 Imported Cars in China Due to AI-Controlled Brake Software Defect
records.description: BMW (China) is recalling 3,561 imported 540i and Z4 vehicles produced between June 2018 and May 2021 due to a software defect in the engine electronic control module (DME) that manages the vacuum pump for braking. The malfunction can impair braking performance, posing a safety risk. Affected vehicles will receive free software reprogramming.

records.title: Bahraini Government Uses Pegasus Spyware to Hack Activists' iPhones
records.description: The Bahraini government used NSO Group's AI-powered Pegasus spyware to hack the iPhones of at least nine activists, including human rights defenders and political dissidents, between June 2020 and February 2021. The attacks exploited zero-click vulnerabilities, bypassing Apple security and resulting in significant human rights violations.

records.title: French COVID-19 App TousAntiCovid Exposes User Privacy via AI-Driven Data Collection
records.description: Researchers revealed that France's TousAntiCovid app, which uses AI-based contact tracing protocols, collects detailed user data that can be cross-referenced to identify individuals and infer sensitive health information. This violates privacy and data protection principles, exposing users to potential harm despite government assurances of anonymity.

records.title: Apple's AI-Based CSAM Detection Sparks Privacy Backlash
records.description: Apple's rollout of AI-driven systems to detect child sexual abuse material (CSAM) on user devices and iCloud has triggered significant backlash from privacy advocates and rights groups. Critics warn the technology could enable privacy violations, wrongful accusations, and government misuse, despite Apple's assurances of privacy protections.

records.title: AI Gunshot Detection System Leads to Wrongful Imprisonment in Chicago
records.description: The AI-powered ShotSpotter system, used by police to detect gunshots, produced unreliable evidence that led to the wrongful arrest and nearly year-long imprisonment of Michael Williams in Chicago. The system's inaccuracies and potential for bias have raised concerns about its use in law enforcement and its impact on civil rights.

records.title: Women Targeted by AI-Enabled Pegasus Spyware Face Harassment and Blackmail
records.description: Governments in India, the Middle East, and North Africa have used the AI-powered Pegasus spyware, developed by Israel's NSO Group, to surveil women. This has led to widespread harassment, blackmail, and privacy violations, with victims facing threats and self-censorship due to fear of being monitored.

records.title: AI-Driven Price Discrimination Harms Chinese Consumers
records.description: Chinese consumers have experienced widespread harm from AI-driven price discrimination, where big data and algorithmic systems charge different prices to users based on personal data. This practice, known as "big data price gouging," has led to unfair economic treatment and privacy concerns, prompting legislative and regulatory responses in China.

records.title: Apple's AI-Driven Political Censorship Extends to Hong Kong and Taiwan
records.description: Apple used an AI-powered keyword filtering system, originally designed for political censorship in China, to restrict political speech in its engraving services in Hong Kong and Taiwan. This overreaching censorship, not legally required in these regions, led to violations of users' freedom of expression and human rights.

records.title: US Senators Urge Investigation into Tesla Autopilot and FSD After Accidents
records.description: US Senators Edward Markey and Richard Blumenthal have called on the Federal Trade Commission to investigate Tesla's Autopilot and Full Self-Driving (FSD) AI systems, citing misleading marketing and multiple accidents, including injuries and a fatality. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration is also formally investigating Tesla's AI-driven systems.

records.title: Google Whistleblower Reveals AI Algorithm Manipulation to Target Trump
records.description: Google whistleblower Zach Vorhies alleges that the company deliberately rewrote its AI-driven news algorithms to prioritize negative stories about President Donald Trump and suppress positive or neutral coverage. This manipulation, supported by internal documents, reportedly influenced public information access and political discourse in the United States.

records.title: Taliban's Access to Biometric Databases Endangers Afghans
records.description: After the Taliban seized control of Afghanistan, concerns grew over their access to AI-powered biometric databases and digital identity systems. These technologies, previously used for voting and aid, are now reportedly being used to identify, track, and target vulnerable groups, leading to human rights violations and threats to personal safety.

records.title: NHS Covid App Error Causes Unnecessary Self-Isolation for Thousands in UK
records.description: A malfunction in the NHS Covid-19 app in the UK caused tens of thousands of people to be wrongly told to self-isolate. The app's algorithm used a five-day lookback period for contact tracing instead of the official two days, leading to widespread unnecessary quarantines before the error was corrected.

records.title: Taliban Seizes U.S. Military Biometric Devices, Endangering Afghan Allies
records.description: During their offensive, the Taliban seized U.S. military biometric devices (HIIDE) containing sensitive AI-processed data such as iris scans, fingerprints, and personal information. This breach poses a direct threat to Afghans who assisted coalition forces, as the data could be used for identification and reprisals.

records.title: Woman Uses Alexa and Smart Devices to Harass Ex-Partner and New Girlfriend
records.description: Philippa Copleston-Warren remotely accessed her ex-boyfriend's Alexa and CCTV cameras in Lincolnshire, UK, to harass his new girlfriend, control smart devices, and issue threats. She also posted a nude photo of her ex online and sent derogatory messages, causing significant emotional distress and privacy violations through misuse of AI-enabled systems.

records.title: Facial Recognition Failure Leads to Fraudulent Loan, Court Rules Victim Not Liable
records.description: A woman in Guangzhou, China, was fraudulently issued a loan after her lost ID was used with facial recognition at a bank. The bank's AI-based identity verification failed to prevent the fraud. The court ruled the victim was not liable, citing inadequate verification by the bank's AI system.

records.title: Self-Driving Tesla Crashes in UK School Car Park, Injuring Seven
records.description: A Tesla Model 3, reportedly operating in self-driving or Autopilot mode, crashed into a school car park in Ardingly, southern England, injuring six children and one adult. One child was critically injured and airlifted to hospital. Authorities are investigating the involvement of Tesla's AI-driven Autopilot system.

records.title: US Investigates Tesla Autopilot After Multiple Crashes Involving Emergency Vehicles
records.description: US authorities have launched a formal investigation into Tesla's Autopilot AI system after 11 crashes since 2018, including one fatality and 17 injuries, where Teslas failed to detect parked emergency vehicles. The probe covers Models Y, X, S, and 3 from 2014 onward and highlights concerns over the AI's safety limitations.

records.title: US Investigates Tesla Autopilot After Crashes Involving Emergency Vehicles
records.description: The US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) launched an investigation into Tesla's AI-based Autopilot system after multiple accidents where the system failed to detect parked emergency vehicles, resulting in injuries and at least 10 deaths. The probe covers 765,000 vehicles sold since 2014 in the US.

records.title: Rubika AI System Creates Unauthorized Accounts and Copies User Content
records.description: The Iranian app Rubika, using automated systems, created unauthorized accounts for public figures and copied their Instagram content without consent, leading to identity forgery and privacy violations. Users discovered fake profiles with their data, sparking public outrage and regulatory intervention over breaches of personal rights and data protection laws.

records.title: AI-Enabled Drones Cause Civilian Harm in Armed Conflicts
records.description: AI-powered drones have been used in military conflicts in the Caucasus and Ethiopia, resulting in casualties and destruction. In the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict, autonomous kamikaze drones caused deaths and property damage. In Ethiopia, armed drones targeted both combatants and civilians during the Tigray war, raising concerns over AI-driven warfare.

records.title: Global Human Rights Violations Linked to Pegasus AI Spyware
records.description: The Pegasus spyware, developed by Israel's NSO Group, uses advanced AI techniques to covertly monitor individuals by exploiting device vulnerabilities. Its deployment by governments worldwide has led to severe human rights violations, including surveillance, harassment, and intimidation of journalists, activists, and political opponents, prompting international calls for a moratorium and regulatory oversight.

records.title: Houthi Forces Shoot Down US AI-Enabled Drone in Marib, Yemen
records.description: Houthi forces in Yemen announced the downing of a US-made Scan Eagle AI-enabled reconnaissance drone over Marib province. The drone, used for autonomous surveillance and target identification, was shot down during ongoing military conflict, highlighting the direct involvement and vulnerability of AI systems in active warfare.

records.title: Spanish Journalist Targeted by Pegasus Spyware Triggers Legal Investigation
records.description: Spanish journalist Ignacio Cembrero was allegedly targeted by the AI-enabled Pegasus spyware, leading to a legal investigation by Madrid's prosecutor. Cembrero submitted his phone for forensic analysis after learning it was among thousands globally surveilled, raising concerns over privacy violations and unauthorized surveillance of journalists and activists.

records.title: UN Experts Call for Moratorium on AI-Enabled Pegasus Spyware After Human Rights Violations
records.description: UN experts have called for a global moratorium on the sale of AI-enabled surveillance technologies like Pegasus, developed by Israel's NSO Group, after revelations that it was used to spy on hundreds of journalists, politicians, activists, and business leaders, leading to serious human rights violations including breaches of privacy and freedom of expression.

records.title: UN Experts Call for Moratorium on AI-Enabled Surveillance Technology After Human Rights Abuses
records.description: UN human rights experts have called for a global moratorium on the sale and transfer of AI-enabled surveillance technologies, such as Pegasus spyware, following revelations of their use to monitor, intimidate, and silence journalists, activists, and political opponents, resulting in widespread human rights violations.

records.title: FacePlay AI App Causes Financial Losses and Privacy Risks for Vietnamese Users
records.description: The AI-powered FacePlay app, developed by BigHead Bros in China, became popular in Vietnam for generating face-swapped videos. However, users experienced unauthorized charges due to misleading subscriptions and faced privacy risks from excessive personal data collection, including unnecessary access to contacts and location, leading to financial and data security harms.

records.title: Twitch AI Moderation Failure Enables Hate Raids and Harassment
records.description: Twitch's AI-powered moderation filters failed to detect and prevent hate speech and racist harassment, leading to harm against marginalized streamers. Following widespread complaints and the #TwitchDoBetter campaign, Twitch identified a vulnerability in its AI system and deployed updates to improve detection and user safety.

records.title: Tests Reveal Major Flaws in Driver-Assist AI Systems Across Automakers
records.description: A Car and Driver study found that advanced driver-assist systems from 17 major automakers, including Tesla, can be easily tricked into operating without a driver present. These AI-based systems failed to reliably detect driver absence or inattention, posing significant safety risks on public roads.

records.title: Fatal Crash Involving NIO ES8's Assisted Driving System in China
records.description: Chinese entrepreneur Lin Wenqin died in a traffic accident while driving a NIO ES8 with the Navigate on Pilot (NOP) assisted driving system active on a Fujian highway. The incident has raised concerns about the safety of AI-assisted driving features, with investigations ongoing and NIO stating the system is not fully autonomous.

records.title: UN Experts Call for Suspension of Pegasus Spyware Sales After Human Rights Violations
records.description: The Israeli-developed Pegasus spyware, created by NSO Group, was used by various governments to surveil activists, journalists, and politicians, violating their human rights. UN experts condemned the unregulated use of such AI surveillance technology and urged a global suspension of its sale and transfer until robust regulatory frameworks are established.

records.title: Instagram AI Wrongfully Censors Almodóvar Film Poster
records.description: Instagram's AI content moderation algorithm mistakenly removed the poster for Pedro Almodóvar's film "Madres paralelas," designed by Javier Jaén, labeling it as erotic content. The removal sparked public backlash over artistic censorship. After criticism, Facebook reversed the decision, citing the image's clear artistic context.

records.title: Deployment of AI-Powered Robotic Police in Medellín
records.description: The city of Medellín, Colombia, has deployed 'Robocop,' an AI-powered robotic police unit equipped with facial and license plate recognition, real-time monitoring, and predictive analytics to reduce crime. The system has contributed to significant reductions in theft and homicide, raising both public safety benefits and concerns about privacy and surveillance.

records.title: Poly Network DeFi Platform Hacked, $600 Million in Cryptocurrency Stolen
records.description: Poly Network, a decentralized finance (DeFi) platform enabling cross-blockchain transactions, suffered a major security breach. Hackers exploited vulnerabilities in its automated smart contract system, stealing over $600 million in digital assets. This incident is considered the largest DeFi hack to date, causing significant financial harm to users.

records.title: AI Deepfake Tool Generates Non-Consensual Nude Images, Causing Widespread Harm
records.description: A website using AI-powered deepfake technology has created and distributed realistic non-consensual nude images of thousands of women, leading to significant privacy violations, reputational harm, and mental distress. The tool has attracted millions of users, highlighting the dangers of AI misuse in generating synthetic, harmful content.

records.title: Twitter Photo-Cropping AI Found to Exhibit Racial, Age, and Gender Bias
records.description: Twitter's photo-cropping AI algorithm was found to favor young, slim, light-skinned, and stereotypically feminine faces, while discriminating against older individuals, people of color, and non-English scripts. After user complaints and a public contest, Twitter disabled the system and acknowledged the algorithmic bias.

records.title: NASA Perseverance Rover Fails to Collect Mars Rock Sample Due to AI System Malfunction
records.description: NASA's Perseverance rover, which uses AI for autonomous sample collection on Mars, failed to collect its first rock sample despite all mechanisms appearing to function correctly. The sample tube was found empty, likely due to unexpected rock properties, causing a setback to the mission's scientific objectives.

records.title: NYPD Secretly Spends $159 Million on AI Surveillance, Leading to Rights Violations
records.description: The NYPD secretly spent at least $159 million since 2007 on AI-powered surveillance tools, including facial recognition and predictive policing software, without public oversight. Civil rights groups revealed these purchases led to privacy violations, wrongful arrests, and disproportionate harm to marginalized communities in New York City.

records.title: Telus Health's Babylon App Violates Alberta Privacy Laws with AI Facial Recognition
records.description: Alberta's privacy commissioner found that Telus Health's Babylon app violated provincial privacy laws by using AI-based facial recognition for identity verification without proper consent and by collecting excessive personal data. Despite recommendations, Telus has not fully addressed these privacy concerns, leading to ongoing legal and public scrutiny.

records.title: Pegasus Spyware Used for Unlawful Surveillance in Mexico and Globally
records.description: The AI-enabled Pegasus spyware, developed by NSO Group, was acquired and deployed by the Mexican government and other states to conduct unauthorized surveillance on thousands, including journalists, activists, and political figures. This use of AI technology resulted in significant violations of privacy and human rights.

records.title: Journalists File Complaints Over Pegasus AI Spyware Surveillance
records.description: Seventeen journalists from seven countries, including five from Mexico, filed complaints with Reporters Without Borders against NSO Group, creator of the AI-enabled Pegasus spyware. The journalists allege they were surveilled by their governments using Pegasus, violating their privacy and human rights. The case has been brought before the UN and French authorities.

records.title: International Bodies Demand Accountability for Pegasus Spyware Abuse in Mexico
records.description: International organizations, including the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights and the UN Human Rights Office in Mexico, have called for a thorough investigation into the misuse of the AI-enabled Pegasus spyware. The software was used to surveil journalists, activists, and opposition figures, violating privacy and freedom of expression in Mexico.

records.title: SEC Shuts Down DeFi Platform for $30 Million Fraud via Smart Contracts
records.description: The U.S. SEC charged Blockchain Credit Partners and its Florida-based founders for defrauding investors of over $30 million using smart contracts and DeFi technology. The company sold unregistered securities and misled investors about returns. Legal action led to restitution and penalties, highlighting AI-driven financial harm.

records.title: Russian Company Xsolla Fires 150 Employees Based on AI Productivity Analysis
records.description: Russian gaming payment company Xsolla dismissed 150 employees after an AI system analyzed their digital activity (Jira, Gmail, chats, etc.) and labeled them as unproductive. The AI-driven decision, lacking human oversight, led to mass layoffs and raised concerns about labor rights and algorithmic fairness.

records.title: AI Surveillance and Privacy Concerns: Pegasus Spyware and Apple's Child Safety Features
records.description: AI-powered Pegasus spyware, sold by Israeli firm NSO Group, enabled covert surveillance of mobile users in 50 countries, breaching privacy and data security. Separately, Apple's AI-based child safety features for iCloud photos sparked global criticism over potential privacy violations and government misuse, with thousands of organizations and experts urging Apple to abandon the system.

records.title: Teenager's Suicide Linked to Harmful Comments Enabled by TikTok's AI Moderation Failures in Brazil
records.description: A 16-year-old in Brazil died by suicide after a TikTok video he posted went viral and attracted homophobic and hateful comments. The platform's AI-driven content recommendation and insufficient moderation allowed harmful content to proliferate, contributing to the teenager's mental health decline and death.

records.title: AI-Generated Fake Accounts Used in Pro-China Disinformation Campaigns Removed by Social Media Platforms
records.description: Over 350 fake social media accounts, many using AI-generated profile images, were discovered spreading pro-China propaganda and disinformation, including denial of human rights abuses and attacks on dissidents. Platforms like Facebook, Twitter, and YouTube removed these accounts after a report by the Centre for Information Resilience exposed the coordinated campaign.

records.title: Journalists File Complaints Over Pegasus AI Spyware Surveillance
records.description: Seventeen journalists from seven countries, supported by Reporters Without Borders (RSF), have filed complaints against NSO Group, alleging unauthorized surveillance using the AI-powered Pegasus spyware. The journalists claim violations of privacy and human rights, prompting legal action in France and appeals to the United Nations.

records.title: Pegasus Spyware Used for Global Surveillance of Journalists and Activists
records.description: The AI-powered Pegasus spyware, developed by Israel's NSO Group, was used by various governments to covertly surveil journalists, activists, and political figures across multiple countries. This led to significant privacy violations and human rights breaches, prompting legal complaints and international condemnation, including cases filed in France and appeals to the UN.

records.title: Pegasus Spyware Targets Indian Supreme Court Officials and Lawyers
records.description: Israeli AI-enabled Pegasus spyware was used to target phone numbers of former Supreme Court judge Arun Mishra, two Supreme Court registrars, and lawyers involved in high-profile cases in India. This unauthorized surveillance constitutes a breach of privacy and legal rights, highlighting misuse of AI surveillance tools against judicial and legal professionals.

records.title: AI-Driven Social Credit Systems Emerge in the US, Raising Rights Concerns
records.description: Major US tech companies are reportedly deploying AI-enabled surveillance and content moderation systems that monitor user behavior and restrict access to services based on subjective criteria. These systems have led to account removals and financial restrictions, raising concerns about violations of free speech and human rights.

records.title: British Human Rights Activist's Phone Hacked with Pegasus Spyware Linked to Dubai
records.description: British human rights activist David Haigh's phone was hacked using the AI-powered Pegasus spyware in August 2020, as confirmed by Amnesty International. The attack, allegedly ordered by Dubai due to Haigh's involvement in campaigns supporting Princess Latifa and Princess Haya, resulted in significant privacy violations and human rights concerns.

records.title: Boeing Starliner AI Software Failure Causes Mission Setback
records.description: Boeing's Starliner spacecraft, developed for NASA missions to the ISS, suffered a critical software malfunction in 2019. The AI-driven navigation system caused the capsule to enter the wrong orbit, resulting in mission failure and wasted resources. Recent propulsion system issues have further delayed subsequent test flights.

records.title: Israeli NSO Group's Pegasus Spyware Used for Surveillance and Human Rights Violations
records.description: Israeli authorities investigated NSO Group after reports that its AI-powered Pegasus spyware was used by government clients to surveil journalists, activists, and politicians, including French President Macron. French security services confirmed Pegasus was found on journalists' phones, highlighting significant privacy and human rights violations.

records.title: Deliveroo Italy Fined for Opaque AI Management and Privacy Violations of Riders
records.description: The Italian privacy authority fined Deliveroo Italy €2.5 million for unlawfully processing the personal data of about 8,000 riders. The violations involved non-transparent AI algorithms for order assignment and shift scheduling, excessive data collection, and continuous geolocation, breaching privacy and labor rights laws.

records.title: Xiaomi 11 Smartphone Overheating Causes User Injuries and Device Failures
records.description: Users of Xiaomi 11 smartphones in China report severe overheating, with some experiencing burns and device malfunctions such as WiFi failure. The issue, linked to AI-driven thermal management in the device, has affected thousands, prompting a large user group to seek redress for health and property harm.

records.title: AI-Guided Drone Attack on Japanese-Owned Tanker Causes Fatalities in Arabian Sea
records.description: A Japanese-owned tanker operated by an Israeli company was attacked by AI-guided, self-destructing drones in the Arabian Sea near Oman, resulting in two deaths. The drones, likely using autonomous navigation and targeting, represent a significant escalation in the use of AI-enabled weaponized drones causing direct harm.

records.title: Pegasus Spyware Used by Governments to Target and Harass Female Journalists
records.description: Governments in the Middle East reportedly used NSO Group's AI-powered Pegasus spyware to hack the phones of female journalists and activists, steal private photos, and leak them online to intimidate, harass, and discredit the women. The attacks caused significant psychological, reputational, and human rights harm to the victims.

records.title: Global Pegasus Spyware Scandal Exposes Widespread AI-Driven Surveillance
records.description: The Pegasus spyware, developed by Israel's NSO Group, was used by governments in countries like Mexico, India, Morocco, and Hungary to conduct AI-enabled surveillance on journalists, activists, and political figures. This led to significant violations of privacy and human rights, highlighting the dangers of AI-driven cyber-espionage.

records.title: Critical AI System Vulnerabilities Expose Hospitals and Android Devices to Remote Attacks
records.description: Security researchers revealed major vulnerabilities in Android's Binder and GPU components, enabling remote root access and device control, threatening user privacy and safety. Separately, flaws in Swisslog Healthcare's TransLogic hospital transport system risked ransomware and data breaches, impacting 80% of North American hospitals and endangering patient care.

records.title: Software Malfunction on Russian Nauka Module Disrupts ISS Orientation
records.description: A software malfunction in the Russian Nauka module's automated thruster control system caused unplanned thruster firing, displacing the International Space Station (ISS) by 45 degrees from its intended orientation. The incident disrupted critical infrastructure and delayed operations, though the crew remained safe and control was eventually restored.

records.title: AI Algorithms Amplify Vaccine Misinformation, Undermining Public Health
records.description: AI-powered recommendation algorithms on social media platforms have amplified COVID-19 vaccine misinformation, leading to reduced vaccination rates and increased public health risks in the United States. The engagement-driven design of these AI systems has enabled organized misinformation campaigns to exploit platform weaknesses, causing tangible harm to communities.

records.title: Russian Military Deploys AI-Powered Combat Robots in Active Operations
records.description: The Russian military has actively deployed AI-powered autonomous combat robots, such as the Uran series, in both training exercises and real combat, including in Syria. These systems have independently engaged and destroyed enemy targets, directly causing harm and fatalities through autonomous decision-making in lethal military operations.

records.title: Calls for Supreme Court Action on Pegasus AI Spyware Surveillance in India
records.description: Over 500 individuals and groups have urged India's Supreme Court to intervene in the alleged misuse of Pegasus AI-enabled spyware for unauthorized surveillance of journalists, activists, and vulnerable groups. They demand a moratorium on its use and accountability from the government and NSO, citing human rights and privacy violations.

records.title: Tesla Settles Lawsuit Over AI-Driven Battery Throttling
records.description: Tesla agreed to pay $1.5 million to settle claims after a 2019 software update—managing battery charge and thermal settings via AI—reduced range and charging speed in 1,743 Model S vehicles. The update caused measurable harm to owners, prompting a class action lawsuit and subsequent compensation.

records.title: Israeli Government Investigates NSO Group Over Pegasus Spyware Abuse
records.description: The Israeli government has launched an investigation into NSO Group after revelations that its AI-enabled Pegasus spyware was used by governments to conduct unauthorized surveillance on politicians, journalists, activists, and public figures worldwide, leading to significant privacy and human rights violations.

records.title: Mexican Prosecutors Fail to Uninstall Pegasus Spyware Amid Ongoing Investigation
records.description: The Mexican Attorney General's Office (FGR) has not confirmed the uninstallation of Pegasus, an AI-powered spyware used to surveil activists and journalists, despite demands from the national transparency institute (INAI). The continued presence of Pegasus raises concerns over ongoing privacy violations and human rights abuses in Mexico.

records.title: Global Human Rights Violations Linked to Pegasus AI Spyware

He demanded a Supreme Court-monitored investigation and a government white paper on the matter.

records.title: Pegasus Spyware Targets World Leaders in Major Surveillance Scandal
records.description: The AI-powered Pegasus spyware, developed by Israel's NSO Group, was used to target high-profile individuals including King Mohammed VI of Morocco, French President Emmanuel Macron, and former Belgian Prime Minister Charles Michel. records.title: Paris Prosecutor Investigates Pegasus AI Spyware Use Against Journalists

records.title: Pegasus AI Spyware Used for Surveillance of Mexican President's Family

records.title: Pegasus Spyware Used for Global Surveillance of Journalists, Activists, and Leaders via iOS Zero-Click Exploits
records.description: The Israeli NSO Group's AI-enabled spyware Pegasus exploited zero-click vulnerabilities in iOS devices, enabling unauthorized surveillance of journalists, activists, and world leaders. records.title: Moroccan Authorities Use Pegasus AI Spyware for Mass Surveillance of Algerian Officials and Civilians

This AI system flaw poses a risk of fraudulent health passes. The Health Ministry plans to address the issue in the next update.

records.title: AI Proctoring Software in German Universities Breaches Privacy Laws
records.description: AI-based proctoring software used during online university exams in Baden-Württemberg, Germany, was found to violate privacy and data protection laws. The state data protection commissioner initiated legal action, citing excessive surveillance of students through tools that monitor behavior, video, and audio, infringing on fundamental rights during the COVID-19 lockdown.

records.title: Rwandan Authorities Use Pegasus Spyware to Target Dissidents and Activists
records.description: Rwandan authorities used the Israeli AI-powered Pegasus spyware to surveil over 3,500 individuals, including Carine Kanimba, daughter of government critic Paul Rusesabagina. Forensic analysis confirmed her phone was repeatedly compromised, violating her privacy and human rights. The incident highlights the malicious use of AI surveillance tools against activists and political opponents.

records.title: Pegasus Spyware Exploits iPhone Zero-Click Vulnerabilities for Targeted Surveillance
records.description: The AI-powered Pegasus spyware, developed by Israel's NSO Group, exploited zero-click vulnerabilities in iPhones to conduct targeted surveillance on journalists, activists, and others. records.title: NHS Covid App Notifications Cause Widespread Holiday Disruption and Financial Loss
records.description: A surge in self-isolation notifications from the NHS Covid app in the UK has led to millions of holiday cancellations and financial losses for travelers. Many affected individuals face difficulties obtaining refunds or rebooking without extra charges, as most travel companies and airlines have restrictive policies regarding Covid-related disruptions.

records.title: Recall of 4,000 Xiaomi Drones Due to AI Flight Control Software Risk
records.description: Beijing FIMI Technology is recalling 4,000 Xiaomi Mi 4K drones manufactured in February 2017 due to a flight control software malfunction. Improper parameter settings in the AI-driven system could cause drones to lose power and crash at high altitudes, posing injury risks. A software update is being provided to address the hazard.

records.title: AI-Driven Facebook Algorithms Amplify COVID-19 Misinformation, Leading to Public Health Harm
records.description: AI-powered content moderation and recommendation systems on Facebook have failed to adequately curb COVID-19 vaccine misinformation, contributing to increased vaccine hesitancy and deaths among unvaccinated populations in the US. The Biden administration criticized Facebook, highlighting the AI systems' role in amplifying harmful misinformation.

records.title: Robot Collision Causes Fire and Disruption at Ocado's Automated Warehouse in London
records.description: A collision between AI-powered robots at Ocado's automated warehouse in Erith, south-east London, caused a fire that damaged part of the facility and disrupted order fulfillment. No injuries were reported, but the incident led to property damage and operational delays, highlighting risks associated with autonomous warehouse systems.

records.title: Global Cyberattacks Attributed to Chinese State-Backed Hackers Involving AI Techniques
records.description: US and allied governments accused Chinese state-backed hackers of orchestrating large-scale cyberattacks using advanced, likely AI-enabled techniques. These attacks targeted Microsoft Exchange servers and critical infrastructure, resulting in theft of sensitive data, intellectual property, and disruption of government and corporate operations worldwide. Multiple indictments and diplomatic actions followed.

records.title: Google Maps AI Routing Endangers Hikers on Ben Nevis
records.description: Google Maps' AI-based routing algorithms suggested dangerous and potentially fatal hiking routes on Ben Nevis and other Scottish mountains, misleading users into hazardous terrain. Mountaineering organizations reported injuries and raised safety concerns, prompting Google to update its maps to prevent further harm.

records.title: Instagram AI Moderation Failure Allows Racist Abuse of England Footballers
records.description: Instagram's AI-powered content moderation system failed to detect and remove racist comments and emojis targeting England footballers Marcus Rashford, Bukayo Saka, and Jadon Sancho after the Euro 2020 final. The malfunction allowed harmful abuse to persist until Instagram acknowledged and fixed the issue.

records.title: Israeli Spyware Used by Governments to Target Activists and Journalists Globally
records.description: Spyware developed by Israeli company Saito Tech Ltd (Candiru) was sold to governments and used to surveil over 100 politicians, dissidents, journalists, and activists worldwide. The AI-powered software extracted data from devices, activated cameras and microphones, and impersonated victims, leading to significant privacy and human rights violations.

records.title: Vulnerability in Windows Hello Facial Recognition Allows Unauthorized Access
records.description: CyberArk Labs discovered a vulnerability in Microsoft's Windows Hello facial recognition system that allowed attackers to bypass authentication using a custom USB camera and a photo of the victim. Microsoft has since released a patch to address this AI system security flaw, which affected millions of Windows 10 users.

records.title: Black Teen Wrongfully Banned by Facial Recognition at Michigan Skating Rink
records.description: A Black teenager, Lamya Robinson, was wrongly barred from Riverside Arena in Livonia, Michigan after its facial recognition system misidentified her as someone previously banned. The incident, which her family describes as racial profiling, highlights ongoing concerns about AI bias and the harm caused by inaccurate facial recognition technology.

records.title: AI-Powered E-Commerce Algorithms Cause Unfair Pricing and Consumer Rights Violations in China
records.description: Chinese e-commerce platforms' AI-driven personalized recommendation algorithms have led to significant price disparities for identical products based on user profiles, resulting in unfair pricing and restricted consumer choice. This practice, known as "data-driven price discrimination," has triggered consumer complaints, legal action, and regulatory scrutiny for violating fairness and consumer rights.

records.title: Japanese Police Arrest Four in $54M AI-Based Crypto Scam
records.description: Four men in Japan were arrested for orchestrating the Oz Project, a fraudulent cryptocurrency investment scheme that falsely claimed to use AI for high returns. The scam lured over 20,000 investors nationwide, resulting in losses exceeding $54 million. The suspects held seminars and used messaging apps to solicit funds.

records.title: TikTok AI Features Amplify COVID-19 Vaccine Misinformation
records.description: AI-driven features on TikTok, particularly the 'Sounds' function and content recommendation algorithms, enabled the viral spread of COVID-19 vaccine misinformation. Despite some moderation efforts, misleading audio clips reached over 20 million views, undermining public health and illustrating the harm caused by AI-enabled content dissemination.

records.title: Cellebrite Spyware Enables Human Rights Abuses in Vietnam and Beyond
records.description: Israeli firm Cellebrite's AI-powered surveillance and data extraction tools have been sold to Vietnam's Public Security Ministry and other repressive regimes, enabling detentions, harassment of opposition figures, and privacy violations, including targeting journalists. Rights groups urge regulators to halt Cellebrite's IPO due to its technology's role in human rights abuses.

records.title: AI Voice Cloning Used in Fraudulent Schemes
records.description: Advances in AI-powered voice cloning technology have enabled cybercriminals to create synthetic voices nearly indistinguishable from real ones. In the US, this technology has been used to impersonate individuals and commit fraud, including a case where a CEO was tricked into transferring $260,000. The misuse highlights significant security risks.

records.title: Fiat-Chrysler Charged in France for AI-Driven Diesel Emissions Fraud
records.description: Fiat-Chrysler has been charged in France for using software in diesel vehicles to manipulate emissions tests, allowing cars to emit pollutants far above legal limits. This AI-driven deception endangered human and animal health, leading to legal action and financial penalties. Other automakers face similar charges.

records.title: Facial Recognition Surveillance Raises Rights Concerns in Chinese City During COVID-19
records.description: Authorities in Ruili, China, deployed facial recognition technology linked to health codes to monitor residents' movements and health status during a COVID-19 outbreak. This AI-driven surveillance has raised significant privacy and human rights concerns, particularly regarding pervasive monitoring and potential targeting of minorities.

records.title: AI-Driven Surge in Antisemitic Content on TikTok
records.description: A University of Haifa study found a 912% increase in antisemitic content on TikTok over the past year. TikTok's AI-driven content recommendation and moderation systems failed to curb the spread of hate speech, amplifying harmful antisemitic posts and usernames, and contributing to community harm.

records.title: Facebook Engineers Fired for Misusing AI-Managed User Data
records.description: Between 2014 and 2015, Facebook fired 52 engineers for abusing their access to AI-managed backend systems to spy on female users, accessing private messages, real-time locations, and personal data. The incident exposed significant privacy violations and highlighted systemic failures in data access controls at Facebook.

records.title: AI-Driven Disinformation Campaign Fuels Protests in Cuba
records.description: A coordinated disinformation campaign targeting Cuba used AI-driven bots, algorithms, and automated accounts to manipulate social media trends and spread misinformation from abroad. This operation, linked to political actors and organizations, contributed to social unrest and protests, demonstrating the harmful impact of AI systems on public opinion and political stability.

records.title: GM Bolt Battery Fires After AI-Managed Recall Repairs
records.description: General Motors warned owners of 2017-2019 Chevrolet Bolts to park outdoors and avoid overnight charging after two vehicles caught fire post-recall repairs. The incidents, in Vermont and New Jersey, highlight failures in the AI-based battery management and diagnostic systems intended to prevent such fires, resulting in property damage and safety risks.

records.title: USPS Uses AI Surveillance to Monitor Social Media and Protests
records.description: The United States Postal Service (USPS), through its Internet Covert Operations Program (iCOP), has used AI tools, including facial recognition and social media monitoring, to surveil individuals and groups involved in protests. This has raised significant concerns about privacy violations and potential breaches of legal rights in the United States.

records.title: Wrongful Arrests Spark Calls for Facial Recognition Regulation in the U.S.
records.description: In Detroit, Michigan, Robert Williams was wrongfully arrested and detained for 30 hours after being misidentified by police facial recognition AI. This incident, highlighted in U.S. congressional hearings, underscores the technology's risks and has intensified calls for federal regulation to prevent further civil rights violations.

records.title: Drone Near Collision with Commercial Aircraft at Helsinki Airport
records.description: A remote-controlled drone operated without authorization in controlled airspace at Helsinki Airport, coming dangerously close to a commercial aircraft during takeoff. Finnish authorities classified the event as a "serious incident," highlighting the direct risk posed by misuse of AI-enabled drone systems to aviation safety.

records.title: Deepfake AI Technology Causes Widespread Harm and Prompts Detection Efforts in China
records.description: Deepfake AI technology in China has led to significant harms, including privacy violations, financial fraud, misinformation, and threats to social and national security. The technology's low barrier to use and high realism have enabled widespread misuse, prompting government and industry to develop AI-based detection platforms to counteract these risks.

records.title: Ctrip Penalized for AI-Driven Price Discrimination Against Loyal Customer
records.description: Ctrip's app used big data analytics to overcharge a loyal customer by displaying inflated hotel prices, violating consumer rights and privacy. A court ordered Ctrip to pay triple compensation and revise its data practices, highlighting the harm caused by AI-driven discriminatory pricing and excessive personal data collection.

records.title: Facebook's AI Moderation Failures Linked to Capitol Attack
records.description: Facebook's AI-driven content moderation failed to prevent escalating threats and harmful posts that contributed to the January 6 Capitol attack. Despite internal warnings, executives did not intervene, highlighting how the platform's AI systems and corporate decisions indirectly enabled real-world violence and public safety risks.

records.title: YouTube's AI Algorithm Amplifies Harmful Content, Study Finds
records.description: A Mozilla Foundation study found that YouTube's AI recommendation algorithm continues to promote harmful content, including misinformation, hate speech, and extremism. Crowdsourced data revealed that 71% of videos users flagged as objectionable were recommended by the algorithm, highlighting ongoing harm to communities despite YouTube's mitigation efforts.

records.title: Apple's AI Emoji Suggestion Stigmatizes People Who Stammer
records.description: Apple's AI-powered emoji suggestion system has been criticized by UK charity STAMMA for recommending a 'woozy face' emoji when users type 'stammering.' The association says this stigmatizes people with speech disorders, causing emotional harm and reinforcing negative stereotypes, with hundreds of complaints from affected users.

records.title: Tesla's Autonomous Driving AI Implicated in Fatal Crash and Safety Failures
records.description: Tesla's autonomous driving AI, including Autopilot and Full Self Driving (FSD), has been linked to fatal accidents, such as the death of Walter Huang, and demonstrated safety failures, including being tricked into operating without a driver. Elon Musk acknowledges the significant technical challenges and delays in achieving safe, fully autonomous vehicles.

records.title: Tencent Uses AI Facial Recognition to Enforce Gaming Curfew on Minors in China
records.description: Tencent has deployed AI-powered facial recognition technology, 'Midnight Patrol,' to enforce government gaming curfews for minors in China. The system verifies users' identities at night, blocking access for those under 18 and raising significant privacy and human rights concerns due to mass biometric data collection and surveillance.

records.title: EU Approves AI Surveillance of Private Messages to Combat Child Abuse
records.description: The European Parliament approved a temporary regulation allowing tech giants like Google, Facebook, and Microsoft to use AI systems to scan private chats and emails for child sexual abuse material. This measure, criticized as mass surveillance, suspends privacy protections for three years, raising significant concerns about violations of fundamental privacy rights.

records.title: Israel Deploys Autonomous AI Drone Swarms in Combat for the First Time
records.description: The Israeli Defense Forces (IDF) became the first military to deploy fully autonomous AI-controlled drone swarms in combat during the May 2021 Gaza conflict. These drones, operating without human intervention after mission launch, identified and attacked targets, resulting in numerous militant deaths and raising significant ethical concerns about autonomous lethal weapons.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot Blamed in Fatal Crash Leading to Lawsuit and Regulatory Scrutiny
records.description: A California family is suing Tesla after their 15-year-old son died in a 2019 crash involving a Model 3 with Autopilot engaged. The lawsuit alleges the AI-driven system failed to prevent the collision, contributing to the fatality. The incident has prompted regulatory investigations into Autopilot's safety.

records.title: Amazon Echo Devices Retain User Data After Factory Reset, Exposing Privacy Risks
records.description: Researchers from Northeastern University found that Amazon Echo smart speakers retain sensitive user data, such as WiFi credentials and location, even after a factory reset. This flaw allows knowledgeable individuals with physical access to extract personal information, exposing users to privacy violations and potential security breaches due to inadequate data protection in the AI-powered devices.

records.title: Glovo's Foodinho Fined for Discriminatory AI Algorithm in Rider Management
records.description: Italian data protection authority fined Foodinho, a Glovo subsidiary, €2.6 million for using AI algorithms in rider management that led to privacy violations, discriminatory work assignments, and breaches of labor rights. The company must revise its algorithmic systems to prevent discrimination and ensure compliance with privacy and labor laws.

records.title: Facial Recognition Apps Expose Users' Private Images to Backend Reviewers
records.description: Multiple reports reveal that some facial recognition apps upload full camera images—not just faces—during verification, exposing users in private or compromising situations to backend human reviewers. This practice has led to widespread privacy violations and public outcry, highlighting inadequate user notification and insufficient privacy safeguards in certain AI-powered systems.

records.title: Google Maps AI Misguides Tourists, Leaving Them Stranded in Mud in Rural India
records.description: A group of tourists from Germany and Uttarakhand were stranded in rural Rajasthan after Google Maps' AI suggested a faster alternative route that led them onto an undeveloped, muddy road. Their car became stuck, forcing them to seek help from a nearby village, highlighting risks of over-reliance on AI navigation.

records.title: Vietnam Warns of AI 'Robot' Investment Scam Causing Financial Harm
records.description: Vietnam's Ministry of Industry and Trade has warned the public about fraudulent investment schemes using so-called 'Robot AI' systems, which claim to autonomously generate income through affiliate marketing and cryptocurrency trading. These unlicensed multi-level marketing operations have led to financial losses for investors, prompting official warnings to avoid participation.

records.title: UN Criticizes AI-Driven Social Media Algorithms for Spreading COVID-19 Misinformation
