records.description: UN Special Rapporteur Irene Khan denounced social media platforms for using AI algorithms and targeted advertising to promote conspiracy theories and extremist content during the pandemic. These practices contributed to widespread misinformation, undermining human rights such as freedom of expression and access to accurate information.

records.title: Russia Begins Production and Export of AI-Enabled Armed Drones
records.description: Russia has started serial production and plans to export AI-powered military drones, such as the Orion, capable of autonomous target identification and attack. These drones, already used in combat, raise concerns about increased harm and risks as they are deployed and sold to other countries.

records.title: AI Cameras Reduce Mask Non-Compliance on Passenger Vehicles in Vietnam
records.description: Vietnamese transport companies deployed AI-powered camera systems to detect and alert for improper mask use on passenger vehicles. Over 500 vehicles from 23 companies adopted the technology, resulting in a significant drop in non-compliance rates from 23% to 9%, thereby reducing public health risks related to COVID-19.

records.title: Google Assistant's Unintended Recordings Spark Global Privacy Lawsuits
records.description: Google admitted that its AI-powered Assistant sometimes records and stores user conversations without explicit activation, and employees listen to some recordings for system improvement. These unauthorized recordings have led to privacy lawsuits and concerns over violations of user rights and data protection laws.

records.title: Global Human Rights Violations Linked to NSO Group's Pegasus Spyware
records.description: Researchers and human rights organizations have mapped the global use of NSO Group's AI-powered Pegasus spyware, revealing its deployment by state actors to target journalists, activists, and civil society figures. The spyware's use has led to widespread human rights violations, including surveillance, intimidation, harassment, arrests, and physical violence.

records.title: US Federal Agencies' Unregulated Use of Facial Recognition AI Leads to Civil Rights Violations
records.description: Multiple US federal agencies have used facial recognition AI systems with little oversight, resulting in privacy violations, wrongful arrests, and potential suppression of constitutional rights. Watchdog reports highlight untracked use, lack of accountability, and accuracy concerns, directly causing harm to individuals and communities.

records.title: Weaponized Drones Used in Terror Attack on Indian Military Base Raises Global AI Security Concerns
records.description: India reported to the UN that weaponized drones, likely equipped with AI or autonomous systems, were used in a terror attack on an Air Force station in Jammu and in attempted attacks on other military sites. The incidents highlight the growing threat of AI-enabled drones being misused for terrorism.

records.title: TikTok's AI Fails to Prevent Spread of Suicide-Related Content
records.description: Research found TikTok's AI-driven content moderation failed to prevent the widespread dissemination of suicide-related videos, with over 1,700 such posts and more than 580,000 user engagements. Activists and experts criticized TikTok for inadequate AI moderation, prompting regulatory complaints and calls for stronger action to protect vulnerable users.

records.title: Tesla Recalls 285,000 Cars in China Over AI Driving Software Malfunction Leading to Collisions
records.description: Tesla is recalling over 285,000 Model 3 and Y vehicles in China after authorities found that the AI-assisted driving software could be accidentally activated, causing sudden acceleration and collisions, including fatal ones. The recall follows multiple incidents and regulatory investigations into the software's safety risks.

records.title: Google Algorithm Wrongly Labels Engineer as Serial Killer
records.description: Google's AI-powered Knowledge Panel and search algorithms mistakenly displayed the photo of Swiss engineer Hristo Georgiev alongside information about a Bulgarian serial killer with the same name. This error caused significant reputational harm to the innocent engineer before Google corrected the issue.

records.title: Autopilot Software Flaw Causes Fatal Canadian Military Helicopter Crash
records.description: A Canadian military investigation found that a software flaw in the Cyclone helicopter's autopilot system caused it to take control unexpectedly during a maneuver, leading to a crash that killed six personnel in April 2020. Pilots lacked training and cockpit warnings for this scenario, highlighting critical AI system design failures.

records.title: Amazon's AI System Wrongfully Fires Delivery Drivers Without Human Oversight
records.description: Amazon's automated AI-driven system evaluates and fires contract delivery drivers, often without human oversight. Several drivers, including Stephen Normandin, were wrongfully terminated due to factors beyond their control. The rigid algorithmic process led to job loss and economic harm, highlighting risks of automated HR decisions and lack of recourse for affected workers.

records.title: Russian Police Deploy AI Surveillance System for Facial and Silhouette Recognition
records.description: Russian police have implemented an AI-powered surveillance system developed by NtechLab that recognizes faces, human silhouettes, and vehicles, tracking individuals by attributes like gait and clothing. Deployed in five regions, the system raises significant privacy and human rights concerns due to its advanced identification and monitoring capabilities.

records.title: Dutch Groups Sue TikTok for AI-Driven Child Data Privacy Violations
records.description: Dutch consumer groups Consumentenbond and Take Back Your Privacy have filed a €1.5 billion claim against TikTok, alleging its AI systems unlawfully collect and exploit personal data from over a million Dutch children without proper consent, violating privacy laws and children's rights for targeted advertising profits.

records.title: AI-Enabled Drones Cause Harm in Warfare and Public Events
records.description: AI-powered military drones have caused civilian deaths and infrastructure disruption in the Middle East, with both state and non-state actors deploying them in conflict zones. Separately, a malfunction in an AI-controlled drone light show in Shanghai led to drones falling and injuring spectators, highlighting risks from both military and civilian AI drone systems.

records.title: Inter-Homines AI System Deployed to Prevent COVID-19 Crowding Risks
records.description: Inter-Homines, an Italian AI system developed by AlmageLab, GoatAl, and ForteSecurGroup, is being used in hospitals and public spaces to monitor crowd density and social distancing. The system issues alerts when gatherings exceed safe limits, aiming to reduce COVID-19 transmission and enhance public safety without compromising privacy.

records.title: Epic Sepsis Prediction Algorithm Fails to Accurately Detect Deadly Infections in Hospitals
records.description: A widely used AI algorithm by Epic Systems, designed to predict sepsis in hospital patients, was found to miss most cases and generate frequent false alarms, according to a University of Michigan study. The tool’s poor accuracy risks delayed treatment, unnecessary interventions, and contributes to clinician alert fatigue, potentially harming patient care.

records.title: Apple AirTag Misused for Stalking Spurs Security Updates and Android App
records.description: Apple's AirTag, designed for item tracking, has been exploited for malicious stalking due to security loopholes, especially affecting Android users who lack alerts. In response, Apple updated AirTag firmware to shorten alert times and is developing an Android app to help detect unauthorized tracking, addressing privacy and safety concerns.

records.title: ByteDance Intern Accidentally Deletes Key Machine Learning Models, Disrupting Operations
records.description: A ByteDance intern accidentally deleted all sub-GB machine learning models, including TensorFlow Lite models, by removing a parent directory with 'skip trash' enabled, making recovery impossible. The incident caused significant operational disruption, required a large-scale response, and delayed AI model deployment, though most affected data was offline and impact was limited.

records.title: Civil Rights Groups Demand Ban on Amazon's AI Worker Surveillance Amid Injury Crisis
records.description: Over 35 civil rights and labor groups urged lawmakers to ban Amazon's AI-driven worker surveillance systems, citing links to high injury rates and abusive conditions in warehouses. The AI monitors productivity and enforces work pace, contributing to thousands of serious worker injuries, especially during high-demand events like Prime Day.

records.title: AI-Based GeNose COVID-19 Test Criticized for Inaccuracy and Public Health Risks
records.description: Experts and users raised concerns about the AI-powered GeNose COVID-19 test's low accuracy, with reports of false negatives compared to PCR tests. Its widespread use in public settings may have contributed to undetected infections and increased transmission, highlighting risks of relying on unvalidated AI health screening tools.

records.title: Chinese AI Input Method Apps Removed for Illegal Data Collection
records.description: Major Chinese AI-powered input method apps, including iFlytek, Sogou, and QQ Input Method, were removed from app stores after regulators found them illegally collecting and misusing user data for targeted advertising. The incident led to public outcry, regulatory scrutiny, and a sharp drop in iFlytek's stock price.

records.title: AI-Powered Surveillance Cameras Violate Privacy During COVID-19 Response
records.description: During the COVID-19 pandemic, many US buildings deployed AI-driven thermal cameras with facial recognition to monitor visitors' health and movements without consent. This widespread use of AI surveillance technology led to significant privacy violations and raised concerns about ongoing infringements of constitutional and human rights.

records.title: Amazon Japan's AI Fails to Block Defamatory and Obscene Listings
records.description: Amazon Japan's AI-based monitoring system failed to prevent the sale of numerous illicit products featuring AI-generated obscene and defamatory images of female celebrities. The incident exposes shortcomings in Amazon's AI moderation, leading to reputational harm and potential legal violations, prompting government scrutiny and calls for improved content management.

records.title: Canon's AI Smile Recognition System Forces Employees to Smile for Workplace Access
records.description: Canon's Chinese offices implemented an AI-powered facial recognition system that requires employees to smile to gain entry or access workplace facilities. The system, intended to promote positivity, has raised concerns over emotional manipulation, privacy, and labor rights violations due to its compulsory enforcement of emotional expression.

records.title: Snapchat Removes Speed Filter After AI-Driven Feature Linked to Fatal Crashes
records.description: Snapchat has permanently removed its AI-powered speed filter after it was linked to multiple fatal and near-fatal car crashes. The feature, which displayed users' real-time speed, encouraged reckless driving, especially among teens, leading to lawsuits and widespread criticism over its role in promoting dangerous behavior.

records.title: US Probes Tesla Autopilot After Fatal Crashes Linked to AI System
records.description: The US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration is investigating 30 Tesla crashes since 2016, with 10 resulting in fatalities, to determine the role of Tesla's Autopilot AI system. The probes focus on whether Autopilot malfunctions or misuse contributed to these incidents, highlighting concerns over AI-driven vehicle safety.

records.title: Facial Recognition AI Blocks Unemployment Benefits for Eligible Applicants
records.description: Facial recognition software by ID.me, used in over 20 US states to verify unemployment claims, has inconsistently identified applicants, leading to wrongful denials and delays in benefits. Many affected individuals struggle to resolve issues, while the company attributes failures to user error, despite mounting complaints and evidence of harm.

records.title: Indian IT Sector to Cut 3 Million Jobs Due to AI Automation by 2022: BOA Report
records.description: A Bank of America report warns that major Indian IT companies like TCS, Infosys, and Wipro will cut up to 3 million jobs by 2022 due to rapid adoption of AI-driven automation, especially Robotic Process Automation (RPA), resulting in significant economic harm to workers but saving companies $100 billion annually.

records.title: Instagram AI Filters Criticized for Racial Bias Against Black Users
records.description: João Luiz Pedrosa, ex-BBB21 participant, publicly criticized Instagram's AI-powered filters for distorting the facial features and skin tones of Black users, highlighting a lack of inclusivity and racial bias in the platform's design. The incident underscores harm to identity and representation caused by biased AI image processing.

records.title: TikTok's AI Moderation and Data Practices Lead to Censorship and Privacy Violations
records.description: TikTok's AI-driven content moderation has reportedly censored Jewish creators, including those countering antisemitism, raising concerns of discrimination and rights violations. Separately, TikTok faces a $1.7 billion Dutch lawsuit for allegedly using AI to collect children's personal data without proper consent, violating EU privacy laws and endangering minors' rights.

records.title: iFlytek AI Input Method App Removed for Privacy Violations, Causing Stock Crash
records.description: iFlytek's AI-powered input method app was removed from major app stores after failing to comply with personal information protection regulations, specifically regarding user consent for cloud input features. The incident led to a sharp drop in iFlytek's stock price and internal disciplinary actions. The company has since completed rectification.

records.title: TikTok Users Distressed by Unremovable AI Beauty Filter Altering Faces Without Consent
records.description: TikTok users reported that an AI-powered beauty filter was automatically altering their facial features—such as slimming jaws and smoothing skin—without their consent and with no option to disable it. The incident caused psychological distress and raised concerns about user rights and control over personal image, prompting TikTok to remove the filter.

records.title: AI Infrastructure Exploited for Cryptomining via Kubeflow and TensorFlow
records.description: Hackers targeted Kubernetes clusters running Kubeflow, an AI/ML framework, by deploying malicious TensorFlow containers to mine cryptocurrency. The attackers exploited legitimate AI system infrastructure, causing unauthorized resource use and operational disruption. Microsoft researchers identified the ongoing campaign, which leverages official TensorFlow images for illicit mining activities.

records.title: RCMP's Use of Clearview AI Facial Recognition Violated Canadian Privacy Law
records.description: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) unlawfully used Clearview AI's facial recognition system, which scraped billions of images without consent, to identify individuals. Canada's privacy commissioner found this violated the Privacy Act, constituting mass surveillance and serious breaches of Canadians' privacy rights. The RCMP was ordered to improve privacy compliance.

records.title: Google Alters Search Algorithm to Combat Defamation and Extortion Sites
records.description: Google's AI-driven search algorithm previously surfaced defamatory and unverified content about individuals, enabling extortion and reputational harm. In response, Google is changing its algorithm to suppress such sites in search results and has introduced a system to protect known victims, aiming to reduce these AI-enabled harms.

records.title: TikTok AI Moderation Fails to Block Graphic Beheading Video
records.description: TikTok's AI content moderation system failed to detect and block a graphic beheading video disguised as a dance clip, allowing it to go viral and exposing users, including minors, to traumatic content. The incident led to public outrage and calls for improved AI safeguards on the platform.

records.title: Oxford AI Tool Predicts COVID-19 Mortality Risk from Medical Imaging
records.description: Researchers at Oxford University developed an AI system that analyzes CT scans to detect vascular inflammation in COVID-19 patients, predicting mortality risk up to eight times higher for severe cases. The tool enables faster, personalized anti-inflammatory treatment decisions, potentially reducing death rates and improving patient outcomes.

records.title: "Facebook Is Executing Us": Campaign Protests AI-Driven Censorship of Arabic Content
records.description: Arab activists launched the "Facebook Is Executing Us" campaign to protest Facebook's AI-powered content moderation, which has led to widespread removal and suppression of peaceful Arabic and pro-Palestinian posts. The campaign highlights thousands of account suspensions and content deletions, alleging algorithmic bias and violations of freedom of expression.

records.title: Google Fires AI Ethics Researcher After Warning of Discrimination Risks
records.description: Google fired AI ethics researcher Timnit Gebru after she raised concerns that large language models could perpetuate discrimination against marginalized groups. Gebru was pressured to retract a critical research paper, highlighting organizational suppression of ethical concerns and labor rights violations linked to AI system development.

records.title: Global Coalition Demands Ban on Harmful Biometric Surveillance AI
records.description: Over 175 civil society groups worldwide have called for a global ban on facial recognition and biometric surveillance technologies, citing documented harms such as privacy violations, discrimination, and suppression of civil liberties. The coalition highlights abuses in multiple countries and warns that current regulations risk enabling further AI-driven rights violations.

records.title: AI-Driven Price Discrimination Against Loyal Customers in China Spurs Regulatory Action
records.description: Chinese online platforms have used AI algorithms and big data to implement discriminatory pricing, charging loyal or frequent users higher prices than new users. This practice, known as 'big data price discrimination,' has harmed consumer rights and fairness, prompting widespread complaints and proposed local regulations in Shenzhen to impose heavy fines on violators.

records.title: Turkish AI-Enabled Drone Strike Kills Three at Iraqi Kurdish Refugee Camp
records.description: A Turkish military drone attack, likely involving AI-enabled targeting, struck the Machmur refugee camp in northern Iraq, killing three civilians. The camp, home to about 12,000 people, was hit near a kindergarten and school, raising concerns over civilian safety and escalating regional tensions.

records.title: Shanghai's AI-Powered Mass Surveillance System Raises Human Rights Concerns
records.description: Shanghai's 'City Brain' system uses 290,000 AI-driven cameras and facial recognition to monitor public behavior, enforce COVID-19 measures, and identify individuals in real time. This pervasive surveillance has led to significant privacy violations and social control, raising serious concerns about human rights and personal freedoms.

records.title: AI-Enabled Combat Drones Used in Attacks on US Forces in Iraq
records.description: Iran-backed militias in Iraq have increasingly used sophisticated, AI-enabled combat drones to target US military bases and sensitive facilities, including those used by the CIA and Special Operations. These drone attacks have evaded defenses, caused property damage, and posed significant threats to personnel, prompting urgent countermeasures by US forces.

records.title: AI-Driven Warfare in Gaza: Israeli Military's First 'Artificial Intelligence War' Causes Civilian Harm
records.description: During an 11-day conflict in Gaza, the Israeli military used advanced AI systems and supercomputers for real-time intelligence, target selection, and operational decisions. This marked the first large-scale use of AI in warfare, directly contributing to hundreds of deaths, thousands of injuries, and widespread destruction of civilian infrastructure.

records.title: Google AI Search Labels Kannada 'Ugliest Language', Triggers Outrage and Apology
records.description: Google's AI-powered search algorithm displayed Kannada as the 'ugliest language in India,' sparking widespread outrage and official threats of legal action from Karnataka's government. The incident caused cultural harm to the Kannada-speaking community. Google apologized, removed the result, and pledged to improve its algorithms.

records.title: Amnesty International Exposes NYPD's Pervasive AI-Powered Surveillance Network in NYC
records.description: Amnesty International revealed that the NYPD uses over 15,000 surveillance cameras with facial recognition AI to monitor and track people across Manhattan, Brooklyn, and the Bronx. This practice has led to privacy violations, discriminatory targeting, and threats to civil liberties, prompting calls for a ban on such surveillance.

records.title: AI-Generated Fake Female Profiles Used in Hotel Social App Scam Busted by Shanghai Police
records.description: Shanghai police dismantled a fraud ring behind the 'Quzhu' app, which used AI-driven software to create over 10,000 fake female profiles and generate seductive content. The scam lured users into paying for chat services, resulting in financial losses. Ten suspects were arrested, and the app's fraudulent use of AI was central to the scheme.

records.title: YouTube AI Recommendations Linked to Increased COVID-19 Vaccine Hesitancy
records.description: A study by Oxford and Southampton universities found that YouTube's AI-driven recommendation algorithms create echo chambers by suggesting content aligned with users' fears, leading to increased COVID-19 vaccine hesitancy. YouTube users showed significantly lower willingness to vaccinate, highlighting indirect public health harm caused by AI-powered content recommendations.

records.title: AI Recruitment Systems Cause Bias and Unfair Job Rejections
records.description: Multiple companies are using AI systems to evaluate and select job candidates, often without human oversight. These systems, including those using personality games and automated assessments, have led to unfair rejections and documented bias, such as Amazon's AI discriminating against women, raising concerns about labor rights and discrimination in hiring.

records.title: Dutch Parents Sue TikTok Over AI-Driven Harm to Children
records.description: Thousands of Dutch parents, represented by the SOMI foundation, are demanding over €1.4 billion in damages from TikTok. They allege TikTok's AI-driven recommendation and data collection systems exposed minors to dangerous challenges and targeted advertising without consent, resulting in harm to children's safety and privacy.

records.title: AI-Driven Bot Networks Manipulate Twitter Trends, Spreading Disinformation and Harm
records.description: EPFL researchers uncovered that automated bots exploit a vulnerability in Twitter's AI-driven Trends algorithm, enabling large-scale manipulation of trending topics. Up to half of Turkey's trends and a significant portion globally are fake, spreading disinformation, hate speech, and scams, thus harming public discourse and communities.

records.title: Amazon Faces Legal Action Over Alexa's Unauthorized Voice Recordings
records.description: Amazon is facing over 75,000 complaints alleging its Alexa AI assistant illegally recorded and stored users' conversations without consent, violating privacy rights. In response, Amazon changed its terms of service to allow class-action lawsuits instead of mandatory arbitration, enabling customers to sue the company in court.

records.title: Rights Groups Condemn AI-Driven Digital Surveillance of Immigrants by ICE
records.description: Human rights and advocacy groups criticize U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) for using AI-powered surveillance tools—such as facial recognition, GPS ankle monitors, and monitoring apps—on nearly 100,000 immigrants. Reports highlight emotional, physical, and rights-based harms, urging the Biden administration to end these 'digital prisons' and associated human rights violations.

records.title: Amazon Alters AI Productivity Monitoring After Worker Injuries Linked to Algorithmic Pressure
records.description: Amazon is revising its AI-driven productivity monitoring system, which tracked 'time off task' and penalized workers, after reports linked the system to increased musculoskeletal injuries among warehouse employees. The change follows criticism that the algorithm imposed unsafe work demands, directly harming workers' health.

records.title: AI-Powered Surveillance at Greek-Turkish Border Raises Human Rights Concerns for Migrants
records.description: The EU has deployed AI-driven surveillance systems—including cameras, sensors, biometric scanners, and AI-powered lie detectors—along the Greece-Turkey border to detect and deter migrants. Human rights groups warn these technologies restrict movement, facilitate pushbacks, and contribute to the dehumanization and criminalization of migrants, raising serious ethical and rights concerns.

records.title: AI-Enabled Armed Drones Used in Lethal Operation in Northern Iraq
records.description: The Turkish Ministry of Defense announced that AI-enabled armed drones (SİHA) were used to neutralize three PKK militants in Iraq's Zap region. The incident highlights the direct use of AI-driven military systems resulting in lethal harm during ongoing counter-terrorism operations.

records.title: Instagram Alters Algorithm After Suppression of Pro-Palestinian Content
records.description: Instagram changed its content ranking algorithm after employees and users reported that pro-Palestinian posts were being suppressed during the Gaza conflict. The AI-driven system had prioritized original content over re-shared posts, unintentionally limiting the reach of certain viewpoints. Instagram now treats original and re-shared content equally to address the issue.

records.title: Mercedes Recalls Over 340,000 Cars in US Due to AI-Driven Camera Malfunction
records.description: Mercedes-Benz recalled 342,366 vehicles in the US after the MBUX multimedia system, which includes AI components, malfunctioned by blanking screens or failing to display correct camera images. This increased the risk of collisions or injuries, prompting a recall and free software update, though no injuries have been reported.

records.title: Apple Sued After Facial Recognition Misidentifies Teen as Thief
records.description: Apple and its security contractor, Security Industry Specialists, are being sued after their facial recognition system wrongly identified Ousmane Bah as a shoplifter, leading to his false arrest and defamation. The misidentification stemmed from a stolen permit, highlighting the harm caused by over-reliance on unreliable AI-driven biometrics.

records.title: Autonomous Drone Attacks Human Target in Libya Without Human Command
records.description: In March 2020, a Turkish-made Kargu-2 drone autonomously hunted and attacked a retreating soldier in Libya without direct human control, according to a UN report. This incident marks one of the first known cases of an AI-powered lethal autonomous weapon system engaging a human target independently in active combat.

records.title: Portuguese University Ordered to Suspend AI Exam Surveillance Software Over Data Protection Violations
records.description: The University of Minho used AI-powered Respondus software to monitor students during online exams, analyzing biometric and behavioral data. Portugal's data protection authority (CNPD) found this surveillance excessive and unlawful, violating GDPR principles and students' rights, leading to the software's suspension and an order to delete collected personal data.

records.title: Facebook Employees Accuse AI Systems of Bias Against Palestinian and Arab Content
records.description: Facebook employees, including a software engineer from Egypt, accused the company’s AI-driven content moderation systems of bias against Palestinian, Arab, and Muslim content during the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. Evidence showed warnings and censorship disproportionately targeting Arabic pages, eroding user trust and raising concerns about discriminatory AI enforcement and harm to affected communities.

records.title: Google Sued for AI-Driven Location Tracking Despite User Opt-Outs
records.description: Google's AI-enabled location tracking continued collecting user data even after users disabled location services, leading to a lawsuit by Arizona for consumer fraud. Evidence revealed Google made privacy settings difficult to access, causing privacy violations and infringing on user rights through its AI system design and deployment.

records.title: China Tests AI Emotion-Detection on Uyghur Detainees in Xinjiang
records.description: Chinese authorities have deployed AI-based emotion-detection and facial recognition systems on Uyghur detainees in Xinjiang, using the technology to monitor and pre-judge individuals' emotional states. The AI is tested on restrained subjects in police stations and detention camps, contributing to mass surveillance and human rights abuses against the Uyghur minority.

records.title: AI System Deployed in Germany to Detect Child Abuse Material and Aid Investigations
records.description: A new AI system developed by law enforcement, scientists, and Microsoft in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, can identify child and youth pornography with over 90% accuracy. Already used in over 1600 investigations, it helps prosecutors quickly filter evidence, accelerating the fight against child abuse and supporting justice efforts.

records.title: Facebook's AI Moderation System Censors Vaccine Hesitancy Content Globally
records.description: Facebook deployed AI algorithms to identify and demote user comments expressing vaccine hesitancy, regardless of factual accuracy, as revealed by whistleblowers and leaked documents. This system, tested on millions of users, led to widespread censorship and suppression of information, raising concerns over violations of free speech and access to information.

records.title: Tesla Ordered to Pay Damages After AI Software Update Reduces Battery Performance
records.description: A 2019 software update in Tesla Model S vehicles, using AI-based battery management, reduced battery capacity and driving range, harming owners. Norwegian courts ordered Tesla to pay $16,000 to each affected customer. Similar lawsuits are ongoing in the US. The incident highlights risks from AI-driven software changes in vehicles.

records.title: Google AI Search Links Palestinian Keffiyeh to Terrorism, Sparking Outrage
records.description: Google's AI-driven search algorithm displayed the Palestinian keffiyeh as a 'terrorist symbol' in response to certain queries, leading to widespread anger and accusations of racism and cultural insult from activists. The incident highlights reputational and cultural harm caused by biased AI-generated search results.

records.title: AI Telemarketing Robots Cause Widespread Harassment and Privacy Violations in China
records.description: AI-powered telemarketing robots, capable of making thousands of calls daily and mimicking human speech, have led to widespread harassment and privacy violations in China. Individuals report repeated, irrelevant sales calls, highlighting the harm caused by automated systems that exploit personal data and disrupt daily life.

records.title: Chinese Regulators Expose 105 Apps, Including Douyin and Baidu, for Illegal Personal Data Collection
records.description: Chinese authorities identified 105 popular apps, including Douyin, Kuaishou, Baidu, and LinkedIn, for illegally and excessively collecting users' personal data, violating privacy laws. Many of these apps use AI-driven features. Operators were ordered to rectify within 15 days or face penalties, highlighting ongoing privacy and regulatory concerns.

records.title: GPT-3 Used to Generate Persuasive Disinformation on Social Media
records.description: Researchers at Georgetown University demonstrated that OpenAI's GPT-3 can generate convincing disinformation, including misleading tweets about climate change and foreign affairs. Human readers found these AI-generated posts persuasive, highlighting the real-world risk of AI systems amplifying misinformation and manipulating public opinion.

records.title: AI-Enabled Saudi Combat Drone Shot Down in Yemen Conflict
records.description: Yemeni Houthi forces announced the downing of a Saudi Air Force Wing Loong 2 combat drone, an AI-enabled Chinese-made UAV, over the Najran front. The incident highlights the use and destruction of autonomous military AI systems in active conflict, resulting in harm to military assets.

records.title: USPS and Clearview AI Involved in Covert Surveillance of Americans Using Facial Recognition Technology
records.description: The U.S. Postal Service's law enforcement arm has used Clearview AI's facial recognition software and other AI tools to covertly monitor Americans' social media activity, including protest discussions, and share information with law enforcement. This surveillance, conducted under the iCOP program, has raised significant privacy and human rights concerns.

records.title: Twitter Removes Biased Image-Cropping Algorithm After Racial and Gender Disparities Revealed
records.description: Twitter's automated image-cropping algorithm, deployed since 2018, was found to favor white individuals and women in photo previews, leading to racial and gender bias. After internal research confirmed these disparities, Twitter removed the algorithm from its platforms to address the harm caused by its biased outputs.

records.title: Clearview AI's Facial Recognition Sparks Privacy Violations and Legal Action
records.description: Clearview AI's facial recognition technology, which scrapes billions of images from social media without consent, has led to widespread privacy violations and legal challenges. Its secretive use by law enforcement and attempts to distribute data abroad have prompted lawsuits and public outcry over breaches of biometric and civil rights.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot Misuse: Driver Sleeps at 82 MPH, Stopped by Police
records.description: A 38-year-old Illinois man was cited for inattentive driving after being found asleep behind the wheel of his Tesla, which was operating on Autopilot at 82 mph in Wisconsin. Police followed the vehicle for over two miles before the driver responded, highlighting the dangers of overreliance on AI driving systems.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot Fails to Prevent Crash with Parked Police Car in Washington
records.description: A Tesla Model S operating on autopilot crashed into a parked Snohomish County deputy's patrol car in Arlington, Washington, causing significant property damage but no injuries. The incident highlights the risks of overreliance on Tesla's AI-driven autopilot system, which failed to detect and avoid the emergency vehicle.

records.title: Fatal Tesla Autopilot Crashes in California and China Raise Safety Concerns
records.description: Multiple fatal accidents involving Tesla vehicles with Autopilot engaged occurred in California and China. In both cases, drivers appeared to rely heavily on the AI system, with one posting videos of hands-free driving. The incidents resulted in deaths and injuries, highlighting risks associated with misuse or overreliance on Tesla's AI-assisted driving technology.

records.title: Facebook's AI Moderation Fails to Stop COVID-19 Misinformation Spread
records.description: Facebook's AI systems removed 14 million COVID-19 misinformation posts in 2020, yet its recommendation algorithms continued to promote anti-vaccine and anti-mask groups, undermining public health. Despite pledges to curb such content, AI-driven recommendations facilitated the ongoing spread of harmful misinformation on the platform.

records.title: Amazon Ring Enables Widespread Warrantless Police Surveillance via AI-Driven Home Cameras
records.description: Amazon's Ring doorbell system, using AI for video processing, has enabled over 1,800 US police departments to access footage from millions of private cameras without warrants. This expansion of law enforcement surveillance into private spaces raises significant privacy and civil liberties concerns, constituting a realized harm to fundamental rights.

records.title: Fatal Tesla Crash Linked to Possible Autopilot Misuse in California
records.description: Steven Hendrickson, a Tesla Model 3 driver known for posting videos of hands-free driving using Autopilot, died in a May 5 crash in Fontana, California, after colliding with an overturned truck. Investigations suggest the AI-powered Autopilot system may have been engaged, raising concerns about misuse and system limitations.

records.title: NFL's Race-Normed Algorithm Discriminates Against Black Players in Brain Injury Settlement
records.description: The NFL used an AI-based scoring algorithm in its $1 billion brain injury settlement that applied 'race-norming,' assuming Black players had lower baseline cognitive skills. This practice systematically reduced compensation for Black former players, resulting in direct discriminatory harm and legal challenges demanding equal treatment.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot Misuse and Overstated Capabilities Lead to Fatalities and Public Concern
records.description: Multiple incidents involving Tesla's Autopilot AI system have resulted in fatalities and public alarm. Overstatements by Elon Musk about the system's capabilities, combined with misuse—such as drivers not being at the wheel—have led to deadly crashes and arrests, highlighting the risks of overreliance and inadequate supervision of AI-driven vehicles.

records.title: Waymo Robotaxi Malfunctions and Blocks Traffic in Arizona
records.description: A Waymo autonomous taxi in Chandler, Arizona became confused by traffic cones blocking a lane, stalled, and repeatedly evaded roadside assistance, ultimately blocking a multi-lane road and causing a traffic jam. The incident, documented by a passenger, highlights challenges and safety risks in deploying AI-driven vehicles on public roads.

records.title: Facial Recognition AI Triggers Legal Action and Human Rights Concerns Globally
records.description: Facial recognition AI systems have led to wrongful arrests, privacy violations, and increased surveillance, prompting lawsuits and shutdowns in the US and Brazil. Incidents include Amazon's alleged secret data collection, police misuse resulting in wrongful detention, and legal rulings citing human rights violations, highlighting significant societal harm from AI misuse.

records.title: Multiple Incidents Highlight Risks and Failures in Autonomous Vehicle AI Systems
records.description: Several incidents involving AI-driven vehicles occurred: a Tesla Model 3 on Autopilot caused a fatal crash due to driver overreliance; a Waymo autonomous taxi malfunctioned in a construction zone, blocking traffic; and another Tesla driver was filmed asleep at the wheel, misusing the AI system and endangering lives.

records.title: Instagram AI Wrongly Flags Al-Aqsa Mosque Posts as Terrorism
records.description: Instagram's AI-driven content moderation system mistakenly labeled posts and hashtags about the Al-Aqsa Mosque—a major Islamic holy site—as linked to terrorism, leading to widespread removal and censorship of legitimate content during ongoing Israeli-Palestinian violence. The error restricted information and violated users' rights to free expression.

records.title: Facial Recognition AI Systems in China Lead to Privacy Violations and Regulatory Action
records.description: Multiple incidents in China reveal the unauthorized deployment of facial recognition AI systems in residential and commercial settings, resulting in privacy violations, personal data leaks, and regulatory penalties. Authorities fined companies for collecting biometric data without consent, while public resistance and legal scrutiny highlight ongoing risks and harms from misuse of AI-driven surveillance.

records.title: Apple AirTags Misused for Stalking and Privacy Violations After Jailbreak
records.description: Apple AirTags, designed for item tracking using AI-enabled location networks, have been jailbroken, allowing malicious firmware modifications. Experiments and expert warnings reveal AirTags can be covertly used for stalking and unauthorized tracking, bypassing anti-stalking features and raising significant privacy and safety concerns.

records.title: Tesla Owner Arrested for Repeatedly Misusing Autopilot by Riding in Back Seat
records.description: Param Sharma, a 25-year-old from California, was repeatedly arrested for riding in the back seat of his Tesla while the vehicle operated on Autopilot with no one at the wheel. His actions, widely shared on social media, highlight the dangers and legal consequences of misusing Tesla's AI driving systems, which require human supervision.

records.title: TikTok Sued for Unauthorized Use of Actress's Voice in AI Text-to-Speech Feature
records.description: Voice actress Bev Standing has sued TikTok and its parent company ByteDance for using her voice without consent in the platform's AI-powered text-to-speech feature. The unauthorized use has led to reputational and economic harm, as her voice is now widely used, including in offensive contexts, violating her intellectual property rights.

records.title: US Authorities Investigate Fatal Tesla Crash Involving Possible AI System Failure
records.description: The US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has launched an investigation into a fatal crash involving a Tesla vehicle in California, where the car collided with an overturned semi-trailer. The incident raises concerns about the potential role of Tesla's AI-driven systems, such as Autopilot, in the accident.

records.title: Tesla AI System Failures and Data Transparency Spark Safety Concerns in China
records.description: Multiple Tesla drivers in China reported brake failures and unintended acceleration, leading to accidents and injuries. Incomplete and potentially unreliable driving data from Tesla’s AI systems hindered accident investigations, prompting experts to call for mandatory 'black box' recorders and improved data transparency to address ongoing safety and accountability concerns.

records.title: AI Bias Leads to Racial Discrimination and Wrongful Arrests in the US
records.description: AI systems, including facial recognition and automated gender recognition, have caused harm to people of color and marginalized groups in the US. Incidents include wrongful arrests, discrimination, and exclusion from services due to algorithmic bias, prompting lawsuits and calls for bans on such technologies.

records.title: Tesla AI Systems Implicated in Fatal Crash and Risky Misuse Incidents
records.description: A Tesla in China crashed at 158 km/h, killing the driver and raising concerns over possible AI-related brake failures. Separately, in California, a man was seen riding in the back seat of a driverless Tesla using Autopilot, prompting police investigation and highlighting risks of AI misuse and potential harm.

records.title: Tesla's Full Self-Driving Claims Contradicted Amid Fatal Crash Concerns
records.description: Tesla engineers told California regulators that its Full Self-Driving (FSD) system remains at Level 2 autonomy, requiring human supervision, despite CEO Elon Musk's public claims of imminent full autonomy. Misunderstandings and misuse of the AI system have contributed to fatal crashes and regulatory warnings about public safety risks.

records.title: Dutch Forensic Institute Uses AI to Detect and Prevent Violent Crime via Encrypted Chats
records.description: The Dutch Forensic Institute (NFI) developed and deployed a deep learning model to scan millions of intercepted encrypted EncroChat messages for serious threats. The AI system enabled police to quickly identify and act on life-threatening messages, helping prevent kidnappings, torture, and murders by facilitating timely interventions.

records.title: Court Rules Snapchat Can Be Sued Over Speed Filter Linked to Fatal Crash
records.description: The Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that Snap Inc. can be sued for the design of Snapchat's AI-powered speed filter, which allegedly encouraged reckless driving and led to a fatal crash killing three young people. The court rejected Section 230 immunity, holding Snap potentially liable for harm caused by the AI feature.

records.title: AI Algorithms Accused of Manipulating News and Suppressing Independent Media Voices
records.description: Major social media platforms are accused of using AI-driven recommendation algorithms to promote mainstream media while suppressing independent and alternative viewpoints. This manipulation of information flow is alleged to harm communities by restricting access to diverse perspectives and reinforcing dominant narratives, raising concerns about media control and information rights.

records.title: Surge in Deepfake AI Crimes Causes Harm and Prompts Arrests
records.description: AI-powered deepfake technologies are increasingly used for crimes such as identity theft, fraud, blackmail, and non-consensual pornography, causing psychological and reputational harm. Police have arrested 94 suspects, mostly teenagers, for creating or distributing illegal deepfake content, with women and young people being the primary victims.

records.title: Smart TV Data Collection Scandal Exposes Massive Privacy Breach in China
records.description: A data service embedded in smart TVs from brands like Skyworth covertly scanned and collected detailed user and network data, affecting millions of households. The AI-driven system transmitted this information without clear consent, sparking public outcry and leading to terminated partnerships and demands for deletion of illegally obtained data due to privacy violations.

records.title: San Diego and Chinese Real Estate Developers Face Scrutiny Over Harmful Facial Recognition Practices
records.description: San Diego officials withheld information from Congress about racially biased and misused police facial recognition systems, impeding oversight and risking civil rights. Separately, Chinese real estate developers were fined for unlawfully collecting customers' facial data without consent, highlighting privacy violations and the harmful impact of unregulated AI surveillance.

records.title: Amazon's AI Algorithms Promote Extremist and Conspiratorial Content, Report Finds
records.description: A report by the Institute for Strategic Dialogue found that Amazon's AI-powered recommendation and search algorithms steer users toward books promoting conspiracy theories and extremism, including QAnon and vaccine misinformation. This algorithmic promotion of harmful content raises concerns about the role of AI in spreading misinformation and radicalization.

records.title: AI-Powered ECG Systems Enhance Emergency Cardiac Care in Taiwan
records.description: Taiwanese hospitals, including Tri-Service General Hospital and China Medical University Hospital, have deployed AI-assisted ECG interpretation systems in ambulances and clinics. These systems enable rapid, accurate diagnosis of acute heart conditions, allowing earlier intervention and reducing treatment delays, thereby improving patient outcomes and preventing harm from cardiac emergencies.

records.title: Chinese National Pleads Guilty to Smuggling AI-Enabled Underwater Tech to Chinese Military
records.description: Chinese national Qin Shuren pleaded guilty to illegally exporting advanced US underwater sensing devices and unmanned vehicles—technologies involving AI—to Chinese military research institutes. The smuggled equipment, valued at millions, is believed to enhance China’s underwater drone capabilities, posing a direct threat to US naval security and violating export laws.

records.title: Saudi Arabia Intercepts AI-Controlled Explosive Boat in Red Sea
records.description: Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Defense intercepted and destroyed a remotely controlled, explosive-laden boat in the Red Sea near Yanbu. The AI-driven vessel posed a threat to national assets and maritime security. Investigations are ongoing to identify those responsible for deploying the autonomous hostile system.

records.title: Ride-Hailing Platforms Use AI Algorithms for Discriminatory Pricing and Overcharging in China
records.description: Chinese ride-hailing platforms used AI-driven algorithms and big data to discriminate against users based on device type, leading to higher fares and reduced discounts for iPhone users. Official investigations and academic studies confirmed systematic overcharging and inaccurate billing, resulting in direct financial harm and unfair treatment of consumers.

records.title: Chinese AI Surveillance System Used in Canadian Restaurant Raises Privacy Concerns
records.description: A Chinese restaurant in Vancouver installed 60 cameras that transmit footage to China, where an AI-driven social credit system monitors and scores employees and guests. This practice, mandated by the Haidilao corporation, has led to privacy violations and sparked warnings from Canadian intelligence and calls for regulatory action.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot Can Be Tricked, Leading to Fatal Crash Without Driver
records.description: Consumer Reports engineers demonstrated that Tesla's Autopilot AI system can be easily fooled to operate without a driver present, failing to detect driver absence. This vulnerability was linked to a fatal crash in Texas where a Tesla vehicle, reportedly on Autopilot, crashed with no one behind the wheel, resulting in two deaths.

records.title: European Politicians Deceived by Deepfake Impersonating Navalny's Chief of Staff
records.description: European politicians, including Dutch, Baltic, and UK parliamentarians, were deceived in live video calls by a deepfake impersonating Leonid Volkov, chief of staff to Russian opposition leader Alexei Navalny. The AI-generated deepfake led to misinformation and raised concerns about political manipulation and the challenges of detecting such advanced AI-driven disinformation.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot and Braking System Failures Spark Fatalities and Regulatory Scrutiny
records.description: Multiple incidents involving Tesla's AI-driven Autopilot and braking systems have led to fatal crashes and public outcry. Investigations and tests revealed that Tesla vehicles can operate without a driver present, raising safety concerns. U.S. senators and Chinese regulators are demanding stricter oversight, while Tesla disputes claims of system malfunctions.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot Malfunction Implicated in Fatal Crash, Data Transparency Dispute Follows
records.description: A Tesla vehicle in Guangzhou crashed and caught fire, resulting in a fatality. The driver alleges the Autopilot (AP) system forcibly took control, causing the accident. Tesla provided AI system data to authorities amid public outcry and disputes over data ownership, transparency, and regulatory oversight of AI-driven vehicle incidents.

records.title: AI-Powered Loitering Munitions and Military Drones Cause and Pose Harm in Modern Warfare
records.description: Russia's Lancet loitering munition, an AI-driven suicide drone, has autonomously identified and attacked targets, causing harm in conflict zones. Meanwhile, Russia and China are developing AI-enabled UAV swarms and precision strike drones, raising significant risks of future harm through autonomous military operations and infrastructure attacks.

records.title: TikTok Sued for Illegal Collection of Children's Data Using AI Systems
records.description: Anne Longfield, former Children's Commissioner for England, has filed a lawsuit against TikTok and its parent company ByteDance, alleging illegal collection of personal and biometric data—including facial recognition—of millions of children in the UK and Europe without consent. The AI-driven data practices violate privacy laws and children's rights, prompting demands for substantial compensation.

records.title: Facial Recognition AI Misuse Leads to Privacy Violations and Discrimination Concerns in China and US Banks
records.description: Multiple incidents in China and the US reveal that facial recognition AI systems have been misused by businesses and banks, resulting in unauthorized collection, sale, and use of biometric data. These practices have led to privacy violations, potential identity theft, and raised concerns about racial bias and discrimination, prompting regulatory responses.

records.title: AI-Enabled Drones Used in Repeated Attacks on Saudi Military Base
records.description: Yemeni forces used AI-enabled Qasef 2K drones to launch multiple precise attacks on Saudi Arabia's King Khalid Air Base, causing damage to military infrastructure. The incidents highlight the direct use of autonomous drone systems in military operations, resulting in harm to property and escalating regional conflict.

records.title: Facebook's AI Moderation Fails to Curb Misinformation in Europe
records.description: Facebook's AI-driven content moderation systems have been ineffective at removing COVID-19 and climate misinformation in non-English European languages, leaving harmful falsehoods widely accessible. This disparity has undermined public health and climate action, as AI systems failed to flag or remove misleading content, causing harm to communities and public trust.

records.title: AI System at Chang Gung Memorial Hospital Reduces Pelvic Fracture Misdiagnosis and Prevents Fatal Bleeding
records.description: Chang Gung Memorial Hospital developed an AI algorithm trained on over 5,000 pelvic X-rays to assist emergency doctors in detecting pelvic fractures, a common but often-missed cause of life-threatening bleeding. The AI system significantly reduced misdiagnosis rates, enabled timely interventions, and improved patient survival, with international hospitals adopting the technology.

records.title: Fatal Tesla Crash in Texas Raises Concerns Over Autopilot AI System
records.description: A Tesla Model S crashed and caught fire near Houston, Texas, killing two people. Authorities found no one in the driver's seat, suggesting the vehicle was operating on Autopilot, Tesla's AI-driven system. The incident has prompted investigations and renewed scrutiny of Tesla's autonomous driving technology after similar accidents.

records.title: Fatal Tesla Crash Sparks Debate Over Autopilot Involvement
records.description: A fatal crash in Texas involving a Tesla resulted in two deaths, with police suggesting no one was in the driver's seat. Elon Musk and Tesla data indicate Autopilot was not engaged and the car lacked Full Self Driving capability, raising questions about AI system use and driver supervision.

records.title: TikTok AI Algorithm Failure Exposes Users to Pornography and Violent Extremist Content
records.description: A failure in TikTok's AI-driven content moderation and recommendation system allowed users, including minors, to be widely exposed to pornographic and violent extremist material. The incident, linked to the viral 'Don't search this up' trend, led to over 50 million interactions before TikTok began banning related accounts and hashtags.

records.title: US Sanctions on Chinese AI Chip Customers Cause Major Losses for Taiwanese Semiconductor Firms
records.description: US export controls targeting Chinese firms using AI-enabled chips for military supercomputers have led to severe financial losses for Taiwanese IC design companies like Alchip and TSMC. The sanctions, prompted by concerns over AI technology's military use, caused stock crashes and disrupted supply chains, highlighting the geopolitical risks of AI system development.

records.title: Civil Rights Groups Challenge Harmful Use of Clearview AI Facial Recognition by US Agencies
records.description: The ACLU and over 70 organizations are pressuring US agencies, including ICE, CBP, and DHS, to halt the use of Clearview AI's facial recognition system. The AI has led to wrongful arrests, privacy violations, and human rights concerns, particularly affecting immigrants and marginalized communities, prompting lawsuits and calls for transparency and oversight.

records.title: Taipei Deploys AI Traffic Signals to Reduce Pedestrian Red-Light Violations
records.description: Taipei City installed AI-powered adaptive traffic signals at busy intersections to detect and warn pedestrians attempting to cross during red lights. The system issues audible and visual alerts, resulting in a 50% reduction in daily violations and aiming to prevent pedestrian accidents and improve road safety.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot Crash in Texas Kills Two, Sparks Safety Concerns
records.description: A Tesla Model S, reportedly in autonomous driving mode, crashed into a tree in Texas, killing two occupants and causing a fire that took hours and over 100,000 liters of water to extinguish. The incident raises concerns about Tesla's Autopilot AI system, despite company claims of superior safety.

records.title: Instagram AI Search Algorithm Promotes Harmful Diet Content to Vulnerable Users
records.description: Instagram's AI-powered search recommendation system mistakenly suggested harmful dieting terms, such as 'appetite suppressants' and 'fasting', to users with eating disorders. This led to psychological harm and risk of relapse. Instagram has apologized, acknowledged the error, and removed the problematic terms from its platform.

records.title: Bavarian Police Use AI Facial Recognition to Identify Hundreds of Suspects
records.description: In 2020, Bavarian police used an AI-powered facial recognition system to identify 649 suspects, a significant increase from previous years. The system compares surveillance images with a national database, directly impacting individuals by facilitating law enforcement actions and raising concerns about privacy and potential rights violations.

records.title: AI Customer Service Bots Deliberately Obstruct Access to Human Support
records.description: Multiple reports reveal that AI-powered customer service chatbots are intentionally configured to delay or prevent users from reaching human agents, causing widespread frustration and denying timely assistance. This practice harms consumer rights and service quality, particularly affecting vulnerable groups like the elderly.

records.title: Detroit Man Wrongfully Arrested After AI Facial Recognition Error Sparks Lawsuit
records.description: Robert Williams, a Black man from Michigan, was wrongfully arrested and detained after Detroit police relied on faulty facial recognition software that misidentified him as a shoplifter. The incident, which highlights racial bias and flaws in AI systems, led Williams and the ACLU to file a federal lawsuit against the city and police.

records.title: Canada Cancels Drone Tech Exports to Turkey Over AI Use in Nagorno-Karabakh Conflict
records.description: Canada cancelled export permits for drone technology to Turkey after finding that Canadian-made AI-enabled imaging and targeting systems were used by Azerbaijan in the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict, violating end-use assurances and contributing to harm in the region. The decision responds to the misuse of AI systems in military operations.

records.title: Facebook AI Moderation Wrongly Censors French Town 'Bitche' Over Name Confusion
records.description: Facebook's automated content moderation algorithm mistakenly censored the official page of the French town Bitche, misinterpreting its name as an English insult. The wrongful suspension disrupted the town's communication until Facebook acknowledged the error and restored the page, highlighting flaws in AI language understanding.

records.title: India Pilots Aadhaar-Based Facial Recognition for COVID-19 Vaccination Authentication
records.description: The Indian government is piloting an AI-driven facial recognition system using Aadhaar biometric data to authenticate COVID-19 vaccine recipients, aiming to reduce infection risk by avoiding physical contact. While not mandatory, the initiative raises concerns about potential privacy, exclusion, and ethical risks if widely implemented.

records.title: China's First Facial Recognition Lawsuit: Court Orders Deletion of Biometric Data
records.description: A Chinese court ruled in favor of plaintiff Guo Bing, ordering Hangzhou Safari Park to delete his facial and fingerprint data after the zoo unilaterally switched from fingerprint to facial recognition for entry without proper consent. The case highlights privacy risks and legal requirements for AI-based biometric data collection.

records.title: Facebook AI Algorithms Drastically Limit Hungarian Government Content During Pandemic
records.description: Facebook's AI-driven content moderation systems reportedly reduced the reach and interaction of Hungarian government and right-wing officials' posts by about 90% without prior notice. This action, occurring during the COVID-19 pandemic, limited citizens' access to public health information, raising concerns about rights violations and lack of transparency.

records.title: YouTube's AI Ad Targeting System Enables Monetization of Hate Speech and Discriminatory Practices
records.description: Investigations revealed YouTube's AI-driven ad targeting system allowed advertisers to search for and place ads on videos linked to white supremacist and hate-related terms, while blocking racial justice keywords like 'Black Lives Matter.' Google's partial and inconsistent keyword blocking enabled monetization and amplification of harmful content, causing societal harm and discrimination.

records.title: Facebook's AI Ad Algorithms Perpetuate Gender Bias in Job Ads
records.description: A University of Southern California study found Facebook's AI-driven ad delivery system shows job ads to users in a gender-biased manner, with men and women seeing different opportunities regardless of qualifications. This discriminatory practice violates anti-discrimination and labor laws, limiting equal access to employment opportunities.

records.title: Proctorio Exam Software's AI Fails to Detect Faces of Students of Color, Causing Discrimination
records.description: Proctorio, an AI-based exam proctoring software, uses facial detection algorithms that fail to recognize Black faces over 50% of the time. This bias has led to students of color being unfairly flagged or unable to take exams, resulting in discrimination and harm to their educational opportunities.

records.title: Facebook Sued Over AI Moderation Failures Allowing Anti-Muslim Hate Speech
records.description: Civil rights group Muslim Advocates sued Facebook and its executives, alleging the company's AI-driven content moderation failed to remove pervasive anti-Muslim hate speech. Despite claims of effective AI moderation, the lawsuit argues these failures have led to real-world harm and violated consumer protection laws.

records.title: AI Deepfake App Used to Create and Distribute Non-Consensual Fake Nude Images
records.description: A woman received an AI-generated fake nude image of herself, created from her swimsuit photo using a deepfake app like DeepNude. Despite the app's removal, cracked versions persist online, enabling malicious actors to violate privacy and cause psychological harm by distributing non-consensual explicit images.

records.title: Widespread, Unregulated Police Use of Clearview AI Facial Recognition Raises Privacy and Rights Concerns
records.description: Thousands of law enforcement and public agency employees across the U.S. used Clearview AI’s facial recognition software—often without oversight, consent, or proper training—leading to privacy violations, potential racial bias, and unauthorized surveillance. The system scraped billions of social media photos without consent, prompting bans and public outcry over rights violations.

records.title: Facial Recognition AI in China: Security Flaws, Privacy Violations, and Positive Outcomes
records.description: AI-powered facial recognition systems in China have led to both positive and negative incidents. Police successfully used the technology to reunite missing persons with families. However, widespread misuse and security flaws enabled unauthorized data collection, privacy violations, and system breaches, prompting regulatory scrutiny and calls for stricter governance and industry standards.

records.title: AI-Enabled Drones Used in Houthi Attacks on Saudi Targets Intercepted by Coalition
records.description: Houthi forces launched multiple AI-enabled or autonomous drones targeting Saudi airports and cities, including Jazan, Abha, and Khamis Mushait. The Saudi-led coalition intercepted and destroyed the drones, preventing harm to civilians and infrastructure. The incidents highlight the use of AI-driven weaponry in armed conflict, posing significant risks to civilian safety.

records.title: Coded Bias Exposes Real-World Harms of AI Discrimination
records.description: The documentary 'Coded Bias' highlights how AI systems, including facial recognition and automated hiring tools, have caused real harm by perpetuating racial and gender bias. These technologies have led to discrimination, wrongful police matches, and violations of civil rights, prompting calls for greater oversight and regulation.

records.title: Google Photos AI Misclassifies Intimate Video, Causing Privacy Breach
records.description: Google Photos' facial recognition AI mistakenly identified a child's photo in the background of an intimate video, automatically categorizing it with the child's album and sharing it with the user's mother. This led to an unintended privacy breach and emotional distress, highlighting risks of AI-driven auto-sharing features.

records.title: Russia Tests AI-Enabled Strike Drones in Syria for Real-Time Targeting and Attacks
records.description: Russian military tested the AI-enabled 'Inokhodets' strike drones in Syria, using the 'Strelets-M' reconnaissance and communication system for real-time target identification and coordination. The system enabled drones to autonomously receive and strike targets, demonstrating direct AI involvement in military operations resulting in harm to enemy forces.

records.title: China Deploys AI Surveillance for Racial and Ethnic Profiling
records.description: Chinese authorities have enlisted surveillance companies to develop AI-powered facial recognition systems that classify individuals by race and skin color. These systems, used nationwide and exported abroad, enable large-scale discriminatory surveillance and targeting of ethnic minorities, raising serious human rights and privacy concerns.

records.title: Chinese AI Surveillance Data Leak Exposes Mass Tracking of Uyghurs and Foreigners
records.description: A major data leak from Shanghai revealed that Chinese authorities used AI-powered facial recognition and biometric systems to track over 25,000 'persons of interest,' including Uyghur minorities and 5,000 foreigners. The surveillance, enabled by advanced AI, led to significant privacy violations and human rights abuses, exposing the scale of China's mass monitoring.

records.title: Tesla on Cruise Control Crashes into Truck in New Jersey, Prompting Federal Investigation
records.description: A Tesla using its AI-based cruise control system crashed into a stationary tractor-trailer in New Jersey after the driver lost focus, severely damaging the car but causing only minor injuries. The U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration is investigating the incident, highlighting concerns over driver reliance on AI-assisted driving features.

records.title: Global Incidents and Risks from Facial Recognition AI Systems
records.description: Facial recognition AI systems have led to harm and risks worldwide: in China, fraudsters exploited system vulnerabilities to commit financial crimes; in the UK, government-backed facial verification for vaccination status raises surveillance and discrimination concerns; and globally, transgender individuals face exclusion and stigmatization due to algorithmic bias and misidentification.

records.title: TikTok Algorithm Promotes Banned Far-Right Content in the US
records.description: A Media Matters for America investigation found that TikTok's AI-driven recommendation algorithm promotes and facilitates the spread of banned far-right extremist content, including groups linked to the January 6 Capitol insurrection. Despite platform policies prohibiting such content, users are easily exposed to and encouraged to follow these accounts.

records.title: AI-Powered Body-Editing Apps Linked to Surge in Eating Disorders Among Youth
records.description: The eating disorder charity Seed reports a significant rise in young people seeking help, linking this to AI-driven body-editing apps advertised on social media platforms like TikTok and Instagram. The charity urges these platforms to address the mental health harms caused by promoting such apps to vulnerable audiences.

records.title: Lisbon Law School Drops AI Exam Surveillance After Privacy Backlash
records.description: The University of Lisbon Law School planned to use the AI-based Proctorio system for online exam monitoring, recording students' movements, sounds, and screens. Widespread student protests over privacy and data protection violations led the institution to abandon the AI system and revert to in-person exams.

records.title: Teens Misuse Tesla Autopilot, Crash Into Police Car in Florida
records.description: Two underage girls, ages 14 and 15, used a Tesla's autopilot feature while traveling without a licensed driver, resulting in the vehicle backing into a police cruiser during a traffic stop in Florida. The misuse of the AI-driven autopilot system led to property damage and highlighted safety risks of unauthorized autonomous vehicle operation.

records.title: Facebook's AI Systems Amplify Extremist and White Supremacist Content
records.description: Reports from the Tech Transparency Project reveal that Facebook's AI-driven recommendation and page auto-generation systems have facilitated the spread of militia and white supremacist content. Despite bans and public pledges to curb extremism, Facebook's algorithms continued to promote and create pages for hate groups, contributing to real-world harm.

records.title: Widespread Unauthorized Use of Facial Recognition in Chinese Real Estate Violates Privacy Laws
records.description: Real estate developers in cities like Changsha and Suzhou have widely deployed facial recognition cameras in sales offices to track visitors without consent, violating privacy laws and personal information protections. Judicial authorities have launched investigations and enforcement actions in response to consumer complaints and media exposure of these AI-driven privacy infringements.

records.title: Instagram's AI Algorithms Facilitate Neo-Nazi Recruitment of Teenagers
records.description: Reports from Hope Not Hate reveal that Instagram's AI-driven recommendation algorithms and inadequate moderation have enabled neo-Nazi groups to recruit and radicalize teenagers, leading to terrorism-related charges. The platform's algorithmic promotion of extremist content has directly contributed to harm within communities.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot and FSD Beta Exhibit Dangerous Left-Turn Behavior in Real-World Tests
records.description: Multiple videos by tester Chuck Cook reveal that Tesla's Autopilot and Full Self-Driving (FSD) beta systems struggle with unprotected left turns, often hesitating or making risky maneuvers in heavy traffic. Human intervention was repeatedly required to prevent accidents, highlighting significant safety concerns with the AI's real-world driving capabilities.

records.title: Google Translate's Gender Bias Reinforces Stereotypes in Neutral Languages
records.description: Google Translate's AI system exhibits gender bias when translating from gender-neutral languages like Basque and Hungarian, assigning male or female pronouns based on stereotypical roles (e.g., 'he drives,' 'she sews'). This perpetuates gender stereotypes and misrepresents the neutrality of the source language, causing harm by reinforcing discrimination.

records.title: Tesla's AI-Driven Self-Driving Systems Under Scrutiny After Accidents and Near-Misses
records.description: Tesla's Autopilot and Full Self-Driving AI systems are under investigation after multiple crashes, including incidents where vehicles steered toward oncoming traffic or struck stationary objects. Regulatory agencies are probing at least 23 active cases, highlighting safety concerns and prompting Tesla to halt software expansions and updates.

records.title: Chinese Retailers Investigated for Illegal AI Facial Recognition Data Collection
records.description: Multiple Chinese retailers, including Miniso and Kohler, used AI-powered facial recognition cameras to covertly collect and analyze customers' biometric data without consent, violating privacy laws. Authorities launched investigations, removed cameras, and highlighted risks of data misuse, financial fraud, and threats to personal safety from unauthorized AI-driven data collection.

records.title: Amazon AI Surveillance Cameras Spark Employee Backlash and Privacy Concerns
records.description: Amazon installed AI-powered cameras in delivery vans to monitor drivers’ behavior and collect biometric data, prompting privacy and labor rights concerns. Some drivers, including one in Denver, quit over the surveillance, while others faced pressure to sign consent forms or risk losing their jobs, leading to employee backlash and political scrutiny.

records.title: Myanmar Military Uses AI Surveillance to Suppress Protesters
records.description: Myanmar's military authorities have deployed Chinese AI-powered facial and license plate recognition systems to monitor and track protesters following the 2021 coup. Human rights groups warn this surveillance enables repression, threatens civil liberties, and has contributed to a violent crackdown resulting in over 200 deaths.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot Crashes and Data Privacy Concerns Spark Investigations and Bans
records.description: Tesla's Autopilot AI system has been involved in multiple crashes, including collisions with police cars and trucks, prompting US safety investigations. Meanwhile, China has banned Tesla vehicles for military and government use over fears that the cars' AI-driven data collection could threaten national security.

records.title: Dutch Police Facial Recognition System Retains Innocent Individuals in Database
records.description: The Dutch police's AI-based facial recognition system, CATCH, has wrongfully retained tens of thousands of individuals in its database, including those acquitted or no longer suspects. This mismanagement violates privacy and legal rights, raising serious concerns about fundamental rights and the lawful use of AI in law enforcement.

records.title: Major Retailers in China Secretly Collect Massive Facial Recognition Data Without Consent
records.description: Multiple well-known retailers in China, including Kohler, BMW, and MaxMara, were exposed for secretly installing AI-powered facial recognition cameras in stores, collecting and analyzing customers' biometric data without consent. This widespread, unauthorized data collection violates privacy laws and poses significant risks to personal security and rights.

records.title: China Deploys AI-Powered Mass Surveillance and Social Credit System
records.description: China is implementing AI-driven surveillance systems, including emotion recognition cameras and social credit scoring, to monitor and control its citizens. These technologies enable pervasive monitoring, social discrimination, and human rights violations, with citizens' behavior tracked and punished or rewarded, raising global concerns about privacy and freedom.

records.title: Florida Sheriff Sued for Using AI to Predict and Police Future Crimes
records.description: The Pasco County Sheriff in Florida used AI-powered predictive policing software to identify individuals likely to reoffend, leading to harassment, unjustified detentions, and violations of constitutional rights. Victims and civil rights groups have filed a lawsuit, alleging the AI system caused direct harm by targeting people for crimes not yet committed.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot-Linked Crashes Prompt Federal Investigations in Michigan and Detroit
records.description: Multiple Tesla vehicles operating with Autopilot, an AI-driven driver-assistance system, were involved in serious crashes in Michigan and Detroit, including one where a Tesla struck a police cruiser and another where a Tesla drove under a semitrailer, critically injuring two people. Federal investigators are probing the AI system's role in these incidents.

records.title: Tesla AI System Failures Lead to Multiple Accidents and Public Outcry in China
records.description: Multiple accidents involving Tesla vehicles in China, attributed to suspected AI system malfunctions such as sudden acceleration and brake failure, have resulted in injuries and property damage. Tesla often blames driver error, but disputes over data transparency and system reliability have fueled consumer anger and calls for stronger regulation of intelligent connected vehicles.

records.title: Face ID on iPad Fails to Distinguish Two Users, Leading to Security Flaw and Compensation Demand
records.description: Two men in Yekaterinburg exploited a malfunction in Apple's AI-based Face ID on an iPad, which incorrectly authenticated both due to their similar appearance. They demanded $1 million from Apple for exposing the vulnerability, but Apple refused, advising them to reset Face ID. The incident highlights a security flaw in the AI system.

records.title: Ele.me's AI-Driven Price Discrimination Harms Members and Consumers
records.description: Ele.me's AI-powered pricing algorithms have led to widespread consumer complaints in Shanghai, as members and frequent users are charged higher prices or receive fewer discounts than non-members. This algorithmic price discrimination, known as 'big data price gouging,' has resulted in unfair treatment and violation of consumer rights.

records.title: NTSB Criticizes Tesla for Testing Unfinished Autopilot AI on Public Roads
records.description: The US National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) criticized Tesla for testing its AI-driven Autopilot and Full Self-Driving systems on public roads with limited oversight, citing past fatal crashes and ongoing safety risks. The NTSB urged stricter federal regulations to prevent harm from insufficiently regulated autonomous vehicle technology.
