records.description: Russia has developed and tested AI-equipped drones, armored vehicles, and electromagnetic (EM) guns that can disable or destroy enemy electronic systems within a 10 km radius. These AI-enabled weapons have already destroyed test targets and pose risks of harm to military personnel and equipment by disrupting critical control systems.

records.title: Clearview AI Suspends Facial Recognition Services in Canada Amid Privacy Investigation
records.description: Clearview AI has halted its facial recognition services in Canada following an ongoing investigation by federal and provincial privacy commissioners into potential privacy rights violations. The company also ended its contract with the RCMP, reflecting concerns over the AI system's collection and use of biometric data.

records.title: Facial Recognition AI Sparks Human Rights and Civil Liberties Backlash
records.description: AI-powered facial recognition systems have led to privacy violations, wrongful arrests, and disproportionate harm to marginalized groups. Activists and rights groups have challenged their use in Russia and the US, citing human rights abuses and racial bias, prompting calls for bans and regulatory action against law enforcement surveillance.

records.title: Turkey Launches Investigation into TikTok Over AI-Driven Data Privacy Concerns
records.description: Turkey's Personal Data Protection Board (KVKK) has launched an official investigation into TikTok following reports and complaints of unauthorized personal data collection and privacy violations. TikTok's AI-driven data processing and surveillance practices are under scrutiny for potentially breaching users' data protection rights.

records.title: AI Camera System Deployed in Japanese Banks to Prevent Phone Fraud
records.description: JVC Kenwood and Bizright Technology deployed an AI-powered edge camera system in Hokuyo Bank branches to detect suspicious behavior, such as making phone calls at ATMs, which may indicate phone fraud. The system notifies staff to intervene, aiming to prevent financial harm from scams without recording or transmitting video data.

records.title: Voice Assistants' False Triggers Lead to Widespread Privacy Violations
records.description: Researchers found over 1,000 words and phrases that inadvertently activate AI voice assistants like Alexa, Siri, Google Assistant, and Cortana, causing them to record and transmit private conversations without user consent. These recordings are sometimes reviewed by company employees, resulting in significant privacy breaches due to AI system malfunctions.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot Crash Leads to Criminal Charges After Police Car Collision in Massachusetts
records.description: A Tesla Model 3 on Autopilot crashed into a parked police cruiser during a traffic stop in Massachusetts, injuring a state trooper and causing property damage. The driver, who admitted inattention while relying on the AI system, now faces criminal negligence charges. The incident highlights Autopilot's limitations in detecting stationary vehicles.

records.title: Boeing 737 Max AI System Malfunction Leads to Fatal Crashes and Regulatory Overhaul
records.description: The Boeing 737 Max's automated flight control system (MCAS), an AI-driven component, malfunctioned and caused two fatal crashes, killing 346 people. Regulators now demand significant design changes and extensive testing of the AI system before the aircraft can return to service, highlighting the risks of flawed AI in aviation.

records.title: Russian Design Studio Secretly Used AI as Human Designer for Over a Year
records.description: Artemy Lebedev Studio developed an AI system, 'Nikolay Ironov', to generate commercial logo designs, presenting it as a remote human employee. For over a year, clients were unaware their projects were AI-created, constituting a significant breach of transparency and consumer rights through deliberate deception.

records.title: Detroit Police Wrongfully Arrest Black Man Due to Faulty Facial Recognition AI
records.description: Detroit police wrongfully arrested Robert Williams, a Black man, after facial recognition AI falsely matched him to a crime. The incident, acknowledged by authorities and highlighted by the ACLU, exposed racial bias and inaccuracies in the technology, leading to calls for moratoriums and policy changes regarding AI use in law enforcement.

records.title: AI-Driven Social Credit Scores Deny Financial Services Globally
records.description: AI systems analyzing social media data to generate social credit scores are causing harm worldwide, with 18% of consumers denied loans or mortgages due to these automated assessments. The lack of transparency and regulation around such AI-driven scoring systems raises concerns about privacy, rights violations, and economic exclusion.

records.title: AI-Driven Bots and Algorithms Manipulate Social Media, Fueling Misinformation and Division
records.description: Social media platforms use AI algorithms and automated bot accounts to curate and amplify content, often spreading misinformation and divisive material. Malicious actors, including hackers and foreign governments, exploit these systems to manipulate public opinion, leading to societal harm and erosion of trust in online information.

records.title: Facebook's AI Fails to Curb Hate Speech in Private Groups
records.description: Investigations by German public broadcasters revealed that Facebook's AI-driven moderation and recommendation algorithms failed to remove thousands of instances of hate speech, incitement to violence, and illegal content in private right-wing groups, allowing harmful material to persist and spread on the platform for years.

records.title: NYCLU Sues Over Facial Recognition in Lockport Schools for Privacy and Bias Concerns
records.description: The New York Civil Liberties Union filed a lawsuit against the New York State Education Department over Lockport schools' use of AI-powered facial recognition technology, alleging violations of student privacy laws, data protection, and racial bias. The system's deployment has sparked controversy and legal challenges regarding its accuracy and intrusiveness.

records.title: AI Image Reconstruction Tool Exposes Racial Bias by Turning Black Faces White
records.description: The AI tool Face Depixelizer, designed to reconstruct high-resolution faces from pixelated images, repeatedly transformed images of Black individuals, including Barack Obama, into white faces. This incident highlights significant algorithmic racial bias stemming from the tool's training data, raising concerns about misrepresentation and discrimination in AI systems.

records.title: Study Finds Uber and Lyft Algorithms Charge Higher Fares in Non-White Neighborhoods
records.description: A George Washington University study of over 100 million Chicago rides found Uber and Lyft's AI pricing algorithms charge higher fares for trips to or from predominantly non-white or low-income neighborhoods, revealing algorithmic bias and resulting in discriminatory financial harm. Both companies dispute the study's methodology but acknowledge the issue of systemic bias.

records.title: TikTok's AI Algorithm Criticized for Promoting Harmful Content and Censorship
records.description: TikTok's AI-driven recommendation and moderation systems have been criticized for promoting content that glamorizes eating disorders and for allegedly suppressing posts from minority creators. These issues have led to harm to users' mental health and violations of rights, highlighting the negative impact of TikTok's AI algorithms on its community.

records.title: Moroccan Journalist Targeted by AI-Driven Spyware Pegasus
records.description: Amnesty International revealed that Moroccan journalist Omar Radi was repeatedly targeted and surveilled by the Moroccan government using NSO Group's AI-powered Pegasus spyware. The attacks, which violated Radi's privacy and freedom of expression, continued even after NSO pledged to respect human rights, highlighting the direct harm caused by AI surveillance technology.

records.title: AI Systems Exhibit Racial Bias, Leading to Discriminatory Outcomes
records.description: Multiple AI systems, including Microsoft's Tay chatbot, facial recognition tools, and beauty contest algorithms, have demonstrated racist biases, resulting in offensive outputs and discriminatory decisions. These incidents have caused harm to minority groups and reignited concerns about AI-driven racial discrimination amid global anti-racism protests.

records.title: YouTube Sued Over Alleged AI-Driven Racial Discrimination Against Black Creators
records.description: A federal lawsuit accuses YouTube and its parent companies of using AI-powered profiling and filtering tools that allegedly discriminate against Black video creators by restricting, censoring, and demonetizing their content based on race, resulting in violations of rights and systematic exclusion from monetization opportunities.

records.title: Deep Learning in Search Engines Causes Sexist Bias, Study Finds
records.description: Researchers from the University of Linz found that search engines using deep learning algorithms, such as Google and Bing, produce particularly sexist and discriminatory results. Their study highlights how AI systems trained on biased human data perpetuate harmful gender stereotypes and discrimination through search outputs, causing real-world harm.

records.title: Snapchat Faces Backlash Over AI Juneteenth Filter Requiring Users to Smile to Break Chains
records.description: Snapchat released an AI-powered Juneteenth filter that prompted users to smile to break virtual chains, causing widespread offense for its insensitivity. The filter, which used facial recognition to trigger effects, was quickly removed after public backlash. Snap apologized and launched an internal investigation into the incident.

records.title: China's AI-Driven Mass DNA Collection Enables Unprecedented Surveillance and Rights Violations
records.description: The Chinese government, with assistance from international biotech firms, has used AI-enabled systems to collect and analyze DNA from tens of millions of citizens—often without consent—to build the world’s largest police DNA database. This facilitates mass surveillance, targeting of minorities and dissidents, and widespread human rights violations.

records.title: Santa Cruz Bans Predictive Policing Over Algorithmic Bias and Harm
records.description: Santa Cruz, California, became the first U.S. city to ban predictive policing after evidence showed AI algorithms like PredPol reinforced racial bias and overpoliced minority neighborhoods. The ban follows public backlash and recognition that the technology caused real-world harm and perpetuated systemic discrimination in law enforcement.

records.title: Amnesty International Warns COVID-19 Tracing Apps Violate Human Rights
records.description: Amnesty International found that several AI-powered COVID-19 contact tracing apps, especially those from Bahrain, Kuwait, and Norway, seriously violate human rights by infringing on privacy and data protection. The apps' centralized data storage and real-time tracking enable potential abuse by authorities and hackers.

records.title: John Oliver Highlights Harms of Facial Recognition AI Used by Law Enforcement and Private Firms
records.description: John Oliver's 'Last Week Tonight' exposed the dangers of facial recognition AI, focusing on Clearview AI's unauthorized data scraping and law enforcement's use of the technology. The show highlighted real harms, including wrongful arrests, privacy violations, and disproportionate impacts on marginalized groups, prompting calls for urgent regulation.

records.title: Russian Schools Deploy AI Facial Recognition Surveillance System
records.description: Russian authorities are installing AI-powered facial recognition cameras in over 43,000 schools, managed by the National Center of Informatization and integrated with the "Orwell" system. While intended to enhance security, the widespread surveillance raises significant concerns about student privacy and potential human rights violations.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot Prevents Collision with Wild Boar in Belgium
records.description: A Belgian baker narrowly avoided a collision with a wild boar when his Tesla's Autopilot system intervened, taking control to steer the car away from the animal. The incident, captured on the vehicle's cameras, went viral online and drew praise from Tesla CEO Elon Musk for the AI system's safety capabilities.

records.title: PimEyes Facial Recognition Tool Raises Global Privacy Concerns
records.description: PimEyes, a Polish AI-powered facial recognition search engine, enables users to find and track individuals online using just a photo. The service has sparked widespread criticism from privacy experts, who warn it facilitates privacy violations, stalking, and unauthorized surveillance by allowing identification and monitoring without consent.

records.title: Microsoft's AI Editor Causes Racial Misidentification in Little Mix Article
records.description: Microsoft's AI-powered news editor on MSN mistakenly used an image of Leigh-Anne Pinnock to illustrate an article about Jade Thirlwall's experiences with racism, causing public offense and highlighting issues of racial misidentification. The error, following the replacement of human editors with AI, drew criticism for perpetuating racial insensitivity and bias.

records.title: Dubai Deploys AI Platform to Monitor COVID-19 Safety Compliance
records.description: Dubai Silicon Oasis and AI firm Derq partnered to deploy an AI-powered platform that analyzes public camera footage to monitor and enforce compliance with COVID-19 safety measures, such as mask-wearing and social distancing, aiming to reduce virus spread and protect public health. No harm or malfunction from the AI system was reported.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot Involved in Both Crash and Harm Avoidance Incidents
records.description: Tesla's Autopilot AI system was involved in two notable incidents: it failed to detect an overturned truck, resulting in a crash, and in a separate case, successfully swerved to avoid a pig at night, preventing harm. These events highlight both the limitations and capabilities of Tesla's AI-driven safety features.

records.title: AI-Enabled Armed Drones Used in Fatal Border Operation Against PKK Militants
records.description: Turkish armed forces, supported by AI-enabled armed drones (SİHA), conducted a military operation on the Iran border, resulting in the neutralization of four PKK militants. The drones provided aerial surveillance and fire support, directly contributing to the operation's lethal outcome.

records.title: Israel Halts AI-Enabled Phone Surveillance of COVID-19 Patients Amid Privacy Concerns
records.description: Israel's Shin Bet used AI-driven phone tracking to monitor COVID-19 carriers, sparking criticism over privacy violations. Following opposition from human rights groups and Shin Bet's chief, the government froze legislation to extend the program, suspending its use and highlighting the risks of AI surveillance to civil liberties.

records.title: Predator Drone Surveillance of Minneapolis Protesters Sparks Rights Concerns
records.description: House Democrats, including Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, are investigating the Trump administration's use of a Predator B drone to surveil Minneapolis protesters after George Floyd's killing. The drone's deployment, possibly involving AI-powered facial recognition, raised concerns about unlawful surveillance, privacy violations, and abuse of authority.

records.title: LGBTQ Creators Sue YouTube Over Alleged Algorithmic Discrimination
records.description: A group of LGBTQ YouTube creators filed a lawsuit against Google, alleging that YouTube's AI-driven recommendation and monetization algorithms unfairly suppress, demonetize, and stigmatize their content, causing financial harm. Google denies discrimination, and the case is being contested in a California court.

records.title: TikTok Apologizes for AI-Driven Suppression of Black Lives Matter Content
records.description: TikTok's AI-driven content display system malfunctioned, making posts with #BlackLivesMatter and #GeorgeFloyd appear to have zero views, leading users to believe their content was being censored. The incident caused harm by suppressing black creators' voices and eroding trust, prompting TikTok to apologize and pledge corrective measures.

records.title: Instagram's AI Anti-Spam System Wrongly Blocks Black Lives Matter Posts
records.description: Instagram's automated anti-spam system mistakenly blocked users from posting or sharing content with the #blacklivesmatter hashtag during a surge in related activity. The AI system, designed to detect spam, incorrectly flagged legitimate posts, restricting communication about the movement and prompting Instagram to address the malfunction.

records.title: Clearview AI's Facial Recognition Sparks Privacy Lawsuits and Protest Surveillance Concerns
records.description: Clearview AI's facial recognition system, used by law enforcement to identify protesters and individuals from social media images, has led to lawsuits from Vermont and the ACLU alleging mass privacy violations and unauthorized biometric data collection, raising concerns over civil rights and the misuse of AI surveillance technologies.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot Fails to Detect Overturned Truck, Causes Highway Crash in Taiwan
records.description: A Tesla Model 3 operating on Autopilot in Taiwan failed to detect an overturned truck blocking the highway, resulting in a high-speed collision. The AI system did not recognize the stationary obstacle or respond in time, causing significant property damage but no injuries. The incident highlights critical limitations in Tesla's autonomous driving technology.

records.title: Microsoft Replaces Dozens of Journalists with AI, Leading to Job Losses
records.description: Microsoft terminated contracts for around 50 journalists, replacing them with AI systems to curate and manage news content on MSN and Edge. The move, aimed at automating news production, resulted in significant job losses and raised concerns about the social impact of AI-driven workforce displacement.

records.title: Police Crackdown Reduces Harmful Bot Activity Spreading Fake News in Brazil
records.description: AI-driven bots linked to pro-Bolsonaro networks were used to spread fake news and threats on social media, manipulating public discourse. Following a Federal Police operation targeting these networks, bot activity on Twitter dropped significantly, highlighting the direct impact of law enforcement on curbing AI-enabled misinformation and harm.

records.title: Pakistan Repurposes AI Surveillance Tech for COVID-19 Tracking, Raising Privacy Concerns
records.description: Pakistan's government, with the help of its intelligence agency ISI, repurposed AI-driven surveillance technologies—originally used for militant tracking—to monitor coronavirus patients and their contacts. This use of geo-fencing and phone monitoring has raised significant privacy and human rights concerns due to the intrusive tracking of citizens.

records.title: YouTube AI Moderation System Censors Comments Critical of Chinese Communist Party
records.description: YouTube's automated moderation system erroneously deleted comments containing Chinese-language phrases critical of the Chinese Communist Party, such as "communist bandit" and "50-cent party." The deletions, which suppressed political speech and violated users' rights to free expression, were attributed to an AI enforcement error that YouTube has since begun to address.

records.title: Facebook Executives Ignored Internal Warnings About AI-Driven Polarization and Extremism
records.description: Internal research at Facebook revealed that its AI-powered recommendation algorithms promoted divisive and extremist content, fueling polarization and hate group growth. Despite clear evidence and proposed solutions, top executives, including CEO Mark Zuckerberg, dismissed or weakened efforts to mitigate these harms, allowing ongoing negative societal impacts.

records.title: AI Systems Fail Amid COVID-19 Mask Usage and Behavioral Shifts
records.description: During the COVID-19 pandemic, AI systems for facial recognition and fraud detection malfunctioned due to widespread mask-wearing and abrupt behavioral changes. Companies in Spain and globally reported increased errors, impacting security, access control, and automated services, highlighting the vulnerability of AI to unexpected real-world changes.

records.title: Permanent Health Code AI System in Hangzhou Raises Privacy and Discrimination Concerns
records.description: Hangzhou's plan to make its AI-driven health code system permanent, integrating personal health and lifestyle data for scoring and community ranking, has sparked widespread criticism. The system has already led to privacy violations and social discrimination, raising serious concerns about human rights and data misuse.

records.title: AI Bots Amplify COVID-19 Misinformation on Twitter
records.description: Researchers from Carnegie Mellon University found that algorithmically controlled Twitter bots were responsible for about 45% of COVID-19-related tweets, spreading false and potentially harmful information. This large-scale AI-driven misinformation campaign poses risks to public health and undermines trust in online information.

records.title: US Tech Giants Enable Blacklisted Chinese AI Surveillance Firms Linked to Human Rights Abuses
records.description: Amazon, Microsoft, and Google have been providing essential web services to Chinese AI surveillance companies blacklisted for human rights violations, including mass surveillance and repression of minorities. These services facilitate the operation of AI-powered technologies used for invasive surveillance, indirectly contributing to ongoing abuses.

records.title: Zuckerberg Admits Facebook's AI Failed to Prevent 2016 Election Disinformation
records.description: Mark Zuckerberg admitted that Facebook was unprepared and late in combating disinformation campaigns during the 2016 US presidential election. The platform's AI-driven moderation systems failed to prevent large-scale misinformation, which compromised the electoral process and drew significant criticism.

records.title: AI-Powered Exam Proctoring Sparks Privacy Backlash in French Universities
records.description: French universities and grandes écoles, including HEC and Rennes 1, deployed AI-based remote proctoring systems for online exams, triggering student protests and concerns over privacy and data protection. The controversy led to exam postponements and highlighted the risks of intrusive AI surveillance in education.

records.title: Clearview AI's Facial Recognition Sparks Global Privacy and Rights Concerns
records.description: Clearview AI, led by Hoan Ton-That, amassed a massive database of billions of photos scraped from social media without consent, selling access to law enforcement and businesses. Police in London, Ontario, and elsewhere used the AI system, raising significant privacy and civil rights concerns and prompting calls for bans and policy reviews.

records.title: Apple's Siri AI Accused of Mass Privacy Violations by Whistleblower
records.description: Whistleblower Thomas Le Bonniec revealed that Apple's Siri AI system recorded and processed users' conversations without consent, violating privacy rights and data protection laws. Despite public outcry and regulatory attention in the EU, Apple allegedly continued these practices, prompting calls for investigation and enforcement against the company.

records.title: Google Nest Hub Bug Exposes Private Video Footage to Unauthorized Users
records.description: A serious bug in Google's AI-powered Nest Hub allowed a user to view private video footage from another person's Nest Cam, resulting in a privacy breach. Google responded by investigating the issue and rewarding the reporting customer, but the incident highlights risks of unauthorized data exposure in smart home AI devices.

records.title: Google AI System Displays Defamatory Label About Cristina Kirchner
records.description: Google's AI-generated knowledge panel erroneously labeled Argentine Vice President Cristina Kirchner as a 'thief,' causing reputational harm and widespread controversy. The label, automatically sourced from web data, remained visible for hours before Google corrected the issue and explained the malfunction of its automated system.

records.title: AI Symptom Checkers Found Inaccurate, Risking Public Health
records.description: Australian research reveals that AI-powered online symptom checkers provide correct diagnoses only about a third of the time and accurate triage advice in less than half of cases. Their frequent inaccuracies risk misleading users, potentially causing unnecessary medical visits or dangerous delays in seeking proper care.

records.title: OnePlus 8 Pro's AI Camera Filter Disabled Over Privacy Concerns
records.description: The OnePlus 8 Pro's AI-enabled color filter camera, capable of seeing through certain materials and fabrics, raised significant privacy concerns. In response, OnePlus temporarily disabled the feature via software updates, acknowledging the risk of privacy violations and committing to address the issue before re-enabling the function.

records.title: Libyan Army Shoots Down Turkish AI Drones in Tripoli Conflict
records.description: The Libyan National Army announced it shot down multiple Turkish Anka-S AI-powered drones, including reconnaissance models, near the strategic Al-Watiya airbase outside Tripoli. The incident highlights the direct involvement of AI-enabled military drones in the ongoing conflict, resulting in property damage and escalating tensions between Libyan and Turkish-backed forces.

records.title: TikTok Accused of Violating Children's Privacy Laws Through AI Data Collection
records.description: A coalition of privacy groups filed complaints with the FTC, alleging TikTok uses AI-driven algorithms to collect and process personal data from children under 13 without parental consent, violating U.S. children's privacy laws. Investigations have also been launched in Colombia and the Netherlands over similar concerns.

records.title: TikTok/Douyin AI Algorithms Used for Censorship and Propaganda, Raising Global Concerns
records.description: TikTok (Douyin) uses AI-driven content moderation and recommendation to censor anti-government content, spread Chinese state propaganda, and promote misinformation. These practices have misled users, violated privacy, and raised national security concerns, with experts and officials warning of the platform's role in information manipulation and potential espionage.

records.title: AI-Powered COVID-19 Surveillance Apps Raise Privacy Concerns in China
records.description: Chinese authorities deployed AI-driven COVID-19 tracking apps that collect personal and location data without user consent, enabling continuous surveillance and health risk assessment. While widely accepted locally, these systems raise significant privacy and human rights concerns due to mandatory use and lack of legal protections.

records.title: Human Rights Watch Warns COVID-19 Tracking Apps Violate Human Rights
records.description: Human Rights Watch criticized the use of AI-powered mobile tracking and geolocation apps by governments during the COVID-19 pandemic, citing risks to privacy and other fundamental rights. The organization highlighted cases in China, Israel, and Russia where such technologies led to arbitrary quarantines, increased repression, and difficult-to-contest decisions.

records.title: Facebook Apologizes for AI Moderation Failures in 2018 Sri Lanka Violence
records.description: Facebook admitted its AI-driven content moderation failed to curb hate speech and disinformation during Sri Lanka's 2018 anti-Muslim riots, contributing to violence that left at least three dead and 20 injured. The company apologized after investigations linked its platform's shortcomings to real-world harm and human rights violations.

records.title: US Senator Calls for Oversight After AI Spyware Pegasus Pitched to Police
records.description: Senator Ron Wyden has demanded aggressive oversight after it was revealed that NSO Group's AI-powered Pegasus spyware, capable of invasive surveillance, was marketed to US police. The spyware's use has led to human rights violations globally, prompting investigations and legal actions in the US, Ghana, and Mexico.

records.title: FarEasTone Uses AI to Block Over 99% of Scam SMS, Preventing Financial Harm
records.description: FarEasTone Telecom deployed AI and big data analytics to intercept over 99% of scam SMS messages, blocking more than 330,000 fraudulent texts and 450 malicious URLs since February. This proactive use of AI has significantly reduced financial fraud and protected users, earning recognition from Taiwan’s Criminal Investigation Bureau.

records.title: Facebook Uses AI to Remove 50 Million COVID-19 Misinformation Posts
records.description: Facebook deployed AI algorithms to identify and remove over 50 million posts containing false or harmful information about COVID-19 on Facebook and Instagram. This large-scale action aimed to mitigate public health risks by curbing the spread of misinformation through automated content filtering systems.

records.title: AI Moderation on Facebook and Twitter Struggles to Contain COVID-19 Misinformation
records.description: Facebook and Twitter deployed AI systems to detect and flag COVID-19 misinformation, labeling millions of posts. However, limitations in AI effectiveness allowed significant amounts of harmful misinformation to persist, indirectly contributing to public health risks by failing to fully contain the spread of false information.

records.title: Ford Recalls 40,000 Vehicles Over Faulty AI Collision Avoidance System
records.description: Ford recalled around 40,000 vehicles, including 2020 Expedition, Lincoln Navigator, and Mustang models, due to malfunctioning Pre-Collision Assist AI systems. The defect prevents the system from detecting or mitigating frontal collisions, increasing the risk of crashes and injuries. No injuries have been reported, but the recall addresses significant safety concerns.

records.title: Clearview AI's Facial Recognition Sparks Global Privacy and Rights Violations
records.description: Clearview AI's facial recognition system, which scraped billions of images without consent, was used by law enforcement and trialled by police in several countries without proper oversight, violating privacy laws and biometric rights. Legal actions and public backlash followed, highlighting significant risks and realized harms to privacy and civil liberties.

records.title: Tech Giants Face Lawsuits Over AI-Driven Biometric Privacy Violations
records.description: Apple and Facebook faced lawsuits for using AI-powered facial and voice recognition features that collected biometric data from Illinois residents without proper consent, violating state privacy laws. Facebook agreed to a $550 million settlement, while Apple faces ongoing legal action over similar alleged privacy breaches.

records.title: WeChat Uses AI to Monitor and Censor International Users' Content for Chinese Censorship System
records.description: Investigations reveal that WeChat employs AI-driven surveillance and censorship on content shared by international users, not just those in China. Data from overseas accounts is analyzed and used to train censorship algorithms, infringing on users' privacy and freedom of expression, and extending Chinese political censorship globally.

records.title: Volvo Recalls Nearly 10,000 Cars in Russia Over Faulty AI Emergency Braking System
records.description: Volvo is recalling nearly 10,000 vehicles in Russia due to a software malfunction in the automatic emergency braking (AEB) system, an AI-driven safety feature. The defect may prevent the system from activating in emergencies, increasing collision risk. Affected vehicles will receive a software update to address the issue.

records.title: Clearview AI Faces Legal Action Over Facial Recognition Use by Private Firms
records.description: Clearview AI's facial recognition system, which scraped billions of images from social media, was used by private companies in violation of Illinois' biometric privacy law. Legal action prompted Clearview to cancel all private and Illinois-based accounts, highlighting the risks of AI-driven privacy breaches and unauthorized biometric data use.

records.title: Utah Suspends AI Policing Contract Over CEO's Extremist Past and Bias Concerns
records.description: Utah suspended its $20 million contract with Banjo, a company providing AI-powered crime detection software, after revelations of the CEO's white supremacist past. The incident raised concerns about potential bias in the AI system, prompting a state audit to investigate algorithmic discrimination and privacy risks in law enforcement use.

records.title: Uncontrolled Drone Incident Disrupts Latvian Airspace and Airport Operations
records.description: A large autonomous drone in Latvia lost control due to a technical failure in its AI-based flight system, resulting in uncontrolled flight for days. The incident led to nationwide airspace restrictions, the closure of Riga Airport, and warnings to neighboring countries, posing significant safety risks to people and aviation.

records.title: AI-Driven Information Warfare Tool Repurposed for US Political Campaigns
records.description: A Democratic-aligned PAC, advised by Gen. Stanley McChrystal, is deploying an AI-powered tool—originally funded by DARPA to counter ISIS propaganda—to map and influence social media discussions about President Trump. The system boosts selected counter-narratives via influencers, raising concerns about AI-enabled manipulation of political discourse and public opinion.

records.title: Xiaomi Accused of AI-Driven User Data Tracking and Privacy Violations
records.description: Security researchers found that Xiaomi smartphones and browsers collect and transmit extensive user data—including browsing history and device identifiers—even in incognito modes, without user consent. The data, processed by AI-enabled systems, is sent to remote servers, raising serious privacy concerns for millions of users. Xiaomi denies wrongdoing.

records.title: Hungarian Police Deploy Facial Recognition for Identity Checks, Raising Rights Concerns
records.description: From May 1, Hungarian police began using AI-powered facial recognition to identify individuals who refuse to show ID, matching photos against government databases. Amnesty International warns this new procedure could violate privacy and fundamental rights due to automated identification without consent.

records.title: Tesla Sued Over Fatal Autopilot Crash Involving Pedestrian in Japan
records.description: The family of Yoshihiro Umeda, killed in 2018 near Tokyo, is suing Tesla, alleging its Autopilot AI system failed to monitor driver alertness and handle unexpected traffic, causing the Model X to accelerate into a group of people. The incident highlights alleged safety flaws in Tesla's AI-driven driving assistance.

records.title: Yandex AI Search Experiment Prioritizes Negative Content About Navalny
records.description: Yandex temporarily used its AI-driven search and recommendation algorithms to prioritize negative materials about opposition figure Alexei Navalny across multiple services. The company called this a 'temporary experiment,' but the manipulation led to biased information exposure, raising concerns about AI-driven content curation and its impact on public perception.

records.title: Instagram Algorithm Manipulated by Coordinated 'Pods' Using AI Detection Tools
records.description: Researchers found that organized groups, or 'pods', systematically coordinate likes and comments to manipulate Instagram's recommendation algorithms, artificially boosting post visibility and distorting information dissemination. Machine learning tools were developed to detect such manipulation, highlighting ongoing harm to community trust and the integrity of online content.

records.title: Google's AI Health Screening Tool Fails in Real-World Clinical Trials
records.description: Google Health's AI tool for detecting diabetic retinopathy, despite high lab accuracy, failed in real-world clinics in Thailand. The system's strict image quality requirements and slow processing led to workflow disruptions, patient and nurse frustration, and delays in care, indirectly harming patient health and reducing effective screening.

records.title: Facebook Removes 'Pseudoscience' Ad Category After AI-Driven Misinformation Targeting
records.description: Facebook's AI-powered ad targeting system enabled advertisers to reach users interested in 'pseudoscience,' facilitating the spread of COVID-19 misinformation and conspiracy theories. After media reports exposed this, Facebook removed the category to prevent further abuse, acknowledging the harm caused by its AI-driven ad platform.

records.title: AI Surveillance in Russia's Lockdown Raises Human Rights Concerns
records.description: Russian authorities used AI-powered facial recognition and digital passes to enforce coronavirus lockdowns, leading to mass surveillance and potential violations of privacy and freedom. Human rights groups called for regulation to ensure these measures are temporary and proportionate, highlighting risks to fundamental rights from unregulated AI surveillance.

records.title: Widespread Use of AI Facial Recognition Leads to Privacy Violations and Legal Action
records.description: Government agencies and private companies in the US have deployed AI-powered facial recognition and license plate readers for mass surveillance, leading to privacy violations and misidentification. Facebook faced a major class action settlement for illegally collecting biometric data, highlighting the real harms and legal risks of AI-driven surveillance technologies.

records.title: AI Voice Robots Enable Large-Scale Scam Calls in China’s '95' Number Segment
records.description: Criminals in China are using AI-powered voice robots bundled with '95' segment phone numbers to automate mass scam and harassment calls. These systems can make thousands of calls daily, screen potential victims, and facilitate financial fraud, causing widespread financial loss and distress despite regulatory crackdowns.

records.title: AI Facial Recognition Used to Prevent Telecom Fraud and Raises Privacy Concerns in China
records.description: Chinese telecom operators, aided by Baidu's AI facial recognition, have implemented real-name verification to combat telecom fraud, directly reducing harm from scams. However, widespread use of facial recognition has led to illegal sales of facial images, raising significant privacy risks and calls for stronger regulation to prevent future harm.

records.title: Hyundai Recalls 2020 Sonata and Nexo Over AI Parking Assist Malfunction
records.description: Hyundai recalled nearly 12,000 2020 Sonata and Nexo vehicles due to a software glitch in the AI-powered Remote Smart Parking Assist system. The malfunction could cause cars to move unintentionally or fail to stop, posing a safety risk. Dealers will reprogram the system to address the issue.

records.title: Fujitsu AI System Reduces Ship Collision Risks in Tokyo Bay Trial
records.description: Fujitsu, in partnership with the Japan Coast Guard, tested its Zinrai AI system in Tokyo Bay from December 2019 to March 2020. The AI accurately predicted vessel collision risks, enabling earlier warnings and improved maritime safety, demonstrating AI's effectiveness in preventing accidents and reducing harm in marine traffic control.

records.title: Israeli AI-Enabled Drone Targets Hezbollah Vehicle on Syria-Lebanon Border
records.description: An Israeli AI-enabled drone targeted a Hezbollah vehicle near the Syria-Lebanon border, launching missiles that destroyed the car but caused no casualties. The incident demonstrates the use of AI systems in military operations, resulting in property damage and posing significant risks to human life.

records.title: Clearview AI's Facial Recognition Use and Data Breach Raise Privacy Concerns in Australia
records.description: Australian Federal Police used Clearview AI's facial recognition system to investigate child exploitation without legal authorization, raising privacy and human rights concerns. Separately, a server misconfiguration at Clearview AI exposed sensitive source code and credentials, highlighting significant risks to the security and responsible management of biometric data.

records.title: Global Concerns Rise Over AI Facial Recognition Surveillance and Regulation
records.description: AI-powered facial recognition systems are being adopted by law enforcement and institutions worldwide, raising significant concerns about privacy, human rights, and potential misuse. While some regions, like Washington State, are introducing regulations, critics argue these measures are insufficient, highlighting the urgent need for robust oversight to prevent harm.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot Fails to Prevent Collision in California Accident
records.description: A Tesla Model 3 operating on autopilot was involved in a collision with a pickup truck in California during rainy conditions. Despite the AI system braking, the vehicle failed to avoid the crash. No injuries occurred, but the incident highlights limitations of Tesla's autopilot AI in real-world scenarios.

records.title: Tencent Disables QQ Group Recommendations After AI System Exposes Minors to Harmful Content
records.description: Tencent's QQ platform used AI-driven group recommendation algorithms that matched educational keyword searches with inappropriate groups, exposing minors to scams and harmful content. Following media reports and public concern, Tencent disabled these recommendation features and pledged to strengthen protections for minors online.

records.title: AI Imaging Systems Aid COVID-19 Diagnosis and Harm Reduction in China
records.description: Chinese tech firms, notably Shukun Technology and Tsinghua University, rapidly developed and deployed AI-powered imaging and diagnostic systems during the COVID-19 pandemic. These systems enabled fast, accurate CT analysis, supported doctors in screening and treatment, reduced cross-infection risks, and improved patient outcomes in hospitals across China and abroad.

records.title: Libyan Army Downs Turkish AI-Powered Drones Targeting Military and Civilian Sites
records.description: The Libyan National Army announced the downing of two Turkish-made AI-powered drones over Tarhuna and Al-Aziziyah. The drones, used in attacks on military positions and reportedly targeting civilian and medical supply sites, highlight the direct harm caused by AI systems in the ongoing Libyan conflict.

records.title: Facial Recognition AI Used to Enforce Quarantine and Monitor Public Health During COVID-19
records.description: Facial recognition AI systems were deployed in Russia's Sakhalin to identify quarantine violators, raising privacy and rights concerns, and in Japan to detect fevers in public spaces to prevent COVID-19 spread. These uses directly impacted individual rights and public health, illustrating both harm prevention and potential rights violations.

records.title: Clearview AI's Facial Recognition System Linked to Far-Right Extremists and Human Rights Violations
records.description: Clearview AI, a facial recognition company used by law enforcement and commercial clients, has been found to have extensive ties to far-right extremists. Its technology, developed and used with input from individuals linked to racist and authoritarian movements, has led to privacy violations and human rights concerns, particularly through unauthorized data scraping and surveillance.

records.title: Google Sued for Unlawful Biometric Data Collection from Schoolchildren via AI Tools
records.description: Google faces a class-action lawsuit alleging it collected facial scans and voiceprints from millions of children using its AI-powered educational tools without parental consent, violating Illinois' Biometric Information Privacy Act and federal COPPA. The suit claims this unauthorized biometric data collection constitutes unlawful monitoring and profiling of minors.

records.title: AI Bots Drive Majority of Pro-Bolsonaro Tweets, Study Finds
records.description: A study by UFRJ and FespSP found that AI-driven bots and automated accounts were responsible for 55% of 1.2 million pro-Bolsonaro tweets using #BolsonaroDay. The coordinated bot activity manipulated political discourse on Twitter, raising concerns about AI's role in influencing public opinion and undermining democratic processes.

records.title: AI Moderation Shortfalls During Lockdown Linked to Rise in Online Child Abuse
records.description: During the COVID-19 lockdown, social networks like Facebook and Twitter increased reliance on AI for content moderation due to reduced human oversight. This shift led to less effective detection of child exploitation and grooming, contributing to a significant rise in online child abuse, as reported by the NSPCC and UK law enforcement.

records.title: Trump Campaign Uses AI-Generated Audio to Falsely Attribute 'Hoax' Comment to Biden
records.description: The Trump campaign released a manipulated audio clip, likely created with AI tools, falsely making it appear Joe Biden called the coronavirus a "hoax." This synthetic media was used to retaliate against similar accusations and highlights the use of AI in spreading political misinformation, risking public harm and undermining democratic discourse.

records.title: Massive Sale of Masked Face Photos for AI Training Sparks Privacy Fears in China
records.description: Vast numbers of masked face photos, sourced from social media, workplace check-ins, and public surveillance, are being illegally collected and sold online in China for AI facial recognition training. This unauthorized trade raises significant privacy and security concerns, as individuals' biometric data is exploited without consent, violating personal rights.

records.title: Stanford Study Finds Racial Bias in Major Voice Recognition AI Systems
records.description: A Stanford University study found that voice recognition AI systems from Apple, Google, Amazon, IBM, and Microsoft have significant racial bias, with much higher error rates for African American users compared to white users. This bias leads to discriminatory outcomes and unequal access to technology.

records.title: AI-Powered Facial Recognition Used for Quarantine Enforcement in Moscow
records.description: Moscow authorities deployed a vast AI-driven facial recognition camera network to monitor and enforce COVID-19 quarantine compliance, identifying and penalizing hundreds of violators. The system, installed despite legal and public protests, raised significant concerns over privacy violations and government overreach, highlighting the societal risks of AI surveillance.

records.title: AI-Powered Fever Detection and Contact Tracing Deployed for COVID-19 Control in Hong Kong
records.description: Hong Kong research teams and startups deployed AI-based fever detection and contact tracing systems at border checkpoints and public venues to identify and isolate potential COVID-19 cases. These systems use computer vision, deep learning, and offline data comparison to enhance public health safety and reduce virus transmission risks.

records.title: Facial Recognition AI in Moscow Courts Leads to Detention of Supporters at Hearings
records.description: Moscow courts covertly deployed facial recognition AI, resulting in the detention of six individuals who attended hearings to support defendants in protest-related cases. The system identified people wanted by police, raising concerns about privacy and human rights violations due to AI-driven surveillance in judicial settings.

records.title: AI Tool Guides Life-or-Death Covid-19 Treatment Decisions in China
records.description: Chinese researchers developed an AI system to analyze Covid-19 patient data and predict survival rates, directly influencing doctors' decisions on treatment prioritization. The tool's use in allocating scarce medical resources raises ethical concerns about AI involvement in life-or-death decisions and potential risks of depriving some patients of care.

records.title: Volvo Recalls Over 700,000 Vehicles Due to AI-Driven Emergency Braking System Malfunction
records.description: Volvo recalled over 700,000 vehicles globally from model years 2019-2020 after discovering a software defect in the AI-powered automatic emergency braking system, which may fail to detect obstacles or pedestrians, increasing crash risk. No injuries have been reported, and a software update is being provided to fix the issue.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot Design Flaws and Regulatory Gaps Blamed in Fatal 2019 Crash
records.description: A fatal 2019 crash in Florida involving a Tesla on Autopilot was attributed to the AI system's design flaws, which allowed driver inattention and activation in inappropriate conditions. The NTSB and IIHS criticized Tesla, drivers, and lax regulations, urging stricter oversight and improved safety measures for autonomous vehicle systems.

records.title: AI-Powered Surveillance in East Asia Raises Privacy and Human Rights Concerns During COVID-19 Response
records.description: China, Taiwan, and South Korea used AI-driven facial recognition, big data analytics, and mobile tracking to identify and control COVID-19 cases, achieving significant virus suppression. However, these measures led to pervasive surveillance, strict enforcement, and raised serious concerns about privacy violations and human rights infringements due to lack of oversight and protections.

records.title: AI Moderation During COVID-19 Pandemic Leads to Erroneous Content Removal and Censorship
records.description: During the COVID-19 pandemic, social media platforms like Facebook and YouTube relied heavily on AI for content moderation due to staff shortages. This led to widespread erroneous removal of legitimate posts, including COVID-19 news, restricting access to information and violating users' rights to free expression and information.

records.title: TikTok's AI Moderation Suppresses Content from Marginalized Groups
records.description: Leaked documents reveal TikTok used AI-driven moderation to suppress or remove videos featuring people deemed 'ugly,' poor, or disabled, and those in deteriorated environments, to attract new users. This algorithmic discrimination led to real harm by limiting visibility and violating rights of affected users.

records.title: China's First AI-Generated Article Copyright Infringement Case Decided
records.description: Tencent sued Net Loan Home for unauthorized reposting of a news article generated by its AI system, Dreamwriter. A Shenzhen court ruled the AI-generated article is protected by copyright, found infringement, and ordered compensation. This landmark case affirms legal protection for AI-generated works in China.

records.title: Clearview AI's Facial Recognition Sparks Legal, Privacy, and Security Incidents
records.description: Clearview AI's facial recognition system, which scraped billions of images from the web for law enforcement use, led to privacy violations, lawsuits (notably in Vermont), and a major data breach exposing client information. Its use by police resulted in criminal charges and raised significant legal and ethical concerns over data collection and rights.

records.title: India's Faulty Facial Recognition System Misidentifies Delhi Rioters
records.description: Indian law enforcement used low-accuracy facial recognition software to identify over 1,900 alleged rioters in Delhi, relying on government ID databases. The system's inability to distinguish genders and its rushed, unregulated deployment have raised concerns about misidentification, privacy violations, and potential harm to innocent individuals.

records.title: Chess Board Startup Uses AI-Generated Fake Engineers and Product Demo to Defraud Backers
records.description: Spanish startup REGIUM used GAN-based AI to create fake engineer profiles and fabricated a product demo video for an automated chessboard, deceiving investors and the chess community. The fraudulent campaign raised over $33,000 on Kickstarter before being exposed and suspended, causing financial and reputational harm.

records.title: Uber Resumes Self-Driving Car Testing in San Francisco After Fatal Crash
records.description: Uber has resumed testing its self-driving cars in San Francisco, two years after a fatal accident in Arizona. The new tests involve two Volvo XC90s operating only during daylight with two safety drivers and no passengers, reflecting increased safety measures but ongoing potential risk from autonomous vehicle AI systems.

records.title: Chinese Facial Recognition AI Identifies Masked Individuals, Raising Human Rights Concerns
records.description: Chinese firm Hanvon developed AI facial recognition technology capable of identifying masked individuals with 95% accuracy, even in crowds. Deployed by authorities for surveillance, including during COVID-19, the system raises significant concerns about privacy violations and human rights abuses, particularly in the context of state monitoring and targeting of minorities.

records.title: Tesla Faces Regulatory Action and Consumer Backlash Over AI Hardware Downgrade in China
records.description: Tesla sold Model 3 vehicles in China with downgraded autonomous driving hardware (HW2.5 instead of HW3.0), misleading customers who paid for advanced AI features. The issue led to regulatory intervention, consumer lawsuits, and Tesla offering free hardware upgrades, but without compensation, raising concerns over AI system transparency and consumer rights.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot Prevents and Fails to Prevent Collisions: Contrasting Incidents
records.description: Tesla's Autopilot AI system was credited with preventing a head-on collision in North Carolina by autonomously swerving to avoid a wrong-way driver, averting potential harm. In contrast, a 2018 fatal crash in Mountain View was attributed to Autopilot's failure to detect a barrier and brake, directly leading to the driver's death.

records.title: Clearview AI Misused for Private Surveillance and Privacy Violations
records.description: Clearview AI's facial recognition software, intended for law enforcement, was misused by private individuals and investors for personal purposes, including identifying people at parties, dates, and in stores without consent. This unauthorized use led to significant privacy violations and breaches of fundamental rights, raising serious concerns about misuse and potential harm.

records.title: AI-Powered Police Body Cameras and Robot Vacuums Raise Privacy Concerns
records.description: Police departments are deploying body cameras with real-time AI facial recognition, enabling instant identification and database searches without public consent, raising privacy and rights concerns. Separately, a robot vacuum with AI-driven video surveillance was found to have faulty encryption, exposing users' video feeds and compromising their privacy.

records.title: Researchers Demonstrate AI Vulnerability in Autonomous Vehicle Perception Systems
records.description: Researchers from the University of Michigan showed that AI-based perception systems in autonomous vehicles can be tricked by spoofed LiDAR signals, causing cars to detect nonexistent obstacles. This manipulation can lead to sudden braking or freezing, posing risks to traffic safety and potentially causing accidents or disruptions.

records.title: Google Wins $179 Million in Self-Driving AI Trade Secrets Case Against Ex-Uber Executive
records.description: Anthony Levandowski, former head of Uber's self-driving unit, was ordered to pay Google $179 million for stealing trade secrets related to AI-based autonomous vehicle technology from Waymo. The misappropriated information was used to found a startup later acquired by Uber, resulting in significant legal and financial consequences.

records.title: Banjo AI System Enables Mass Surveillance in Utah, Raising Privacy Concerns
records.description: Utah has granted Banjo, a private company, real-time access to extensive surveillance infrastructure, including traffic cameras, 911 systems, and social media data. Banjo’s AI system autonomously analyzes this data to detect and alert law enforcement to potential crimes, sparking significant concerns over privacy violations and lack of oversight.

records.title: Innocent Man Wrongly Targeted by AI-Driven Geofence Warrant
records.description: Florida police used Google's AI-powered geofence warrant system to collect location data, wrongly identifying Zachary McCoy as a burglary suspect because his bike route passed the crime scene. The AI system's data sharing led to legal and emotional harm for the innocent man, highlighting risks of AI-driven surveillance.

records.title: AI-Powered Kamikaze Drones Deployed in Turkish Military Operations
records.description: STM-developed AI-enabled kamikaze drones, including the Kargu model, have been delivered to and actively used by the Turkish Armed Forces in counter-terrorism operations. These autonomous drones, capable of targeting and neutralizing threats with explosives, represent a realized deployment of lethal AI systems in military conflict.

records.title: Senators Probe Google and Ascension Over Project Nightingale's AI-Driven Health Data Practices
records.description: U.S. senators are investigating Google and Ascension's 'Project Nightingale,' which uses AI to collect and analyze millions of patients' health records without patient consent. Lawmakers cite incomplete disclosures, privacy concerns, and possible HIPAA violations, raising alarms about transparency and the protection of sensitive health data.

records.title: Facebook's AI Algorithms Cause Emotional Distress by Resurfacing Painful Memories of Ex-Partners
records.description: A study led by Anthony Pinter at the University of Colorado Boulder found that Facebook's AI-driven recommendation and memory algorithms repeatedly surface painful reminders of ex-partners, even after users block or mute them. This algorithmic insensitivity has caused emotional distress, highlighting the harm AI systems can inflict by failing to understand human relationships.

records.title: Google's AI Health Data Practices Spark Privacy Backlash and Lawsuit
records.description: Google partnered with hospitals and universities to collect patient health data for developing AI health prediction algorithms. Privacy activists and a lawsuit allege that the data, though claimed to be anonymized, could be re-identified, violating privacy laws and patients' rights. The incident has led to legal and public scrutiny.

records.title: ICE Sued for Manipulating AI Risk Assessment to Unlawfully Detain Immigrants
records.description: A lawsuit alleges that ICE deliberately altered its Risk Classification Assessment AI system to eliminate release recommendations, resulting in nearly all detained immigrants being held without individualized review. This manipulation led to widespread unlawful detention, violating due process and federal immigration law, and causing significant harm to detainees.

records.title: AI-Enabled Turkish Drones Cause Mass Casualties in Syrian Conflict
records.description: Turkish Armed Forces used AI-enabled armed drones (SİHA), produced by Baykar, to destroy over 600 targets and neutralize thousands of enemy soldiers in Syria following attacks on Turkish troops. The incident highlights the direct and large-scale harm caused by autonomous AI systems in modern warfare.

records.title: Ultrasonic 'Surfing Attacks' Exploit AI Voice Assistants for Unauthorized Access
records.description: Researchers from Washington University in St. Louis demonstrated that ultrasonic waves can activate AI voice assistants like Siri and Google Assistant on smartphones, enabling attackers to make calls, take photos, or read texts without the owner's knowledge. This vulnerability allows privacy breaches and unauthorized access using inexpensive hardware.

records.title: AI Systems Cause Job Losses and Data Breaches, Raise Privacy Concerns
records.description: Amazon's AI system autonomously fired over 900 warehouse workers for low productivity, highlighting job loss risks from workplace automation. Separately, facial recognition firm Clearview AI suffered a major data breach, exposing sensitive client information and sparking privacy lawsuits and investigations. These incidents underscore the harms and risks associated with AI deployment in employment and data management.

records.title: Clearview AI's Facial Recognition App Sparks Privacy Violations and Regulatory Action
records.description: Clearview AI's facial recognition app, which scrapes billions of images from the web without consent, has been used by law enforcement and private entities, leading to significant privacy violations. Apple banned the app for policy violations, and leaked customer data further highlighted the risks of unauthorized surveillance and misuse.

records.title: ICE Uses AI Facial Recognition for Warrantless Searches on Maryland Immigrant Drivers' Licenses
records.description: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) used AI-powered facial recognition to conduct warrantless searches on millions of Maryland driver's license photos, including those of undocumented immigrants. This practice violated privacy and trust, leading to arrests and fear among immigrant communities, and sparked legislative efforts to restrict such AI use.

records.title: Amazon Alexa Recordings Expose Cheating, Raise Privacy Concerns
records.description: A woman discovered her husband's infidelity after Amazon Alexa devices secretly recorded his intimate encounters with another woman. The AI system's routine voice data storage led to a significant privacy breach and emotional harm, highlighting risks associated with smart assistants' data retention and user privacy.

records.title: Babylon Health AI Chatbot Faces Criticism Over Unsafe Medical Advice and Data Privacy Breach
records.description: Babylon Health's AI triage chatbot has been criticized by Dr. David Watkins for providing unsafe medical advice, potentially endangering patient health. In response, Babylon publicly attacked Watkins and posted his data online, raising additional concerns about privacy and the company's handling of safety issues.

records.title: US Regulators Suspend EasyMile Autonomous Shuttles After Passenger Injury
records.description: The US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration suspended EasyMile's autonomous shuttle passenger operations in 16 cities after an unexplained emergency braking incident in Columbus, Ohio injured a passenger. The AI-driven shuttles' malfunction prompted a nationwide halt while regulators investigate safety concerns related to the vehicles' technology and operations.

records.title: Clearview AI Suffers Data Breach Exposing Law Enforcement Client List
records.description: Clearview AI, known for its facial recognition system with a database of over 3 billion photos, suffered a data breach exposing its entire client list, including law enforcement agencies, and usage details. The incident raised significant privacy concerns and prompted criticism from lawmakers and investigations by privacy authorities.

records.title: AI-Powered Wearable Patch Predicts and Prevents Heart Failure Readmissions
records.description: Researchers from the University of Utah and VA Salt Lake City developed an AI-powered wearable patch that monitors heart failure patients' physiological data to predict worsening conditions. The system enables early intervention, potentially preventing up to one-third of hospital readmissions and improving patient outcomes by detecting crises days in advance.

records.title: TikTok's AI Algorithm Accused of Racial Bias and Privacy Violations
records.description: TikTok's AI-driven recommendation algorithm has been found to create filter bubbles based on users' race and appearance, reinforcing social biases and limiting exposure to diverse content. Additionally, experts warn of privacy violations, illegal data collection, and censorship linked to TikTok's Chinese ownership, raising concerns about surveillance and human rights.

records.title: Smart Speakers' AI Malfunction Leads to Frequent Accidental Eavesdropping and Privacy Violations
records.description: A Northeastern University study found that AI-powered smart speakers like Alexa, Siri, and Google Assistant are accidentally activated up to 19 times daily, often by mishearing words from conversations or TV. This malfunction results in unintended recordings, raising significant privacy concerns and potential security risks for users.

records.title: AI Bots Amplify Political and Climate Disinformation on Twitter
records.description: Automated AI-driven bots were used in Mexico to manipulate political discourse in favor of Enrique Peña Nieto and in the US to spread climate change denial, especially after Trump’s Paris Agreement withdrawal. Studies found bots generated up to 38% of climate-related tweets, distorting public opinion and spreading misinformation.

records.title: Boeing 737 Max MCAS AI System Linked to Fatal Crashes and Regulatory Misconduct
records.description: Boeing's automated MCAS flight control system, classified as AI, was central to two fatal 737 Max crashes. Investigations allege Boeing employees, including the chief technical pilot, misled regulators about MCAS's safety, leading to administrative suspensions and a federal criminal probe into the company's conduct.

records.title: Moscow Uses AI Facial Recognition to Enforce Coronavirus Quarantine
records.description: Moscow authorities deployed AI-powered facial recognition to monitor and enforce coronavirus quarantine compliance for around 2,500 returnees from China. The system tracked individuals' movements, leading to involuntary surveillance and enforcement actions, raising concerns over privacy violations and human rights infringements due to AI-driven public health surveillance.

records.title: Malaysian Courts Use AI in Sentencing, Raising Constitutional Concerns
records.description: Sabah courts in Malaysia used AI to recommend sentences in drug-related cases, marking the judiciary's first such use. The AI analyzed case details to suggest punishments, which judges considered in their decisions. Lawyers objected, citing potential violations of constitutional rights to liberty and equality before the law.

records.title: US Homeland Security Algorithm Bars Human Rights Investigator from Entry
records.description: Eyal Weizman, director of Forensic Architecture, was barred from entering the US after a Department of Homeland Security algorithm flagged him as a security risk. The AI-driven decision, lacking transparency and due process, disrupted his professional activities and raised concerns about algorithmic bias and human rights violations.

records.title: Researchers Trick Tesla's AI into Dangerous Speeding with Simple Tape Hack
records.description: McAfee researchers demonstrated that placing a small piece of tape on a speed limit sign caused Tesla vehicles using the MobilEye EyeQ3 AI system to misread '35' as '85', triggering the cars to accelerate by 50mph. This adversarial attack exposes critical vulnerabilities in Tesla's AI-based traffic sign recognition, posing significant safety risks.

records.title: Yemeni Army Downs Houthi AI-Enabled Drone in Al-Jawf
records.description: Yemeni government forces shot down a Houthi-operated drone attempting to target military positions in Al-Jawf province. The incident highlights the ongoing use of AI-enabled or autonomous drones in the Yemen conflict, posing direct threats to military personnel and contributing to the escalation of hostilities.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot Prevents Fatalities During Storm Dennis by Emergency Braking
records.description: During Storm Dennis in the UK, Tesla's Autopilot AI system activated emergency braking in two Model X vehicles, preventing a 400-year-old tree from crushing eight occupants. The AI's timely intervention avoided serious injury or death, demonstrating the system's direct role in safeguarding passengers during a hazardous event.

records.title: Twitter Bots Amplify Climate Change Denial, Study Finds
records.description: A Brown University study found that about 25% of climate change-related tweets during the period around the US withdrawal from the Paris Agreement were generated by AI-powered Twitter bots. These bots predominantly spread climate science denial and misinformation, significantly distorting public discourse and amplifying denialist messages online.

records.title: AI-Generated Deepfake Videos Used in Indian Election Campaigns to Mislead Voters
records.description: During the Delhi elections, AI-powered deepfake technology was used to create and widely circulate fabricated videos of BJP leader Manoj Tiwari speaking in multiple languages, falsely criticizing opponents. These deepfakes, produced by a political communications firm, misled voters and undermined trust in the electoral process, raising concerns about AI-driven misinformation in politics.

records.title: Police and Stadium Use of Facial Recognition AI Raises Privacy Concerns in France and Europe
records.description: Police forces in France and across Europe are increasingly using AI-powered facial recognition systems for surveillance and security, raising significant concerns about privacy violations and potential breaches of fundamental rights. Recent deployments include police investigations and experimental use in stadiums, often without adequate public consent or regulatory oversight.

records.title: French Tax Authorities Use AI to Recover Hundreds of Millions in Tax Fraud Crackdown
records.description: French tax authorities deployed AI-driven data mining and machine learning algorithms to detect and combat tax fraud, leading to the recovery of approximately €785 million in 2019. The AI systems enabled more targeted audits, increased detection of fraudulent cases, and raised concerns about privacy and data use in enforcement actions.

records.title: Facial Recognition AI Used by Indian Police Sparks Rights Concerns During Protests
records.description: Indian police deployed AI-powered facial recognition during protests against a new citizenship law, leading to detentions and raising fears of mass surveillance, privacy violations, and suppression of dissent. Activists and protestors report a chilling effect on freedom of expression, citing insufficient regulation and lack of transparency around the technology's use.

records.title: Facial Recognition AI Sparks Global Privacy and Rights Violations Debate
records.description: Law enforcement agencies worldwide, including in Sacramento and Australia, have used AI-powered facial recognition systems like Clearview AI, leading to privacy violations, unauthorized data scraping, and wrongful identifications. These practices have triggered legal challenges, moratoriums, and widespread concerns over fundamental rights and discriminatory impacts, especially for marginalized communities.

records.title: Alipay Facial Recognition System Exploited by Fraudsters Using AI-Generated 3D Avatars
records.description: In 2018, fraudsters exploited Alipay's AI-powered facial recognition by using software-generated 3D avatars and stolen personal data to create fake accounts and claim rewards. Alipay detected the anomaly, alerted authorities, and upgraded security. No user financial losses occurred, but the incident highlighted vulnerabilities in biometric AI systems.

records.title: AI Welfare Fraud Detection Systems Wrongly Punish the Poor
records.description: AI algorithms used by US states to detect welfare fraud have wrongly accused thousands of poor individuals, leading to severe financial and social harm, including evictions and suicides. High error rates and lack of oversight in these automated systems have resulted in widespread unjust penalties against vulnerable populations.

records.title: Indian Police Use AI Facial Recognition to Reunite Missing Children
records.description: Indian police in Telangana used a facial recognition AI app as part of Operation Smile to identify and reunite thousands of missing and trafficked children with their families, significantly mitigating harm from child trafficking and disappearance. The initiative is praised as a major advance in addressing these issues.

records.title: California Police Misuse AI License Plate Readers, Violating Privacy Laws
records.description: A state audit found that California law enforcement agencies, including LAPD, Fresno PD, and others, misused AI-powered automated license plate readers (ALPRs) by violating privacy laws, excessively retaining and broadly sharing personal data, and lacking proper oversight, resulting in direct harm to individuals' privacy and civil liberties.

records.title: Biometric AI Systems Cause Loss of Benefits and Privacy Breaches
records.description: Biometric identification systems using AI have led to significant harms, including individuals losing access to public benefits due to mismatches, fraud through replicated biometric data, and large-scale data breaches exposing sensitive information. These incidents highlight the risks and vulnerabilities of deploying AI-driven biometric verification in both government and private sectors.

records.title: Police Use of Clearview AI Facial Recognition Sparks Privacy Lawsuits and Rights Concerns
records.description: Toronto police admitted to using Clearview AI's facial recognition tool, which scrapes billions of images without consent, raising privacy and legal concerns. A lawsuit alleges Clearview and its partner CDW violated Illinois biometric privacy laws by collecting and storing residents' biometric data without notice or consent, highlighting risks of AI-driven surveillance.

records.title: China's AI-Powered Social Credit System Restricts Millions' Rights
records.description: China's Social Credit System uses AI, facial recognition, and algorithmic scoring to monitor and rate citizens' behavior, impacting access to jobs, travel, and social services. Millions have already faced travel bans and other penalties, raising concerns over human rights violations and large-scale harm caused by AI-driven surveillance and scoring.

records.title: Tesla Autopilot Failures Lead to Fatal Crashes Investigated by NTSB
records.description: Tesla's Autopilot, an AI-driven driver assistance system, malfunctioned in multiple incidents, steering vehicles into barriers and causing fatal crashes in California and Florida. Victims, including Apple engineer Walter Huang, had previously reported the system's defects. The NTSB is investigating these incidents, highlighting the AI system's direct role in the fatalities.

records.title: Apple's AI System Scans iCloud and Email for Child Abuse Images
records.description: Apple uses automated hash-based AI systems to scan iCloud and email content for known child abuse images. When flagged, emails or files are quarantined and reviewed, with confirmed cases reported to authorities. This AI-driven process aims to prevent the distribution of illegal content while raising privacy concerns.

records.title: FAA Probed After Boeing 737 Max Crashes Linked to Automated Flight-Control System
records.description: The U.S. Department of Transportation is investigating FAA pilot training after two fatal Boeing 737 Max crashes, where pilots struggled with the MCAS automated flight-control system. The AI-driven system malfunctioned, repeatedly forcing the planes' noses down, leading to deadly accidents and raising concerns about automation in aviation.

records.title: AI-Powered Skin Cancer Detection Apps Found Unreliable and Poorly Regulated
records.description: Multiple studies led by UK researchers reveal that AI-based smartphone apps for skin cancer detection frequently miss cases or give false positives, potentially delaying treatment or causing unnecessary anxiety. The apps' poor accuracy and inadequate regulation pose health risks, highlighting the need for stricter oversight and improved validation.

records.title: AI Algorithm Identifies High Suicide Risk via Text Analysis
records.description: Crisis Text Line uses an AI algorithm to analyze millions of messages and prioritize individuals at high suicide risk. The system identifies specific words and the pill emoji as strong indicators of imminent danger, enabling faster intervention and potentially preventing harm to those in crisis.

records.title: Google and WeWork Face Lawsuits Over AI-Driven Biometric Privacy Violations
records.description: Google and WeWork are facing class-action lawsuits for allegedly using AI-powered facial recognition systems to collect and store biometric data without users' informed consent, violating Illinois' Biometric Information Privacy Act (BIPA). The lawsuits claim these practices breach legal obligations and privacy rights, highlighting risks of AI misuse in biometric data handling.

records.title: Man Suffers Hypothermia After Following Google Maps Across Frozen River
records.description: A man in Minneapolis fell through the ice on the Mississippi River and suffered mild hypothermia after reportedly following Google Maps directions that he interpreted as instructing him to cross the frozen river. Fire officials believe the app intended for him to use a nearby bridge.

records.title: Facial Recognition Bias in 'Giggle' App Excludes Trans and Nonbinary Users
records.description: The 'Giggle' app uses AI-based facial recognition to verify users' gender for access to its female-only platform. The system, trained primarily on cisgender faces, misgenders or excludes trans and nonbinary individuals, resulting in discriminatory access and harm to these communities.

records.title: AI-Powered CT Diagnostics Aid COVID-19 Detection and Mitigate False Negatives in China
records.description: AI systems, including those from Huawei Cloud and startups like 推想, were rapidly deployed in Chinese hospitals to analyze CT scans for COVID-19. These AI tools improved diagnostic speed and accuracy, helped identify cases missed by nucleic acid tests, and reduced doctors' workload, directly contributing to better patient outcomes during the pandemic.

records.title: AI-Powered Surveillance in China During COVID-19 Leads to Widespread Privacy Violations
records.description: During the COVID-19 pandemic, Chinese authorities deployed AI systems—including facial recognition, thermal imaging, and big data analytics—for mass surveillance, tracking individuals' movements and health status. This led to significant privacy violations and social control, with authorities and employers intervening based on AI-generated data, raising serious human rights concerns.

records.title: Amazon's AI-Driven Choice Badge Misleads Consumers Through Fake Reviews
